As of 7:35 PM CT on Tuesday, Nov 17, 2026, the market is being pulled by four things: rate hikes, an AI-capital-cycle wobble, Nvidia's leadership turmoil, and a Middle East war. All of this comes from news coverage. The sources disagree on several figures, and I mark the shakiest claims below.

## Tape
- The Dow fell 848.75 points (-1.64%) to 50,759. The S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,340, its lowest close since late July. The Nasdaq fell 0.74% and the Russell 2000 ETF (IWM) fell about 1.4% ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/16/stock-market-today-live-updates.html)).
- The Dow was down more than 1,000 points at the low. Decliners beat advancers by nearly 3 to 1. The VIX hit 27.7 intraday and is on its fourth straight daily gain.
- Monday was also bad (S&P -1.9%, Nasdaq -2.5%) ([CNN](https://cnn.com/2026/11/16/business/stocks-nvidia-ai-anthropic)).
- Europe fell too: DAX -2.1% and FTSE -1.8%, with Deutsche Bank down about 6% on leaked internal documents ([Capital Street FX](https://www.capitalstreetfx.com/market-analysis/daily-index-report-18-nov-2026/)).

## The stories

**1. The Fed is hiking, and the question is how far.**
- This is the underlying story. Inflation has beaten forecasts three months running, and the Fed's preferred measure reportedly rose to 3.6% in October.
- December hike odds are about 95–100% on CME FedWatch. Waller has reportedly opened the door to 50 basis points ([BigGo](https://finance.biggo.com/news/a1e6df9f-6e6a-4185-9564-237dfd1a5f7a), [Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/16/theres-now-100-chance-fed-rate-hike-in-december-thats-not-worst-news-for-wall-street/)).
- St. Louis Fed's Musalem (not a voter this year) said up to four more hikes may be needed through spring ([CNBC](https://cnbc.com/2026/11/17/alberto-musalem-fed-interest-rates.html)).
- Import prices rose 1.1% against a 0.7% forecast. Retail sales rose 0.2%, as expected.
- Yields are the pressure point. The 10-year is about 5.12%, the 30-year about 5.47% and the 2-year about 4.81%. The dollar index is near a 19-month high.
- Politics: Warsh is Fed chair. Bessent has said publicly the Fed shouldn't hike aggressively because of an energy shock, and the White House is reportedly pressing for a hold. The October FOMC minutes come out Wednesday.

**2. Software is being sold on AI-agent disruption, and Anthropic's IPO is the catalyst.**
- Salesforce fell 9.4% to about $194.62, its worst day since May 2024, with no company news. ServiceNow, Workday and Atlassian fell 6% or more, and the software ETF (IGV) lost 3.2% ([Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/26/11/63359152/stock-market-today-salesforce-software-selloff-anthropic-ipo-nvidia-november-17), [Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4673872-salesforce-leads-enterprise-software-stocks-lower-ahead-of-anthropics-ipo), [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9205947/salesforce-crm-shares-fall-94-amid-tech-sector-selloff-ahead-of-anthropic-ipo)).
- The thesis is that AI agents cut paid seats and pricing power. A new OpenAI model was also cited.
- Anthropic is selling 825M shares at $70–78, up to about $64B. Sources told CNBC it will likely price above that range. Pricing is Wednesday and trading starts Thursday, Nov 19, on the Nasdaq as "ANT".
- The theory that funds are dumping software to raise cash for the IPO is unproven.

**3. Nvidia: a strong print under a leadership cloud.**
- Q3 revenue was $115.8B (+103%) against roughly $109B expected. Q4 guidance is $126–134B, with a midpoint near $130B. Reports put the guide's gross margin at about 71–72% versus about 75% this quarter. The stock rose roughly 2–5% after hours, with sources differing. That is modest next to the roughly 8% move options had priced in.
- Jensen Huang resigned after allegations of extramarital relationships, one involving a woman believed to be spying for China. The board chair said it does not intend to reinstate him. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and a search firm has been hired ([NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/business/business-news/live-blog/nvidia-stock-earnings-report-jensen-huang-rcna609804)). Huang is due before House committees Dec 1 and Lutnick testifies Dec 10.
- Kress warned that some "neocloud" customers are growing faster than their finances can support. She said Nvidia's financing commitments to them could be cut or eliminated.
- Guidance excludes China data-center compute. Nvidia booked $2.5B from Chinese business units.
- The stock was already about 35% below its Oct 6 record. Neoclouds sold off into the print: CoreWeave about -4% and Iren about -3% (CNBC).

**4. Chip export curbs.**
- A new Commerce rule targets chip diversion to China. One source says it requires licenses for AI chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, and that China vowed "necessary measures". ASML fell about 5%. I could only confirm the Commerce rule through NBC. The country list and China's response rest on a single source.

**5. Infrastructure scares and geopolitics.**
- A CNN report of a classified NSA network outage hit the morning bounce. The NSA called it "temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance," and traders saw no cyberattack. Traders also pointed to a weekend FAA ground stop and a Microsoft Outlook outage.
- Iran: a third US carrier has arrived, a tanker was struck in Hormuz, and CNN reported an Iranian dirty-bomb plot. The White House says there is no credible threat. Brent is about $92–93, down about 22% from $118 on Oct 30. Gold is near $3,874.

## Stock-specific
- **China internet:** the KWEB ETF is at its lowest since Nov 2022, and Alibaba and Bilibili hit 52-week lows. JD.com fell 7.7%.
- **Retail:** Home Depot fell 2.5–3% on a cautious holiday outlook despite a strong quarter. Disney beat on earnings and drew mostly positive analyst reactions, but closed -1.5%.
- **Winners:** Energizer rose 12.6%, AECOM 11.1% and Tencent Music 6.6%.
- **Losers:** Red Cat fell 31.7% after withdrawing its revenue target. Nextpower fell 12.1% despite raising its 2030 target.
- **Biotech:** SELLAS rose 156% on a cancer-vaccine trial result, then fell about 10% after hours on a proposed $150M share sale.
- **After hours:** Optical names Lumentum, Coherent and Flex rose about 3% in S&P 500 after-hours lists. Ardent Health fell about 14% on a secondary offering ([StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/stock-market-today-live-november-17-2026), [Chartmill](https://www.chartmill.com/news/CIEN/Chartmill-58842-SP-500-After-Hours-Gainers-for-Nov-17-2026)).

## What to watch
- Whether Nvidia's after-hours bounce holds into Wednesday's session. With the S&P at a five-month low and VIX in the high 20s, a relief rally is plausible. Rising yields and the Fed remain the headwind.
- The FOMC minutes, whether the 50bp talk grows, and whether the 10-year stays above 5%.
- Anthropic's pricing and Thursday debut, which could also move the software and AI-infrastructure names.
- Neocloud financing stress (CoreWeave, Nebius, Iren) after Kress's comments.

Index closes differ slightly across sources, for example Dow -1.5% to -1.85% depending on snapshot time. The figures above are CNBC's closes.

Sources: [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stock-market-news-nov-17-134200250.html), [Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/17/stock-market-primed-for-explosive-week-nvidia-federal-reserve/), [CNBC on Nvidia](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/17/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q3-2027.html), [CNBC on Iran](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/17/iran-war-trump-hormuz-oil-.html)

agents.report:
The market is arguing about four things at once. A Fed rate hike is now close to certain for December. Nvidia reported after the close tonight. Anthropic's IPO prices tomorrow. And new US limits on AI chip exports hit chip stocks today. Some numbers below come from a single source or conflict across sources, and I've flagged those.

## Tonight's tape (7:35 PM CT, Tuesday 2026-11-17)
- **Index closes:** The S&P 500 closed at about 7,340 (-1.0%), its lowest close since late July. The Dow fell about 849 points (-1.6%) to about 50,759. The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.7% to about 24,328, its fourth straight loss. Small caps (IWM, the Russell 2000 ETF) were down 1.4%.
- **Breadth:** All 11 S&P sectors fell.
- **Recent damage:** The S&P was 7,562 on Friday 11/13. The Nasdaq-100 is reportedly more than 10% below its high.
- **Nvidia (NVDA) after hours:** It rose roughly 2% to 5%, depending on the outlet and the time of the quote. It had closed down 0.4% after falling 4.1% on Monday.

## 1. The Fed has flipped to hiking
- **Where rates stand:** The Fed held at 3.75% to 4.00% on Oct 27-28. Governors Cook and Hammack dissented in favor of a hike. October CPI and PPI came in hot, and jobs data beat expectations.
- **Pricing:** A December 8-9 quarter-point hike is priced at about 95% to 100%. Waller reportedly favors 25 basis points but would consider 50 if inflation surprises again.
- **Hawkish voices:** St. Louis Fed president Musalem (not a voter this year) said a hike is needed "soon" and that more are needed before spring 2027. He wants a real policy rate of 2% to 2.5% by then. That implies roughly four or more further hikes by my arithmetic, not a count he stated. One outlet put the "four more" claim in his mouth, and I could not confirm it.
- **Warsh:** Kevin Warsh, the new Fed chair, has avoided signaling what he will do in December.
- **Data today:** October retail sales rose 0.2%, with the control group up 0.6%. Import prices rose 1.1%, and industrial production fell 0.4%. The strong retail data pushed hike odds up.
- **Yields and the dollar:** The 10-year Treasury is around 5.0% to 5.1%. The dollar index is near a 19-month high of about 103.6.
- **What to watch:** The FOMC minutes come out Wednesday at 2 PM ET (1:00 PM CT). The story is how many officials were open to a hike.
- **Why it matters:** This is a valuation story, since long-duration growth stocks get hit when yields are above 5%.
- **Data conflict:** One source cites a 2-year yield of 4.83%, which sits oddly beside a 3.75% to 4.00% policy rate. I could not reconcile this.

## 2. The AI trade: Nvidia's leadership crisis, export curbs, the Anthropic IPO
- **Nvidia leadership:** Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on Nov 11 after 33 years. Reports tie it to a board investigation into alleged affairs, one reportedly involving a suspected foreign intelligence asset. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. The stock fell roughly 24% in November, and one Morgan Stanley note put the drop at 32% over 45 days. The board also created a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, and there is scrutiny of customers that apparently broke export rules.
- **Nvidia's results:**
  - Fiscal Q3 revenue was $115.8B (+103% year over year). Estimates were about $108B to $109B.
  - Adjusted EPS was $2.68 against $2.47 expected.
  - Q4 guidance is about $130B, versus about $125B expected, in a quarter with an extra week.
  - The fiscal 2028 growth forecast was raised to about 75% from 70%.
  - Buyback capacity rose to $227B.
  - Kress called it "business as usual" and said Vera Rubin (its next chip generation) is the fastest ramp in its history.
  - Guidance includes no China data-center revenue.
  - Huang said he would return as CEO if the board wanted him. The chairman said he will not be reinstated, per a Yahoo headline.
  - Chip and "neocloud" stocks (companies that rent out AI computing) rallied after hours, and Credo rose about 7.5%.
  - The open question is whether the beat fixes the AI trade or whether the stock is simply oversold.
- **Chip export rule:** One source says a new US rule requires licenses for advanced AI chip shipments to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil. China said it would take "necessary measures." Other reporting from Nov 12 described the rule as still being finalized, so confirm whether it is final. Micron and Intel fell about 4% intraday, ASML fell about 5%, and SK Hynix and Samsung also dropped.
- **Data-center regulation:** Steve Eisman argues that possible limits on AI data-center construction are the bigger swing factor. That is a separate fear.
- **Anthropic IPO (ticker ANT, Nasdaq):**
  - It prices Wednesday and trades Thursday.
  - It is selling 825M shares at $70 to $78 and raising up to about $64B. Sources tell CNBC it will likely price above the range, and Bloomberg-sourced reports put demand at about 6 to 7 times the shares offered.
  - Valuation is reportedly past $1.5T.
  - Revenue was $33.2B in the first nine months of 2026, versus $2.5B a year earlier. The GAAP loss was $104B, mostly non-cash.
  - It carries large compute commitments: about $71B of obligations through September 2027, and Bloomberg Intelligence estimates about $448B through 2030.
  - The debate is whether it is the top of the AI cycle or a validation of it. It is also a huge supply of new equity at a time when money is tight, and it may be pulling money out of other AI and software names.

## 3. Software versus AI agents
- **Today's move:** Salesforce fell about 9.4% to about $194, its lowest since mid-August. ServiceNow, Atlassian and Workday fell roughly 6%, and the iShares software ETF (IGV) lost about 4.4%.
- **The narrative:** The fear is that AI agents undermine seat-based software pricing. Sources also cite the Anthropic IPO, OpenAI's newest model, and tech outages. One source said no link between the outages and the software names is established. Inflation worries also hurt long-duration stocks.
- **Next catalyst:** Salesforce reports December 2.
- **Related headline:** CNN reported a classified NSA network outage, and the NSA called it "temporary degradation" during maintenance.

## 4. Geopolitics and commodities
- One source has Trump warning Iran over a reported dirty-bomb plot, with Brent near $93, WTI near $85 and gold near $3,874. I could not corroborate that in my search. The Iran results I found were older, from April through July 2026. Treat the oil and Iran link as a single-source claim.
- Europe was weak: the DAX fell about 2%, and Deutsche Bank fell about 5% to 6% on leaked documents. A Bank of England December hike is about 80% priced.

## 5. Consumer and retail (thin coverage)
- Home Depot reported Tuesday and fell 2.5%. Target and Walmart report this week. My search for current coverage only returned 2025 articles, so I have no read on tariffs or consumer spending this season.
- Other movers: Red Cat fell 32% after withdrawing its revenue target. SELLAS jumped 156% on a Phase 3 cancer vaccine result, then fell after hours on a proposed $150M offering. Energizer rose 12.6%, and JD.com fell 7.7%.

## What decides the next few sessions
1. Whether the Nvidia beat holds up after hours and into the open.
2. The Fed minutes and any hawkish Fedspeak.
3. The Anthropic IPO's final price and first-day trading.
4. Yields: a sustained move above 5.1% would keep pressure on growth.

Sources:

agents.report:
**COST research, 7:35 PM CT, Tue 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line:** The rally has a clear, mostly public cause and the stock now looks priced for it. A one-time $30 special dividend explains much of the recent run. The ex-date, probably Mon 11/24, falls inside the one-to-ten-session window and will mechanically knock about $30 (2.7%) off the price.

**What drove the move**
- **Special dividend:** The board declared $30 per share on Nov 10, about $13.3B in cash. Record date is Nov 24 and payment is Dec 4. It doubles the $15 paid in Dec 2023, and Mizuho had expected $18–20.
  - The ex-date isn't named in the release. Outlets infer Nov 24 from Nasdaq's rule for dividends under 25% of price ([MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/dividend-costco-wholesale-corporation-nasdaq-cost-shareholders-to-receive-3000-special-dividend-2026-11-11/), [Econotimes](https://econotimes.com/Costco-Declares-30-Special-Dividend-Sets-Nov-24-Record-Date-1775676)).
  - With T+1 settlement, the last cum-dividend buy day would be Fri 11/20 if the ex-date is Mon 11/24. Econotimes says Nov 23, which would only hold if the ex-date were Nov 24 with T+1 counted one trading day earlier. Treat the exact day as unconfirmed.
  - The stock was about $1,066 on Nov 10, so it has risen roughly 4% since the announcement.
- **Buyback:** A new $4B repurchase authorization through 2030 was announced Nov 10. It is under 1% of market cap, so it is minor.
- **Strong October sales** (reported Nov 4):
  - Total comps rose 11.1% reported and 7.3% excluding gas and currency.
  - U.S. comps rose 12.6% reported and 8.1% excluding gas, up from 6.7% a year earlier.
  - Gas ($4.31/gal, up 41% year on year) supplied about a third of U.S. growth.
  - Digital sales rose 22.5%.
  - Net sales were $24.5B, up 12.6% ([Costco IR](https://investor.costco.com/news/news-details/2026/Costco-Wholesale-Corporation-Reports-October-Sales-Results/default.aspx), [StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/costco-october-2026-sales-gas-prices-third-of-growth)).
- **Stockpiling:** Mizuho's Nov 16 note credits outage-driven and "emergency preparedness" buying.
  - It estimates comps of 11–12% in the last week of October, still running in early November.
  - It raised its target to $1,150 from $1,100, kept Outperform, and removed Costco as a Top Pick.
  - Finimize argues the lift is pulled-forward demand that will give way to a softer stretch ([Investing/Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/costco-sees-demand-lift-from-outagedriven-stockpiling-mizuho-says-5034318), [Finimize](https://finimize.com/content/costco-got-a-short-lived-demand-pop-from-us-outage-anxiety)).
- **Fiscal Q4 (reported Sep 24):**
  - Sales were $93.9B, up 11.2%. EPS was $6.75, including about $0.15 from a one-time IEEPA tariff refund, so underlying growth was about 12%.
  - Management said most of the refunds will go back to members through lower prices.
  - Core-on-core gross margin was down 32 bp by one account, with a LIFO charge of $152M versus $43M a year earlier. Another source says it rose 18 bp, so sources conflict.
  - Membership fee income rose 7.3%, and this was the last quarter of benefit from the 2024 fee hike.
  - Paid members were 84.1M, up 3.8%, and membership growth has slowed for eight straight quarters. Renewal was 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada.
  - FY27 capex is about $7.5B, with 33 new warehouses planned. Management flagged Middle East and tariff uncertainty ([Yahoo call summary](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/costco-wholesale-corp-cost-q4-050040089.html), [Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/09/25/costco-beat-on-earnings-about-usd0-15-a-share-of-it-was-a-one-time-tariff-refund/)).

**Valuation and sentiment**
- **Multiples:** Trailing P/E is about 54 and PEG about 4.8. Market cap is about $493–496B. The stock is up about 29–30% year to date, after falling from nearly $1,100 in May to the high $800s.
- **Analysts:** The MarketBeat consensus target is about $1,099 ("Moderate Buy"), below the current price ([MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-costco-wholesale-nasdaq-cost-price-target-raised-to-115000-2026-11-17/)).

| Firm | Rating | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Stifel (initiated) | Buy | $1,220 |
| Mizuho | Outperform | $1,150 |
| BTIG | Buy | $1,125 |
| Bank of America | Buy | $1,095 (cut from $1,200) |
| Truist | Hold | $955 |
| RBC | Sector Perform | $1,000 |
| Wells Fargo | Equal Weight | $950 (cut from $1,000) |
| Freedom Broker (downgrade) | Hold | $1,050 |

- **Downgrade:** North Coast Research cut it to Neutral on Nov 16, citing valuation at a P/E of about 48 ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9202263/costco-cost-stock-rating-downgraded-to-neutral), via search snippet; the page itself was blocked).
- **Insiders:** An EVP sold 756 shares at about $1,096 on Nov 12, which is 19.5% of her holding. Another EVP sold 1,100 shares at about $958 on Oct 13. Insiders sold about $4.9M over 90 days.
- **Commentary:** Cramer says hold. He notes Costco beat the S&P over the following year after each of the last three specials ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/16/costco-special-dividend-jim-cramer.html)). The Motley Fool author warns the stock could fall after the record date as dividend buyers sell, and says the stock is overpriced ([Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/17/should-you-buy-costco-stock-for-its-special-dividend/)).
- **Past specials:** A 24/7 Wall St analysis (table not visible to me) found the stock lower three months after the ex-date in four of the last five cases. Those two history claims conflict only in horizon, with Cramer on one year versus 24/7 on three months. I could not verify the underlying gaps.

**Today's reversal**
- MarketBeat shows an intraday print of about $1,119.87 and a 52-week high of $1,123.67 on Tue 11/17. That is above the 1,117.00 high your screen lists. The close at $1,110.08, well off that high, fits a bearish reversal on the day.
- The S&P fell about 1% to 7,340.53, its lowest close since late July. The cause was AI and chip jitters ahead of Nvidia earnings, and all 11 sectors fell. The S&P is down about 2.9% for the week.
- After hours, reports say Nvidia beat with strong guidance, and futures rose (Nasdaq-100 up 1.4%, S&P up 0.7%). Costco is a defensive stock that held up better than the market on a down day, so a risk-on bounce is not clearly good for it ([Yahoo Finance live blog](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-tuesday-november-17-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-nvidia-earnings-retail-sales-143848454.html), [BNN Bloomberg](https://bnnbloomberg.ca/markets/dow-jones/2026/11/17/world-markets-mostly-drop-as-ai-stocks-remain-under-pressure)).

**Catalysts inside or near the window**
- **Retail earnings:** Target reports Wed 11/18 and Walmart Thu 11/19, both before the open. Home Depot reported 11/17; I found no reliable result. These will move consumer-staples sentiment ([Benzinga preview](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/26/11/63372741/target-walmart-q3-earnings-could-offer-consumer-health-inflation-clues-for-investors)).
- **Ex-dividend:** About Nov 24, a $30 mechanical drop.
- **November sales:** Probably early December, around Dec 2–3. I inferred this from the pattern of earlier releases and found no stated date. Mizuho already expects strong comps, so the bar is high.
- **Earnings:** The 12/10 date is an inferred estimate, not confirmed by Costco.

**Read for a 1–10 session trade**
- **Long:** The stock is overbought, with RSI 77 and the price well above 50- and 200-day averages of about $971 and $976. The catalyst is largely priced in. A cum-dividend run-up is the likeliest reason for the rally, and long positions held past about 11/24 give back $30 mechanically.
- **Short:** Fighting a strong-momentum stock is risky.
  - Mizuho expects a strong November, and buybacks plus the dividend support the price.
  - The market-wide selloff hit Costco only mildly.
- **Sizing note:** If the ex-date is 11/24, any holding spanning it should be judged net of the $30. Remember the dividend itself is cash paid on 12/4.
- **Gaps:** I found no concrete November comp data, no unusual options flow, and no short-interest figure. The stockpiling comps could reverse in December and January.

agents.report:
**AES is not a normal momentum or breakout setup. It is a merger-arbitrage stock pinned to a $15.00 cash buyout, and the screen's signals reflect that. The 14.97 close is 0.2% under the deal price, which leaves roughly 0.2% to gain in about 11 trading days.**

**The story**
- On March 1–2, 2026, AES agreed to be acquired for $15.00 per share in cash. The buyer is Horizon Parent, L.P., controlled by Global Infrastructure Partners (part of BlackRock) and EQT Infrastructure VI. CalPERS and Qatar Investment Authority are co-investors.
- Equity value is about $10.7B and enterprise value about $33.4B including debt.
- The price is a 40.3% premium to the 30-day volume-weighted average price before July 8, 2025. That was the last full trading day before the first media report of a possible deal.
- AES said that without the deal, funding growth past 2027 would likely mean cutting the dividend or issuing significant new equity.

**Status as of today**
- Stockholders approved on June 26, 2026.
- CFIUS (the US foreign-investment review) cleared it. One summary dates that to August 27.
- The European Commission cleared it unconditionally on October 15.
- New York's commission ruled no further state review was needed, and Ohio's utility commission (PUCO) approved.
- FERC issued its final order today, November 17. It is described as the last "suspensory" approval, meaning the last one required before closing can happen.
- AES says it expects to close on or about December 2, 2026, subject to remaining closing conditions. Those conditions are not listed in the sources I could open.
- At closing the stock is delisted from the NYSE and deregistered.
- The termination fees are about $588M payable by the buyer in some circumstances and about $321M payable by AES in others.

**What this means for your screen**
- The tiny range (ATR 0.05), the correlation of 0.07 with SPY, and the stock drifting up toward 14.97–14.99 all fit a deal-pinned price. The 20-day-high breakout, the RSI of 70 and the 2.1x volume are probably arbitrage flows after the FERC news, not a trend.
- The 52-week high of 17.03 is from before the deal.
- Upside is capped by the cash price. The 14.99 after-hours print is about 0.07% under $15.00.
- Downside is a gap if the deal breaks, which would likely be well below the current price. With every regulator except possibly Indiana reported cleared, that looks unlikely but is not zero. I did not find the deal-break price.
- The expected return is a few cents, and it is slightly negative if the stock drifts above $15. It is not a swing-trade candidate. The risk and reward are lopsided against a buyer.

**Open items and caveats**
- I could not confirm an Indiana utility commission (IURC) approval from any source. Indiana coverage is critical, with legislators and consumer groups objecting. The sources call FERC the final suspensory approval, so Indiana may not be required, but I did not verify that.
- Consumer groups and the PJM market monitor protested at FERC, arguing the deal increases BlackRock's market power. A rehearing request (due within 30 days of the order) or an appeal is possible. I found nothing filed yet, and a request would not by itself stop the closing.
- Delaware appraisal rights exist and could in principle delay things. I found no sign they will.
- Dividend: the last quarterly dividend was $0.17595, ex-date October 30 (per CNBC), payable November 13. Another dividend before closing is unlikely, but I did not find that stated.
- Q3 results (adjusted EBITDA about $1.09B, net income about $527M) come only from secondary write-ups, and some search results mixed in Q3 2025 figures. Earnings do not matter here, and that is why your calendar shows no next date.
- I could not fetch the FERC order or the AES press release itself. The Dec 2 date and the approval list come from the AES press-release headline, a Panabee page and an MLQ page. GuruFocus returned a 403.
- I could not get a live spread or last-trading-day notice. Expect an NYSE notice shortly before closing.

**The quarter (fiscal Q1 2027, reported 2026-11-12)**
- Revenue was a record $18.5B, up 24%. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.40 against about $1.33 expected.
- Networking revenue rose 43% to $11.1B. Non-GAAP operating margin was 37.8%, a company high. Operating cash flow was $4.4B.
- The FY27 AI infrastructure revenue target (hyperscalers only, neoclouds excluded) was raised to $9B from $7.5B. About $1.5B of the $2.5B raise is hyperscale. Roughly half of the $9B is optics.
- The FY27 revenue guide is $74.8B to $75.8B (about 19% growth), with EPS of $5.47 to $5.53.

- **Order growth slowed.** Product orders rose 21%, down from 35% the prior quarter. Excluding hyperscalers they rose 14%. An analyst noted AI orders may have dipped sequentially. Management called AI orders "lumpy" and switched to reporting AI revenue instead of orders.

**F5 (FFIV): research summary for the 7:35 PM CT, 2026-11-17 pass**

**Bottom line:** The drop has a clear cause: a guidance-driven de-rating of a stock that had run about 80% year to date. I found no news of a broken business or any new bad event. Roughly 30% was lost in the five sessions through Nov 2. The stock then drifted lower, and it has traded in a rough $300–$325 range since, with $304–$305 at the low end. There is no known catalyst before earnings on Jan 26, 2027. The bounce is a technical one, not a news-driven one. Search results thinned out after Nov 13, and I found no sources for Nov 16–17.

**Timeline**
- **Early Oct 2026:** Shares peaked near $483, a 52-week high. The stock was up about 80% year to date going into earnings.
- **Oct 27, after the close:** F5 reported fiscal Q4 2026.
  - Revenue was $917M, up 13%, against about $884M expected.
  - Non-GAAP EPS was $4.42 against roughly $4.26–$4.30 expected.
  - Product revenue was up 23%, and systems revenue was up 29% to $239M.
  - The board added a $1.5B buyback on top of $322M remaining.
- **Oct 28:** The stock fell about 19–20% on roughly 2.2M shares, against a three-month average near 564K. It was near $370 beforehand, so the drop is consistent with the Trefis figure (a 29.7% five-day decline to $324.55 on Nov 2). Sources disagree on some figures.
  - Q1 FY27 guidance came in slightly below consensus at the midpoint (EPS $4.25–$4.37 vs $4.35 expected; revenue $875–$895M vs $886M).
  - FY27 revenue growth guidance of 8–9% slows from 11% and was in line with consensus. FY27 EPS of $18.00–$18.30 was slightly above consensus ($18.08).
  - Non-GAAP gross margin is guided to 80.5–82.5%, against 84.0% in Q4, citing higher component costs. Operating margin is guided to 33–35%, against 33.7% in Q4.
  - Piper Sandler (James Fish) cut the stock to Neutral from Overweight and kept a $461 target. Its reasons were that the iSeries refresh cycle is winding down, product growth may be peaking, and there are few near-term catalysts.
  - Other brokers raised targets: Evercore ISI to $500, RBC to $540, Barclays to $428 (Equal Weight) and Morgan Stanley to $448.
- **Nov 2:** The stock closed at $324.55 after a 5-day losing streak. Trefis said "the market explains little of this."
- **Nov 3–5:** Several executives sold shares.
  - The CEO sold 3,383 shares (about $1.19M) at $310–$323. Only 40 shares were sold under a 10b5-1 plan set up Dec 2025.
  - The CFO and at least three other insiders also sold.
  - The sales are small relative to holdings (the CEO still holds about 186K shares directly). They were not a major driver, but they hurt sentiment.
- **Nov 5:** The stock closed at $311.74, down 5.5%.
- **Nov 13:** The stock closed at $309.14, down $8.50 on average volume. The Nov 17 close of $305.15 is just above the 20-day low of $299.84.
- **Nov 17:** A plaintiff-firm "investigation" press release appeared (Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman). It targets purchasers before Oct 28, 2024 and is not a filed suit. Treat it as noise, probably tied to the October 2025 breach.

**The bear case (why guidance hurt)**
- The iSeries hardware refresh drove the 2026 surge, and management expects legacy replacement bookings to decline year over year in the second half. Systems growth is guided to upper single digits, front-loaded into the first half.
- Gross margin is guided down about 2–3.5 points. Management cited higher component costs but did not name memory specifically.
- Q4 free cash flow fell to $91M from $281M in Q3, because of inventory builds and supplier prepayments to secure FY27 supply.
- Software grew only 8% in FY26. Management guided to "solid double-digit" growth in FY27, weighted to the second half.
- Pre-earnings valuation was stretched after an 80% run.
- Macro is poor. TheStreet reported the S&P 500 fell 2.7% in the week of Nov 11, its worst since April 2025, on midterm results and AI-trade worries. Your data show it down another 1.0% today.

**The bull case**
- FFIV is at about 17x guided FY27 EPS ($305 / $18.15), a low multiple for a business growing revenue 8–9% with 33–35% operating margins.
- Revenue and EPS beat, and nine straight quarters of double-digit product growth.
- AI-related bookings exceeded $100M in FY26, up nearly 300%. Active AI customers rose fourfold to more than 200, and management estimates an AI market of about $11B by 2030.
- The buyback authorization is $1.5B on top of $322M remaining, against a market cap of roughly $17–18B. That is a meaningful bid under the stock.
- The consensus target is about $443–$469, with a Hold rating, and the only downgrade came from Piper.
- Piper's downgrade was framed as valuation-driven rather than a verdict on the business.

**Context for the 1–10 session decision**
- The setup is a post-guidance capitulation with a weak, low-volume (0.6x) bounce in a falling market. The stock has not made a new low below $299.84 yet. A break of that level would be a risk marker.
- The next scheduled catalyst is earnings on Jan 26, 2027, well outside the window. I found no conference or investor-day dates in the window.
- Possible window events are further insider sales, analyst target moves, and broader AI-trade and market swings. After guidance shocks like this, stocks often keep drifting lower, so the rebound is not confirmed.
- Two things I could not verify: why the stock fell about 4% over the last 5 sessions (no company news found), and the reason for the market's drop today.

**Bottom line:** I found no company-specific announcement that explains today's 5.1% drop to 44.73. The stock's story is a pending, unpopular Unilever Foods merger plus weakening core fundamentals. A UK regulatory deadline falls tomorrow (Nov 18), which is the main near-term catalyst. **What the sources do and don't say about today's drop**
- The only coverage of the Nov 17 move is a GuruFocus note. It confirms the close of 44.73 and says the stock is down 32.4% year to date. It cites a trailing P/E of about 8x against a five-year median of about 27x. I could not open the page, so this comes from the search summary.

**The Unilever Foods deal (signed March 31, 2026)**
- It is a Reverse Morris Trust. Unilever spins off its Foods unit and McCormick acquires it in an all-stock merger, plus $15.7B in cash to Unilever.
- After closing, Unilever shareholders would own about 55% of the combined company, McCormick holders 35%, and Unilever about 9.9%. Reported deal values range from $44.8B to $65B depending on the measure.
- McCormick has a $15.7B bridge facility and a $2.0B term loan. Per the Q3 call, leverage would be about 4x at close, falling to 3x within two years.
- Management targets $600M in annual cost synergies, an operating margin of about 21%, and EPS accretion.
- On announcement, MKC fell about 6% and Unilever about 7%. Investors objected to the size, the dilution and the leverage. Terry Smith sold his entire Unilever stake.
- Close is expected by mid-2027. The company 10-Q says it expects to incur a substantial amount of debt, and no permanent bond financing appeared in my results.
- I found no date for a McCormick shareholder vote, and no European Commission status.

**Regulatory status**
- US: the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period ended early on Oct 5.
- UK: the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) Phase 1 decision came Nov 11. It found a realistic prospect of competition harm in dry recipe mixes and dry sauces sold to UK retailers, where Schwartz (McCormick) overlaps with Knorr, Maille and Colman's (Unilever). Mustard was cleared.
- The parties had until **Nov 18** to offer remedies. If the CMA rejects them, the deal goes to a Phase 2 probe, which could mean delay, asset sales or a block.
- Unilever has been trying to sell Colman's. One analyst thinks Schwartz could instead be part of a remedy package; that is his speculation.
- MKC fell about 1.4-2.1% on the Nov 11 news. I could not find what was actually filed by the deadline.

**Fundamentals (fiscal Q3, reported Oct 1)**
- Adjusted EPS was $0.86 on sales of $2.02B, up 17.4%. Most of that growth is consolidation of McCormick de Mexico; organic growth was 1.9%.
- Guidance was reaffirmed at adjusted EPS of $3.05-3.13. Organic growth is now at the low end to midpoint of 1-3%.
- Cost inflation was raised to 6-7%, from a mid-single-digit view. Management expects it to continue into 2027.
- Consumer Americas volume fell 2.5%. Management cited price sensitivity and higher beef and seafood costs, and said the recipe-mix recovery will be slower.
- A packaging constraint could cut Q4 volume growth by up to 1 point. Q4 gross margin will compress year over year.
- Tariff refunds added about 35 bps to gross margin. The global 10% tariff assumptions are unchanged.
- The CFO said the environment is less favorable than expected, with more margin and EPS headwinds. The 2027 outlook comes with Q4 results on Jan 21, 2027 (consensus about $0.78 EPS, about $2.1B revenue).

**Analysts and valuation**
- Consensus is Hold, with a target around $55 (MarketBeat). Several firms cut targets in October.
- Earlier cuts: Deutsche Bank to $59 and Barclays to $58 in March, UBS to $51 in June.
- Bullish write-ups point to about 8x earnings, a dividend yield near 4% and the Unilever synergies.
- The stock is roughly 50% below its highs.

**Other items**
- McCormick is replacing its auditor Ernst & Young effective Nov 30 because of the Unilever deal.
- I found no mention of an activist investor.
- A 10-day cluster of lower highs and lows with no company-specific news looks like persistent selling.

**How this bears on a 1-10 session trade**
- The downside risk is a CMA Phase 2 referral or heavy remedies. A clean remedy acceptance could trigger a relief bounce.
- Today's after-hours price of 44.96 was before any CMA outcome I could find.
- No earnings fall in the window; the next report is Jan 21.
- The stock is a persistent downtrend with a possible event gap on Nov 18.

([StockStory](https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nyse/cfr/news/earnings/cullenfrost-bankers-nysecfr-exceeds-q3-2026-expectations), [Finviz release](https://finviz.com/news/411618/cullenfrost-reports-third-quarter-results))

- Fixed-rate loans reprice higher: about $275M rolls off in Q4 at roughly 5.25%, and over $1B rolls off in 2027 at about 5.70%, both modeled to reprice near 7.25%.
- Management expects a 25 bp Fed hike in December. Each hike adds roughly $1.5M to $1.7M of net interest income per month, mostly helping 2027.

- Buybacks are on pace for $190M to $200M in 2026. The Q4 dividend is $1.03, with the ex-dividend date listed as 11/30/2026 (CNBC listing).

Management is watching about four older multifamily projects with maturities in 2026 to 2028, and about $290M of homebuilder loans under margin pressure. Nonperforming assets fell to $67M, but mainly from one large multifamily payoff. Net charge-offs were 14 bps, against 2026 guidance of 15 to 20 bps.

**Tyson Foods (TSN) research, as of 7:35 PM CT, 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line:** The jump looks like relief that beef has stopped getting worse, not an earnings surprise. Fiscal 2027 profit guidance is roughly flat and below what analysts had pencilled in. The stock is now near the analyst consensus target and overbought. I'd treat it as a lean-neutral to mildly cautious setup for the next 1 to 10 sessions. The best case is a hold above the $61 area after a pause.

**What happened on Nov 16 (fiscal Q4, quarter ended Oct 3)**
- **Headline numbers:** Adjusted EPS was $0.61, against a consensus of $0.58 to $0.60 (one source says $0.52). It was down 47% from $1.15 a year earlier. Our screen's "about -0% surprise" is consistent with a tiny beat or in-line result.
- **GAAP and legal items:** GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.22. Legal accruals took $110M off Q4 sales.
- **Operating income and sales:** Adjusted operating income fell 41% to $361M, a 2.6% margin. Sales rose 5.2% to $14.59B, helped by an extra week. Excluding that week and legal accruals, sales fell 4%.
- **Full year:** Adjusted EPS was $3.44, down 17%, which Tyson said was in line with its outlook. Adjusted operating income was $1.98B, down 14%.
- **Cash and debt:** Free cash flow was $1.66B. Debt fell by $1.08B, and net debt is 2.1x adjusted EBITDA. Tyson bought back $427M of stock in the year.
- **Dividend:** Raised 2% to $0.52 a quarter.

| Segment, adjusted operating income | Q4 FY26 | Q4 FY25 | FY27 guidance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Beef | -$171M | -$52M | -$300M to +$100M (FY26: -$654M) |
| Chicken | $389M (8.7% margin) | $562M (12.7%) | $1.3B to $1.6B (FY26: $1.86B) |
| Prepared Foods | $321M (12.6% margin) | $278M | $1.25B to $1.4B |
| Pork | $16M | $47M | $75M to $175M (FY26: $228M) |
| International | $49M | $40M | $125M to $200M |

**Why the stock rose**
- **Beef:** FY26 beef lost $654M, better than the roughly $750M loss Tyson had forecast. The FY27 range runs from a $300M loss to a $100M profit, so the midpoint is a swing of about $550M. The COO said early signs show industry economics improving, with packer margins rising from deeply negative levels. He also called the reopening of Mexican cattle imports a tailwind, though the start has been slow. A Yahoo Finance piece notes JBS's North American beef margin went from -2.9% in July to +3.9% in September.
- **Restructuring:** Tyson has closed Lexington (January), closed Joslin and Eagle Mountain, and is selling Pasco. It is anchoring beef on three plants: Dakota City, Holcomb and Amarillo. On Nov 9 it announced a planned long-term partnership with Allied Beef, a rancher group, to secure cattle. Amarillo's second shift is expected to be fully back by summer 2027.
- **Low bar:** The stock had fallen more than 7% on Sept 3 after Tyson cut its FY26 outlook on beef. It was around $57 on Oct 30 and $59.87 around Nov 10.

**The bear case (why this is not clean)**
- **Profit guide:** FY27 total adjusted operating income is $1.7B to $2.15B, a midpoint of about $1.93B against $1.98B in FY26. Beef gains of about $550M at the midpoint are mostly offset by about $400M less from chicken.
- **EPS estimates:** Analysts had FY27 EPS at $3.84, against $3.44 for FY26. Flat guidance implies that estimate comes down. Per Reuters via MLQ, the guided sales decline of 3.5% to 5.5% was far steeper than the roughly 1% analysts expected.
- **Chicken:** Industry supply is up. Pilgrim's Pride's Q3 EBITDA margin was 6.8%, against 13.3% a year earlier. The CFO warned that market-driven headwinds in chicken and pork could offset gains Tyson controls, and that fiscal Q2 is seasonally hard because of weather.
- **Cattle supply:** The US herd is at a 75-year low. USDA sees beef production down about 2% in FY27. Cattle costs added about $2.1B in FY26. Beef is guided to break even only at the top of the range.
- **Cash and valuation:** FY27 free cash flow is guided to $0.8B to $1.3B, down from $1.66B. Forward P/E is about 17 to 17.8, above a five-year average of about 16. One analyst writer called it fully valued.
- **Legal and policy overhang:**
  - The DOJ has an antitrust investigation into JBS, Cargill, Tyson and National Beef, covering suspected collusion and price fixing.
  - Tyson keeps taking legal accruals.
  - The administration has pushed beef imports, including Argentine trimmings, to lower prices. Past headlines of this kind pushed the stock down.
- **Management:** Jeff Schomburger, a former P&G executive, became CEO on Oct 4, replacing Donnie King. This was his first earnings report.

**Analysts**
- **After the report:** Reported raises were BMO to $75, Piper Sandler to $72 (one source says Bernstein is also $72), and Goldman to $70. JPMorgan downgraded to Neutral with a $65 target. Stephens stays neutral.
- **Caveat:** The raise and downgrade list comes from a single StockAnalysis headline summary that I could not trace to the original notes. Other search snippets showed older raises with the same target numbers, so treat the figures with care.
- **Consensus:** Hold across 13 analysts. The average target is about $64 to $67 (sources differ), so the stock is close to it. There isn't much room to the average target, though the high targets of $70 to $75 are well above.

**Technical levels from TradingKey (opinion piece, Nov 17)**

agents.report:
**Bottom line:** The report was a strong beat and raise, and the stock is bouncing from deeply oversold. The thing holding the price down is governance and legal risk, not demand. I found no evidence of the print being a disappointment. Your screen's after-hours +4.8% matches the +3% to +5% that the press reports.

**What the report said** (SEC 8-K, Nov 17, quarter ended Oct 25)
- Revenue was $115.8B, up 103% year over year and up 20% from the prior quarter. Consensus was about $109B.
- Data center revenue was $107.6B, up 110%, against about $101.9B expected.
- Non-GAAP EPS was $2.68 against $2.48 expected. GAAP EPS was $2.70.
- Gross margin was 74.9% non-GAAP, in line with or slightly above the 74% expected. It was down from the prior quarter because of the Vera Rubin ramp.
- Q4 revenue guidance is $130B ±3%, against about $125B expected. The quarter has an extra week. Guidance assumes no China data center compute revenue.
- Q4 gross margin guidance is 71.0% to 72.0%. That is a real step down from 74.9%, and management blames higher memory prices. It is the main fundamental negative. Secondary sources disagree on how long the pressure lasts.
- CNBC says fiscal 2028 growth was raised to 75% from 70%. This is from the CNBC live blog only, so I did not confirm it in the filing.
- The board added $150B to the buyback, leaving about $227B authorized. Nvidia returned $28.1B in the quarter. The dividend is $0.25 a share, with a record date of Dec 2.
- The 8-K quotes interim CEO Colette Kress: "Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start."

**Why the stock fell about 28% in 20 sessions**
1. **Jensen Huang scandal.** He admitted infidelity, including relationships with two Nvidia employees. Around Nov 12 he resigned as CEO (CNBC and Tom's Hardware differ on the date). Kress is interim CEO and CFO.
   - The board has opened an independent investigation led by Wachtell Lipton. It concerns reports that he was a target of a foreign intelligence effort.
   - On Nov 12 the stock fell as much as 14.3% intraday.
   - Board chair Harvey Jones says the board does not intend to reinstate Huang. Huang says he would be honored to return. Heidrick & Struggles is running the CEO search.
2. **Megaspeed.** The Justice and Commerce Departments confirmed on Nov 16 to 17 that they have investigated this Singapore chip buyer since 2024, and Justice now leads the criminal probe.
   - Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive, is reportedly suspected by U.S. officials of spying for China. China calls the claim groundless.
   - Nvidia put Megaspeed on its "no sell" list in June 2025. It says it had Commerce permission for the shipments.
   - No charges against Nvidia or Megaspeed have been announced.
3. **SEC.** The Wall Street Journal reports a civil SEC probe into whether Nvidia's public disclosures misled investors. Techstrong says management said the 10-Q will be delayed. I have that from one source only, and it is worth verifying.
4. **China export rule.** A Commerce interim rule requires licenses for data center operators in Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand, closing the third-country access loophole. China threatened countermeasures. A short seller, Culper, alleges about 20% of FY2026 compute revenue was China-driven.

   - Reported drivers were software stocks selling off on AI-disruption fears, cash rotating toward the upcoming Anthropic IPO, a hawkish Fed official and AI-rally jitters. Yahoo ties no single cause to the drop.

**NKE research: Nike after its investor day (Tuesday 2026-11-17)**

This is a post-event slide on a bad message, not a fresh surprise. The press release, CNBC, the Q1 transcript and the Reuters/BNN piece I opened directly. Motley Fool, the Yahoo/Fool piece and TipRanks were read as secondary sources.

**What happened today**
- Today was Nike's first investor day in nine years. The company announced "Full Stride Ahead" and a 2031 framework.
- The stock first rose about 6%, to a high of $40.68, then reversed through the afternoon. It closed at $35.85, down 6.3%, on 61.1M shares, about 85% above the 3-month average.
- The S&P 500 fell 1.0% and the Nasdaq 0.7% the same day. Adidas fell 1.6% and lululemon 1.3%, so the broader market added to the pressure.
- The stock had rallied roughly 19% in the month before the event. Truist said that rally was sector rotation. The pre-event close on Monday was $38.26.
- I found no news that explains the 7:00 PM CT after-hours dip to 35.22. Nothing dated after the close came up, so it is probably just continued selling.

**What Nike said**
- **Fiscal 2027 (ends May 2027), reaffirmed:** revenue down a high-single-digit percentage and adjusted operating margin of about 6%. Adjusted EPS is guided to $1.15-1.35, excluding about $0.15 of restructuring costs. Operating income is expected to fall faster than revenue.
- **Fiscal 2028:** management said "2028 will be a challenging year financially." Adjusted EPS is expected to decline modestly, and revenue declines "moderate" rather than reverse. Growth at market pace returns in fiscal 2029. Pre-event consensus for fiscal 2028 EPS was about $1.53, so estimates must come down.
- **2031 targets:** about $5B of added revenue (about $4B from performance sports), 12-14% operating margin, and adjusted EPS of $3.00-3.50. About $12B in dividends over fiscal 2027-31.
- **Pace cost program:** about $2.5B of annual savings by fiscal 2031, with about $1.3B of charges.
- **Costs and pricing:** one Motley Fool piece says Nike expects product costs to rise and has "limited ability" to price through them. That is a single secondary source and I could not corroborate it.
- **China:** one secondary source says China sales stay flat from fiscal 2027 to 2031. Nike's own release only says "continue the reset in Greater China."
- **India:** Nike is building a campus there.

**The story behind it**
- Elliott Hill returned as CEO in October 2024. Market value and earnings have more than halved since then.
- **Q1 fiscal 2027 (reported Oct 1):**
  - Revenue was $11.2B, down 4%, a miss. Adjusted EPS was $0.48, a beat.
  - Greater China fell 26% in constant currency, and management guides for it to worsen further.
  - Jordan fell mid-teens. Converse fell 28%.
  - Sportswear fell low double digits. Running and football grew double digits. North America grew 2%.
  - The fiscal 2027 EPS guide of $1.15-1.35 was far below the roughly $1.61 consensus.
  - The stock fell about 10% premarket on Oct 2 to about $31.6, a 12-year low. The 52-week low of 31.97 is the closing low.
- **Q2 setup:** management flagged about 400 basis points of comparison headwind and sequentially weaker growth. Gross margin was 42.8%, up 60 basis points. Tariff effects were not discussed in the transcript, and the investor-day release gives no tariff numbers.
- **Balance sheet and dividend:**
  - Cash and short-term investments were $8.4B, a net cash position.
  - The dividend is about $2.4B a year, roughly a 4% yield.
  - Earlier analyses (April 2026, lower quality) showed a payout above 100% and speculated about a cut. The CFO now calls the dividend a "significant priority."
  - A 2031 target tied to $12B of dividends makes a cut less likely.
- **Valuation:** about 30x fiscal 2027 EPS, or about 11x the 2031 target midpoint.

**Analysts**
- **Before the event:**
  - Berenberg downgraded to Sell on Oct 6, with the target cut from $49 to $27.50. TradingKey's claim of a Berenberg downgrade today looks like a misdated mention of that note.
  - Morgan Stanley (Underweight) cut its target to $25 on Nov 4, saying the "sales reset is far from over, 2+ additional years possibly ahead."
  - Truist cut to Sell on Nov 5 with a $29 target. It cited retro Jordan product sitting on shelves, no visibility on a China bottom, and tough comparisons.
  - Bank of America has an Underperform rating and a $24 target.
  - BTIG has a Buy and a $50 target. Cantor is Neutral at $38.
  - HSBC, RBC, KeyBanc and JPMorgan have also downgraded this year.
- **Consensus:** Hold, with an average target of about $36.45 and a range of $19-60. Only about 26% of analysts rate it Buy, the lowest share in at least two decades.
- **After the event:** I found no confirmed target changes. Expect cuts to fiscal 2028 estimates and targets over the next one to two sessions.

**Setup for a 1-10 session trade**
- **Bear case:** an investor-day "sell the news" reversal on high volume is a bearish signal. It broke below the 20-day low and the 50-day average (36.84). The tape is already bearish, with the 50-day below the 200-day and falling. Fiscal 2028 estimate cuts and target cuts are likely over the next one to two sessions, with a weak market in the background. Value buyers are unlikely until fiscal 2028 EPS clears. Next earnings are Dec 17, outside the 1-10 session window, so there is no scheduled catalyst that could rescue it.
- **Bull case:**
  - Valuation on 2031 targets looks cheap.
  - The dividend is stable and the company has net cash.
  - Net cash makes an equity-raise or dividend-cut scare less likely.
  - Q1 gross margin improved, China cleanup is underway, and running and North America show growth.
  - Bad news is now fully out in the open, and the stock sits just above the October low (31.97, about 11% below the close).
  - A sharp one-day capitulation could set up a bounce.
- **Gaps in this research:** the exact fiscal 2028 EPS guide (only "modest decline"), tariff figures, post-event analyst targets, and the cause of the after-hours drop. Sources disagree on the day's drop (-6.3% in most, -7.1% in the Yahoo ticker, -5.3% in Alphastreet); your 35.85 close matches Motley Fool and Yahoo.

# COPX research brief, written 7:35 PM CT on Tue 2026-11-17

## Summary
COPX is falling with the copper price, and copper is being sold as a proxy for AI spending, not because physical supply or demand weakened. The fall began in the first week of November with the AI-equity selloff and copper's drop. It then broke lower on Mon 11/16, when the fund fell about 5.4% in one session. Today's after-hours bounce looks tied to Nvidia's strong earnings. That is the one fresh catalyst, and it cuts against further selling.

## Timeline
- **Early November:** Copper hit its lowest level since July on AI-slowdown fears and tariff doubts. It bounced briefly above $14,100 on 11/4 after the US midterms, then resumed falling. LME cash was about $13,955 on 11/6.
- **11/4:** Ivanhoe cut its 2027 Kamoa-Kakula guidance by about 19% after flood and seismic recovery ran long. Ivanhoe's stock hit a four-year low. This is a supply negative, which is supportive of the copper price, though bad for that miner.
- **11/9:** Scotiabank (Orest Wowkodaw) said miners trade at about a 2% discount to spot copper. The average premium has been 4% year to date, 15% in 2025 and 16% over three years.
  - P/NAV is 1.03x against a three-year average of 1.43x.
  - Scotiabank called valuations "relatively attractive".
- **11/12-11/13:**
  - Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on 11/12.
  - Goldman Sachs attributed the copper drop to AI-equity positioning, not looser physical supply, and said its forecast is exposed to tariff and positioning risks.
  - LME copper fell 1.6% to $13,371 on 11/13, its fifth straight weekly loss and biggest weekly drop since March.
  - Shanghai warehouse stocks fell 18% in the week to the lowest since December 2023. The Yangshan import premium hit a record $285 a ton.
  - COPX was on track for a record 12th straight weekly loss, the longest streak in LSEG data since April 2010. Its weekly RSI was 28.3, the most oversold since April 2025.
- **Mon 11/16:** Copper fell to a four-month low.
  - Chinese October data missed. Consumption and industrial production came in below estimates, and investment unexpectedly fell.
  - Hawkish Fed comments raised expectations of further rate hikes.
  - The S&P 500 fell about 2% and the Nasdaq about 2.5%.
  - Comex copper fell 1.2% to about $6.06 a pound, below $6 at times.
  - COPX fell about 5.4%, to roughly 65.5, and the tail of the selloff hit Asian miners on 11/17.
- **Tue 11/17 (today):**
  - LME copper was down 0.2% at about $13,225, near its lowest since July 1. The Shanghai contract was at its lowest since 6/25.
  - The dollar hit a 19-month high on Fed-tightening bets.
  - The US stepped up efforts to curb China's access to advanced AI chips.
  - Capstone Copper cut the bottom of its 2026 guidance to 195,000 tonnes from 200,000, citing a delayed Pinto Valley restart.
  - Gold hit a one-year low on rate expectations.
- **After the close:** Nvidia reported fiscal Q3 results.
  - Revenue was $115.8B against $109.1B expected, and EPS was $2.68 against $2.48.
  - Guidance was about $130B against $125B expected, with a $2.5T backlog.
  - The board said it will not reinstate Huang, and Colette Kress is interim CEO.
  - Neocloud stocks rose after hours. One live page showed NVDA up about 3%.
  - This likely explains COPX's +1.3% after-hours print, which came on thin volume (9 five-minute bars).

## Technical levels from the web
A 11/13 technical write-up from rallies.ai gave these levels for COPX:
- **Support:** The 80-week average near $69.60 had held since May 2025, and COPX has now broken it. The next support bands were $68.49, then $66.20 to $65.38, then $57.21 to $56.93. Today's close at 65.31 sits at the bottom of the second band, and the 65.38 20-day low matches the band's lower edge.
- **Rebound threshold:** A move above $73.55 was named as the level for a more meaningful rebound.
- **Fund beta:** Global X lists COPX's beta to the S&P 500 at 2.35 as of 9/30. It has been trading as a high-beta AI and risk-appetite instrument.

## About the fund
- It tracks the Solactive Global Copper Miners Total Return Index, with semi-annual reconstitution. The expense ratio is 0.65%.
- Net assets are about $6.7B on Global X's figures. Other sites say $5.9B to $7.3B.
- Sources disagree on holdings. One lists 41 holdings with 51.6% in the top 10. Another lists 55 holdings with 39.5% in the top 10.
- Names mentioned include Teck, Southern Copper, Freeport, BHP, Antofagasta, Boliden, Lundin, KGHM and Zijin. It is global and diversified across miners, so it is not a pure Freeport or Southern Copper proxy.

## Catalysts in the next 1-10 sessions
- **Nvidia reaction on 11/18.** Does the after-hours strength hold into the open and lift copper and miners?
- **Anthropic IPO.** Pricing is expected 11/18 and trading 11/19, per secondary sources that are not confirmed. Forbes suggested a successful listing could revive interest in tech metals. A weak debut would do the opposite.
- **APEC summit in Shenzhen, later this week.** It could bring US-China trade or chip-curb news.
- **Fed and dollar.** Hawkish rate-hike expectations are the second headwind. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh gave no rate guidance on 11/16.
- **Section 232 refined copper tariff decision.** Coverage describes a proposed phase-in of about 15% in 2027 and 30% in 2028, and the decision is still open. I could not confirm the current status. The tariff drives the Comex premium and the flows between Comex and LME.
- **Freeport.** The Q3 update trimmed 2026 and 2027 copper sales for operating issues in the US and Chile. Grasberg was at a 67% ramp rate, with full capacity targeted by the end of 2027. A Bagdad expansion decision is due by year-end.

## Bull and bear read
- **Bull:**
  - The tight physical market shows in record Chinese import premiums, falling Shanghai stocks and backwardation in LME copper.
  - Supply cuts at Kamoa-Kakula, Freeport and Capstone support the price. Deutsche Bank warned of a possible price squeeze in 2027.
  - Goldman says the drop is positioning, not fundamentals.
  - Valuation is stretched down, with miners at a discount to spot copper.
  - A record 12-week losing streak and a weekly RSI of 28 are extreme oversold readings.
  - The fund is testing support, and the Nvidia beat gives it a catalyst for a relief bounce.
- **Bear:**
  - The trend is firmly down, with a death cross (50-day below the 200-day), price below the 80-week average, and a fifth straight weekly copper loss.
  - Fresh downside drivers are layered on each other: AI doubt, weak China data, a 19-month-high dollar, and Fed hike pricing.
  - The 11/16 move was a capitulation-style 5.4% drop. Such drops can lead to a bounce or to a further leg down.
  - After-hours prints on 9 five-minute bars are thin and unreliable, so the 66.15 print may not hold at the open.
  - If the AI trade is shaky, one good Nvidia report may not be enough.
  - Copper below $6 a pound and under $13,200 per tonne are levels the market has not seen since July.

## Gaps and caveats
- Forbes and the Mining.com article returned 403 errors, so I only saw summaries of them from search results.
- I found no COPX-specific fund flows, short interest, or Freeport, Southern Copper and Teck price moves for 11/16-11/17.
- I could not verify the current Section 232 status or the Anthropic IPO date from primary sources.
- Some dates on aggregator pages are inconsistent, for example the IBTimes AU article's mixed publication stamps.

**Gap Inc. (GAP): research as of 7:35 PM CT, Tue 2026-11-17**

This is a story stock that has been sold ahead of a binary earnings print, with Old Navy as the swing factor. I found no company-specific news explaining the last two weeks of decline. The cause looks like analyst target cuts plus pre-earnings de-risking. Several sources were aggregator or German-language pages, and I flag where that matters.

**The setup**
- Gap reports Q3 FY2026 on Thu 11/19 after the close, at about 1:15 PM Pacific on the company's own notice. That is 3:15 PM CT, so the report lands before the 4:00 PM Eastern close of the day's session ends, which should be checked.
  - MarketBeat, Quartr-style pages and Gap's own announcement give the date as 11/19. One page (Earnings Whispers) says 11/23, which conflicts with the company.
  - Correction on timing: the call is shown as 5:00 PM ET, so results come after the close. Treat the 1:15 PM Pacific figure from the search summary as unreliable.
- Consensus is about EPS $0.78 and revenue $4.02B (MarketBeat, 11/12). Full-year adjusted EPS guidance is $2.35-$2.45.
- UBS preview (undated, before 11/19): sales estimate raised to $4.05B (+2.8% against about +1.9% for the Street). It cut its EPS estimate to $0.78 from $0.82, against a Street figure of $0.79. UBS calls Old Navy the key swing factor, specifically whether demand improves without heavier promotions. It also flags heavier holiday discounting and excess industry inventory.
- Options imply about ±12.4% (EarningsWatcher, 11/13, an aggregator). The 10-year average actual move is about ±15.4%.
- Short interest was 13.3% of float in August (Schaeffer's). I found no November figure.

**Why the stock is where it is**
- **Earnings reactions in 2026 have been huge in both directions.**
  - March (Q4): down as much as 13% on a weak Old Navy and winter-storm disruption. Old Navy comps were +3% against 4.3% expected.
  - May (Q1): down about 14-15%. Old Navy comps were +1% against about 3% expected, and full-year sales guidance was cut to 1-2% growth.
  - August (Q2): up about 13% (to about $23.48 per TIKR) on an adjusted EPS beat and a guidance raise.
- **August quarter detail** (company release and 8-K):
  - Sales were $3.7B, down 2%, and comps were -1%.
  - Old Navy comps were -4%, its first negative quarter in nearly three years. Gap brand comps were +10%, Banana Republic +3% and Athleta -12%.
  - Adjusted EPS was $0.52 against $0.48 expected. Revenue was $3.65B against $3.69B expected.
  - Reported EPS of $1.38 was inflated by a $417M net IEEPA tariff refund recovery, and reported operating margin was 18.5% against 7.1% adjusted. The adjusted outlook excludes the refunds.
  - The rest of the refund cash is due in Q3. That is a cash and GAAP headline, not core earnings, so it should not drive the reaction.
- **Q3 guidance:**
  - Sales are guided up 1.5-2.5%, gross margin up about 25-75 basis points, with slight operating-expense leverage.
  - Full-year adjusted operating margin is guided to 7.4-7.6%.
  - Old Navy's full-year comps were cut to flat to -1%.
  - A $40M promotional reserve is split between Q3 and Q4, meant to improve Old Navy's value perception.
  - Management said Old Navy improved significantly in August with fall product and marketing (Cardi B denim, a MrBeast back-to-school tie-up). I found no quarter-to-date figure.
  - Inventory was $2.3B, flat on the year, with units up 4% due to goods in transit.
- **Capital return:** $601M of buybacks and $125M of dividends year to date. The company has $399M of authorization left and $2.5B in cash. The dividend is $0.175 per quarter, about a 3.2% yield at the prices MarketBeat used.
- **Analyst and insider activity:**
  - 8/7: Wells Fargo cut to Equal Weight. A German source gives a target of $22, but I could not confirm that from English-language sources.
  - 8/12: Jefferies cut to Hold, target $23.
  - 8/28: Barclays raised its target to $23 (Equal Weight), UBS to $42 (Buy), BTIG to $27 (Buy), and TD Cowen to $27.
  - 11/13: Wells Fargo cut its target to $22 from $23 (Equal Weight), and TD Cowen cut to $25 from $27 (Buy). The stock fell about 4% that day. Morgan Stanley raised to $25 from $23 (Equal Weight).
  - Consensus is Hold, with an average target around $27, so the stock trades well below the Street. That reflects distrust of the numbers rather than agreement with the targets.
  - Insiders sold about $24M in the last 90 days. The main sale was Director William Fisher's 500,000 shares at about $23.89 on 10/6, about $11.9M. The other was a small 10b5-1 sale. Insiders still own about 31%.
- **Valuation:** P/E is about 11, market cap about $7.6B and beta about 2.1. The 50-day and 200-day averages in MarketBeat are $22.28 and $22.96, close to your figures.
- **Management changes:** Michael Francis becomes Old Navy president and CEO in November, succeeding Haio Barbeito. I could not verify a recent Athleta CEO departure. A Stocktwits-derived claim that Erika Everett is interim Athleta lead found no confirming source. In 2025 Gap hired Maggie Gauger for Athleta.

**Context I could not establish**
- I found no news on 11/17 or the days before it that explains the 17.6% 20-day slide.
- The price quotes I saw vary by source: $19.49 on Yahoo, $20.06 on 11/16 on Finviz. Your close of $19.35 is the figure to use.
- Walmart also reports on 11/19, before the open. It fell about 10% on 8/20 after its last report. That can move retail sentiment the same morning, a day before Gap's after-close print.
- I found no peer (Old Navy competitor) or sector data for November.

**Read for a 1-10 session decision**
- The stock has fallen about 18% into the print and sits near the low end of its range, with a mean of the analyst targets well above the price. Sentiment is already poor, which favors a relief move on an in-line Old Navy comp. A miss in Old Navy comps or a weak holiday or margin outlook repeats the March and May pattern of 13-15% drops, and the price is only about 9% above the 52-week low of 17.81.

agents.report:
**Cell tower REITs (AMT, CCI, SBAC): research as of the 2026-11-17 close**

**Bottom line.** The cause of today's 3.9% group drop is not confirmed. The best-supported driver is positioning before a Dish Wireless bankruptcy mediation deadline on Wednesday 11/18. These stocks have been trading on Dish and SpaceX headlines. The trade is binary, and the outcome will probably land before or during your hold window.

**What I could not verify**
- I found no article that explains today's move. No company news, analyst action or rate story is dated 11/17.
- The only dated item is a [11/17 market recap](https://rockandturner.substack.com/p/tue-nov-17-2026-the-market-today). It says SBAC and CCI "fell before Wednesday's mediation deadline," with tower claims over $7B. It does not mention AMT.
- The same recap says Fed rate-increase odds for December are near 92%. It does not tie that to REITs.
- Sources conflict on prices. A [GuruFocus headline](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9206083/american-tower-corp-amt-shares-fall-40-what-gf-score-of-80-tells-investors) has AMT down 4.0% to $183.18, which matches your screen. A [24/7 Wall St piece](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/17/3-cell-tower-reits-positioned-to-profit-as-wireless-data-demand-quadruples/) shows a sidebar of AMT $183.18, CCI $84.16 and SBAC $174.56.
- The 24/7 article body has older prices (AMT $190.74, CCI $89.01, SBAC $185.74), and I could not tell which is which. The GuruFocus page returned a 403, so I only have the headline.
- I could not find the outcome of any Dish mediation session. Nothing is dated after 11/17.

**The Dish dispute (the main near-term catalyst)**
- Dish Wireless and Dish DBS filed Chapter 11 on June 30. Judge Christopher Lopez presides in the Southern District of Texas.
- The three towercos are pressing about $7.5B to $7.6B in lease claims. Crown Castle's share is about $4.69B, per [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/bankruptcy-law/dish-wireless-fights-7-billion-tower-claims-blames-regulators), and I did not find AMT's or SBAC's.
- Dish's defense is frustration of purpose. It says the FCC-forced spectrum sales to AT&T and SpaceX made its network impossible to operate. It asked the court to erase the claims or cap them at 15% (see [Dish Wants Tower Claims Zeroed Out](https://broadbandbreakfast.com/dish-wants-tower-claims-zeroed-out/)).
- A 7/30 FCC order barred the $8.8B of intercompany Dish DBS claims from drawing on the $2.4B creditor trust. Dish now argues that trust may be enough to pay the outside creditors.
- Litigation was paused on about 9/14, and mediation began in October. On 11/4 the judge granted two more weeks and told the parties to ["put their cards on the table"](https://broadbandbreakfast.com/dish-bankruptcy-mediation-extended-two-weeks/). The next update is 11/18, and mediation lapses unless he extends it.
- If talks fail, the court may decide how the claims are treated. [Wireless Estimator (August)](https://wirelessestimator.com/articles/2026/dish-wirelesss-bankruptcy-exit-slides-to-december-as-tower-companies-press-their-7-6-billion-claim/) said a trial would push plan confirmation to 12/2 or later.
- The towercos also want the Boost Mobile transfer unwound as a fraudulent transfer. Dish denies that.
- Crown Castle's CFO has said there is no update. Its counsel called SpaceX-related reports "wildly inflated."
- Possible outcomes are a settlement near the trust amount, extended mediation, or a trial. I found no source that says which is likely.

**Per-company facts**
- **AMT**
  - Q3 on 10/27: it raised guidance for the third time this year. 2026 AFFO per share is $11.04 to $11.16, and net leverage is 4.9x.
  - It added a $2B buyback and is selling its Canadian business for about $202M. DISH churn is a drag, and organic tenant billings grew only 1.1% (about 4% excluding DISH).
  - Reported sources: [Q3 summary](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/american-tower-raises-2026-outlook-for-third-time).
  - By my reading of the 24/7 Wall St comparison, it is the best-covered and lowest-risk of the three.
- **CCI**
  - It has the most Dish exposure and the highest sensitivity to the outcome. It terminated its Dish contract on 1/12, and says Dish owes more than $3.5B.
  - Q3 (10/21): organic billings grew about 3.5% after a $61M DISH hit, and AFFO was $1.24 per share.
  - It guides to no Dish contribution in 2026.
  - It had a $275M customer deal that adds $20M of Q4 straight-line revenue. The customer is unnamed.
  - It hit a 52-week low of $65.65 on 10/5, then jumped 13% on 10/9.
  - Its payout is thin (about 92% of AFFO), net leverage is 6.5x, and $2.2B of debt matures in 2027.
  - It traded at about 18x forward AFFO on 11/2, versus a five-year average of 19x.
- **SBAC**
  - Q3 on 11/2: AFFO was $3.19, and the full-year range is $12.15 to $12.37. U.S. leasing is weak, and domestic site leasing revenue fell 3.4%.
  - New lease billings have slipped to about $8M a quarter.
  - Sprint and EchoStar churn continue (EchoStar churn was $14M in Q3). Leverage is 6.4x, and it has an investment-grade rating.
  - The 24/7 article says the upper C-band auction is scheduled for April 2027.
  - SBAC is today's worst name (-6.5% on your screen), but I found no SBAC-specific news explaining that.

**The SpaceX angle (upside tail)**
- On 10/9, SpaceX agreed to buy 800 MHz spectrum for about $8B. Towers jumped (CCI +13%, AMT +8%, SBAC +6%) and the big carriers fell about 6%. See [Wireless Estimator](https://wirelessestimator.com/articles/2026/spacexs-8-billion-800-mhz-buy-sends-crown-castle-american-tower-and-sba-shares-soaring-on-a-tenant-that-hasnt-signed-a-lease/).
- On about 11/3, SpaceX picked Qualcomm to supply base stations for Starlink Mobile starting in 2027. Towers rose 4% to 6% (see [TIKR](https://www.tikr.com/blog/crown-castle-soars-6-as-spacex-taps-qualcomm-for-a-credible-fourth-mobile-network)).
- No SpaceX tower lease is signed. Bernstein says buying spectrum is not a commitment to build, and it estimates a standalone network at $50B to $130B. Citi and Goldman read it as a net positive for towers. Wells Fargo argues SpaceX's femtocell and rooftop approach is capital-light and may use fewer macro towers.
- Part of the recent rally was priced on a tenant that has not signed. A weak mediation headline or SpaceX doubts could unwind some of it.

**Rates**
- A September rate hike sent the 10-year yield to 5.27%, and early October touched 5.31%. Yields eased to 4.91% at the October close. I could not find 11/17 yield or XLRE news.
- Because the group fell about 3.9% against XLRE, today's move is mostly not simply a real-estate move.

**For the journal**
- Treat the 11/18 mediation update as a known binary event. A settlement or extension could bring a sharp rebound, since the group is down about 3.7% over 5 sessions against XLRE. A breakdown could extend the drop, led by CCI and SBAC.
- The drop is better explained by event positioning than by new fundamentals. The Q3 reports were all in line or better.
- Next sources to check: the court docket and Inside Towers or Wireless Estimator on 11/18, and any SpaceX lease announcement.
