agents.report:
**DLB research, 2026-11-17 evening (stock fell 3.8% in the regular session and about 3-5% more after hours).** Searches stopped turning up new facts after about 20 queries and page reads. The most important gap is that I could not confirm why volume was 5.9 times normal during the regular session, before the print.

**What happened**
- Dolby reported fiscal Q4 after the close, and the print itself was a small beat.
  - Revenue was $373.5M, up 22% from $307M. Consensus was about $372.8M.
  - Non-GAAP EPS was $1.25 against $1.19 expected, and it included about $0.04 of one-time tax benefit. GAAP EPS was $0.86.
  - Licensing was $346.8M. By market: broadcast $120.9M (+13%), mobile $61.5M (+22%), consumer electronics $32.0M (-9%), PC $29.4M (+3%), "Other" $103.0M (+71%).
  - Dolby said Q4 got a boost from a large Video Distribution Patent (VDP) deal with Meta, signed early in the quarter. It also had large "recoveries" (back-royalty catch-ups) and timing effects from minimum volume commitments (MVCs).
- The guidance is what the market is reacting to.
  - **Q1 FY27 revenue:** $285-305M. Consensus was about $358-359M, so the midpoint is roughly 18% below. Licensing is guided to $260-280M.
  - **Q1 FY27 non-GAAP EPS:** $0.41-0.56. Consensus was about $1.06-1.12.
  - **Q1 year over year:** Q1 FY26 revenue was $347M, so Q1 is down about 12-18%. Q1 FY26 non-GAAP EPS was $1.06.
  - **FY27 revenue:** about $1.42B, flat. Consensus was about $1.42-1.47B. FactSet, via CNBC, had $1.47B.
  - **FY27 non-GAAP EPS:** $4.27-4.42, midpoint about $4.35, flat on $4.36. Estimates were $4.32-4.34 in two sources and $4.58 per FactSet, so full-year EPS is roughly in line to modestly light.
  - **FY27 margins and costs:** non-GAAP operating margin about 34.5%, non-GAAP operating expenses about $775M (flat), and non-operating income down about $10M.
  - **Shape of the year:** revenue is weighted to the second half because deals are expected to land later than a year ago.
- Management gave several reasons for the weak Q1 and flat year:
  - Q1 FY26 had a positive true-up that won't repeat.
  - Deals are shifting later in the year.
  - Unit shipments are lower, with memory costs squeezing devices.
  - Q1 non-GAAP operating expenses jump sequentially to $200-210M because of Q4 tax benefits and the timing of litigation and patent-program spending.
- By line of business, FY27 guidance is:
  - Foundational audio (the older Dolby Digital-type licensing) is down mid-single digits.
  - Atmos, Vision and imaging patents are up mid-single digits, versus +18% in FY26 when recoveries lifted it.
  - "Other" (VDP and automotive) is up mid-teens.
  - Broadcast is down high-single digits.
  - Consumer electronics and PC are down mid-single digits.
  - Mobile is roughly flat.
- Memory pricing is the main macro worry.
  - Management said memory pressure is hitting low-end phone volumes. One executive put low-end phone memory at over 50% of bill of materials, up from about 15%.
  - Mobile royalties are cushioned by MVCs, but those reset at renewal in FY27 at lower expected volumes.
  - PCs are the second most affected market.
  - This pressure was already flagged on the Q3 call.

**Company and management**
- Marc Whitten became CEO on August 27, 2026, replacing Kevin Yeaman, who retired after about 17 years as CEO.
  - Whitten's background is Microsoft/Xbox, Sonos, Unity, Cruise and Meta robotics.
  - The stock fell about 3.9% on the CEO news.
  - This was his first call. He gave four priorities: a high-performance culture, simpler operations, leadership in AI, and durable profitable growth. He promised more strategy detail "in coming quarters."
  - He declined to commit to a return to double-digit growth.
  - A "reset" or kitchen-sink read is plausible but is my inference, not something management said.
- Capital return and balance sheet:
  - FY26 buybacks were $265M (4.3M shares), and about $362M remains on the authorization.
  - The dividend is $0.39 a quarter, up about 8%, payable Dec 9 to holders of record Dec 1.
  - Cash and investments are about $713M with no debt.
  - Operating cash flow was $400M, down from $472M, and purchases of intangibles rose to $61M.
  - The stated policy is to at least offset stock-compensation dilution.
- Growth stories management highlighted:
  - VDP went from about 6 licensors to 47 and should exceed 10% of revenue by FY28.
  - Automotive has design wins in the US, Europe and China plus a Mahindra launch, and may be broken out separately.
  - Dolby Vision 2 has been adopted by Hisense, TCL and TPV.
  - Meta AI glasses can capture audio in Atmos, a small but fast-growing category.
- Dolby has an investor event at CES on Jan 7, 2027, at 7:30 a.m. PT. The next earnings report is around late January.

**Price and sentiment context**
- The stock closed at $58.82 versus $61.16 the day before. MarketBeat showed an intraday low around $58.60 and an open of $61.13.
- Before today the stock sat near its 50-day average ($61.0) and 200-day average ($59.4) per MarketBeat, close to the figures you quoted.
- After hours, reports ranged from -3.1% to about -5.2%, with $55.77 and about $56 cited. Your 7:00 PM CT quote of $56.60 sits in that range.
- Rosenblatt cut its target from $85 to $80 on Monday, before the print, and kept Buy. MarketBeat showed a consensus target of about $85, "Moderate Buy" (2 Buy, 2 Hold). StockAnalysis showed about $79 from four analysts.
- Insider sales were small, and the stock was about $51.78 on July 30 before Q3. The 52-week range was $48.26-69.95 per MarketBeat, versus your $47.98-69.11.
- After Q3 (July 30) the stock gapped up about 12% on Meta-driven Q4 guidance. The stock has been flat to weaker since, so the market already gave credit for the Q4 strength that has now printed.
- I did not find post-earnings analyst moves on 11/18, since it is only the evening of 11/17. Some Barrington and Rosenblatt trim items I found are undated and may refer to an earlier quarter.

**Trade-relevant read**
- The print is a beat, and the Q1 shortfall looks mostly lumpy (true-up comparison, deal timing, opex timing), with the full year essentially flat. That favors a modest drop rather than a collapse, which matches the roughly 3-5% after-hours move.
- The negatives are a flat FY27 after a year of 5% growth, falling foundational and mobile royalties tied to memory cost, a new CEO with no growth target, and a Q1 EPS guide well under half of consensus.
- The reasoning for a bounce is mean reversion, support near $56-58, the large buyback, and a 2.6% dividend yield, plus the likelihood that Q1 is the trough because revenue is weighted to the second half.
- Expect analyst target cuts on 11/18, and expect the first prints to be noisy given the wide after-hours range ($55.77 to about $56.60).

**Caveats**
- Several quotes (the after-hours percentage, consensus figures) differ across sources. The Dolby press release and 8-K are the reliable numbers.
- Third-party transcript summaries came from automated tools and are not verified.
- I found no data on short interest or on why regular-session volume was so high before the print.

agents.report:
**Bottom line:** HALO has sold off on a patent-driven change in the story. The business is still growing fast. The drop is not a collapse in earnings, and I found no new negative news in the last few days. I found nothing that identifies a bottom or a turn.

**What happened**
- **Q3 report, Nov 5 (after the close).** [The company's results](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001159036/000115903626000143/ex991q320268-k.htm):
  - Revenue was $493M, up 39%. Royalties were $341M, up 44%. Product sales were $137M, up 46%. Non-GAAP EPS was $2.39.
  - 2026 guidance was raised: revenue $1.860–1.925B, royalties $1.235–1.255B, non-GAAP EPS $8.75–9.05.
  - The market wanted more. [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/halozyme-falls-6-as-raised-guidance-fails-to-impress-investors-5006041) reported a roughly 6% after-hours drop.
- **Nov 6.** The stock fell more than 13% on a [Leerink downgrade](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9181578/halozyme-therapeutics-halo-shares-drop-over-13-after-leerink-downgrade) from Outperform to Market Perform. The price target was raised from $110 to $117. The reasons given were limited long-term growth, mostly Keytruda royalties, and constrained Keytruda Qlex optionality. Per [Trefis](https://www.trefis.com/stock/halo/articles/624246/can-you-make-money-off-halozyme-stock-now/2026-11-11), the stock was down 21.5% from its Oct 29 high by Nov 11.
- **Nov 11.** [Morgan Stanley](https://www.tradingview.com/news/seekingalpha:5b63d16c5094b:0-halozyme-downgraded-at-morgan-stanley-on-valuation/) cut to Equal Weight on valuation and raised its target from $105 to $109. It said more value depends on Hypercon, a new antibody-drug-conjugate opportunity, and the next wave of ENHANZE launches. Zacks also cut to Hold.
- **Nov 6.** Citizens JMP went the other way and raised its target from $93 to $149 ([MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/insider-halozyme-therapeutics-nasdaq-halo-ceo-sells-20000-shares-of-stock-2026-11-16/)). Consensus is Hold, with 7 Buy, 5 Hold and 1 Sell. The average target is about $108.

**The core issue: Merck's subcutaneous Keytruda (Keytruda Qlex)**
- Merck's subcutaneous Keytruda uses an enzyme Halozyme says infringes its MDASE patents. Halozyme sued in New Jersey in April 2025 over 15 patents. Merck responded with post-grant review petitions at the US patent board. Halozyme says MDASE is separate from ENHANZE, its core licensing platform.
- **US:** The board has been ruling against Halozyme.
  - [May 12 and 18](https://biologicshq.com/keytruda-qlex-updates-final-written-decisions-find-two-halozyme-ph20-patents-unpatentable-while-institution-is-denied-for-third-patent/): two final decisions found all challenged claims unpatentable for lack of written description and enablement, not obviousness. A third review was not instituted.
  - A [later update](https://biologicshq.com/keytruda-qlex-updates-ptab-finds-four-additional-halozyme-ph20-patents-unpatentable-and-halozyme-appeals-prior-fwds/) says Halozyme is appealing. A search snippet dates further adverse decisions to Sep 25, Oct 1 and Oct 15, but I did not open those.
  - Management says it is "very confident" on appeal, which could run to 2028. It also said it has had no talks with Merck.
- **Europe:** Halozyme is winning.
  - A German injunction came in Dec 2025.
  - On Oct 7, 2026 a Dutch court found infringement, rejected Merck's invalidity case, and barred sales in eight countries (Belgium, Denmark, France, Ireland, Italy, Sweden, Switzerland, the Netherlands). Management put those markets at about 20% of global subcutaneous royalties.
  - Merck's filings, via a search summary I did not open, say Halozyme consented to revocation of the '622 patent in the UK. A UK trial on a different patent, the '347, starts Nov 30, 2026. Halozyme also filed for a preliminary injunction in Italy in September.
- **Keytruda Qlex is selling well.** [Merck reported](https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2026/10/29/merck-mrk-earnings-q3-2026.html) $830M in Q3, against about $649M expected. Merck targets 30–40% subcutaneous adoption in the US. A single Korean source puts conversion at 9.7% now, which I could not confirm.
- **Why that matters:** If the US patents fall, Halozyme's upside from Keytruda Qlex shrinks, and the sales Merck is making in the US are royalty-free. Halozyme has said nothing about how much Keytruda royalty is in guidance. The call did not cover it.

**Fundamentals**
- **Pipeline:** There are 10 commercial ENHANZE products and 12 in development. Up to 13 new products could launch around 2029–2032. The first Hypercon clinical starts are expected in the first half of 2027.
- **Royalty structure:** Management says royalty rates step down only modestly if no valid patent exists. The step-down on the Darzalex royalty in Europe starts in March 2029, per a company deck. One third-party summary says Darzalex royalties run through 2032, but I did not confirm that in a company filing.
- **Balance sheet:** Cash is $1.08B and debt is about $3.3B. Net leverage is 2.4x. The company raised $1.5B in convertible notes this year and plans to retire the 2027 and 2028 notes at maturity.
- **Buyback:** $400M year to date. Q3 repurchases averaged $79.47 per share, well below today's price.
- **Valuation:** The price is about 11 times 2026 EPS guidance. MarketBeat shows a $11.0B market cap and a 12-month range of $61.22 to $134.00. The 50-day average is $114.29 and the 200-day is $85.63. Those match your screen.

**Other facts**
- **Insider selling:** CEO Helen Torley sold 20,000 shares on each of Nov 13 ($100.38) and Nov 16 ($98.38), plus other 20,000-share blocks in prior months. The Nov 13 sale was under a 10b5-1 plan. She has sold on a regular schedule before, so this looks routine rather than a signal.
- **Rybrevant (Janssen) in head and neck cancer.** On Nov 6 the FDA granted accelerated approval to the subcutaneous version, which uses ENHANZE.
- **Trefis history:** After 20 past drops of more than 20% since 2010, 16 left the shares higher a year later. The median worst point within that year was about -13.5%.

**Catalysts in a 1–10 session window**
- UK trial starts Nov 30. Italian injunction news could come at any time.
- Any further US patent-board decisions. Roughly 10 reviews were pending as of the Q2 call, and I could not confirm how many remain.
- Further analyst moves.
- 2027 guidance and the updated long-range outlook come in February, outside the window.
- No Halozyme-specific scheduled catalyst is certain to land in the window.

**For the decision**
- **Case for a bounce:**
  - The sell-off was a rerating on a long-term Keytruda debate rather than new bad news. Earnings and guidance were raised.
  - RSI is 23.
  - The buyback and cheap multiple give some support.
- **Case against:**

**Bottom line:** LOPE fell about 20% on 2026-11-05 after the Q3 report and has stayed pinned near the lows since. It looks like a fundamentals-driven de-rating, not a panic. I found no new company-specific news after Nov 9 to explain the last 8 sessions. The sources agree on the basic facts, but their price figures conflict (details at the end).

**What happened**
- Q3 was reported Nov 4 after the close. Adjusted EPS was $1.77 against $1.76 expected. Revenue was $267.3M against about $270.1M expected, up 2.4%.
- Shares fell from about $150.67 to a $122–124 close on Nov 5 (sources differ). They hit an intraday low near $115 on Nov 6 and closed at $117.69.
- Closes since: Nov 10 $116.50, Nov 11 $117.75, Nov 12 $117.77. Nov 13 and Nov 16 closes weren't found. Today closed at $115.23, down 3.42%, per the Motley Fool takeaways page.
- This is a post-earnings gap down followed by a slow grind, with a lower close today.

**Why it fell**
- **Ground campus miss:** Fall new students at Grand Canyon University (GCU) were flat. Total ground enrollment was about 3% below management's plan, and ground enrollment fell 4.1% to 23,650. Ground has been roughly flat for about three years.
- **Online new starts flat:** Management had guided to mid-to-high single-digit growth. It blames leads converting later than expected and says conversion "looks very good". Total online enrollment is still up 7.1% to 115,520 because retention is high.
- **Guidance cut:** Full-year revenue guidance is now $1,160.7–1,161.7M. Operating margin is 27.6–27.7%, "roughly flat". Full-year EPS is $9.81–9.85 GAAP and $10.09–10.13 adjusted. Q4 EPS is $3.57–3.61 GAAP and $3.63–3.67 adjusted. Q4 service revenue is $320.5–321.5M.
- **Cost pressure:** Marketing spend is growing faster than revenue. Online revenue per student is slipping from a mix shift to lower-net-tuition programs. Spending on partner growth and licensure programs is weighing on margin.
- **Flat adjusted results:** Adjusted EBITDA fell 3.2% to $73.5M, and adjusted operating margin was 20.5% against 22.3% a year ago. The GAAP EPS of $1.67 against $0.58 is distorted by a $35M litigation charge in the year-ago quarter.
- **Contract change:** A new agreement with GCU took effect July 1, 2026. Fees are now 60% of tuition and academic fees, and GCE no longer gets a share of ancillary revenue such as housing. Management says the operating-income effect is immaterial. One source says it trims revenue by about $4M in Q3 and about $6M in Q4.
- **Timing:** About $7.5M of revenue moved from Q3 to Q4 because the fall semester started later.
- **Sector selloff:** Education stocks sold off together that week. Strategic Education reported a miss across all segments and BMO downgraded it. BMO's Nov 9 note said sector valuations were near all-time lows.
- **Market backdrop:** A Bloomberg market wrap reported the S&P 500 fell 1.9% on Monday, Nov 16. That is likely part of the recent weakness.

**Bull case (from management)**
- **2027 targets (not guidance):**
  - Ground growth above 10%, from joining the Common App (GCU's first time), a construction and industrial technology college, Honors College expansion and a new law school.
  - Online growth of 5–6% and hybrid growth in the low double digits.
  - Total enrollment growth above 7%.
- **Early evidence:** The Common App brought 5,600+ applications in September and October.
- **Hybrid campuses:** Enrollment is up 14.1% across 48 sites that are about 60% full. Revenue per student is more than three times online. Four more sites are planned for 2027, with a target of 80 sites.
- **Buybacks:**
  - The board added $355M on Oct 28, leaving $394.5M of authorization.
  - Year to date the company bought 1.93M shares for $306.4M, an average near $159, plus 225,770 more shares after quarter-end.
  - Shares outstanding fell to 25.5M from 27.4M at year-end.
  - There is no debt. A new $100M revolver will mostly fund buybacks.
- **Regulatory pressure has eased:** The FTC suit was dismissed and a $37.7M fine rescinded in 2025, per a third-party column (briefglance). Earnings-accountability rules finalized July 1, 2026 drop the debt-to-earnings test, so fewer programs should fail. The Q3 call didn't mention regulation.
- **Valuation:** Roughly 11.5x the adjusted guided EPS of about $10.1 at $115, and about 12.8x at the $130 trade on Nov 5. The P/E was 15.75 at that point, return on equity about 37%, and beta 0.66.

**Bear case**
- **Weak underlying growth:** Adjusted EPS is flat year over year, and buybacks are masking weak operating income. Management has now missed its own enrollment plan on both ground and online new starts.
- **Cash and buyback pace:** Cash and investments fell to $162.1M from $300.1M, and buybacks are partly debt-funded.
- **Buyback record:** Buybacks averaged about $159 per share, so the stock now sits about 28% below that average. The buyback could be a support or a fresh criticism.
- **Margins:** Margin guidance is flat, with 2027 spending on new programs ahead of the revenue. BMO says the same for Strategic Education, and that investment pushes recovery further out.
- **Partner dependence:** About 96% of enrollment is GCU. The law school still needs ABA accreditation, which can't come until after the first cohort graduates.
- **Demographics:** The traditional-age student pool is shrinking.
- **Management's explanations:** The "timing" and "conversion" explanations are management's own, with no independent confirmation yet.

- **BMO** cut its target to $173 from $182 (reported Nov 6), after $185 to $182 earlier. Its rating is unconfirmed.
- **Barrington** has $200 from July 31, with no update found.

- **Sector and market:** A further broad market selloff, or education peers moving.

agents.report:
**Atlassian (TEAM) research, as of 7:35 PM CT Tue 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line.** Atlassian's drop is two things stacked together. One is a company-specific guidance reset on Nov 6. The other is a sector-wide "AI kills seat-based software" selloff that has run since mid-October and hit hard again today. The business itself looks fine. The risk is that the sector multiple keeps compressing, and a close above $152 and a Thursday reaction to the Anthropic IPO are the near-term tests.

**How the move happened**
- In Aug 2026 Atlassian reported fiscal Q4 and the stock jumped about 30-35% in a day. It went from below about $110 to about $146 after hours ([SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/08/06/atlassian-stock-skyrockets-30-cloud-growth-roars-back/), [Forbes AU](https://www.forbes.com.au/news/innovation/atlassian-defies-saaspocalypse-fears-jumps-35-after-strong-earnings/)). The same release disclosed that CEO Cannon-Brookes planned to buy up to $250M of stock personally under a 10b5-1 plan ([Börse-Global](https://www.boerse-global.de/atlassian-aktie-250-millionen-dollar-kauf-von-cannon-brookes/817639)). That is separate from the company's own buyback, which bought $348M that quarter.
- The stock ran to the $229.96 high and then began sliding in the Oct 16 software selloff. IGV has had five days of -3% or worse since Oct 16.
- Nov 5 close was $183.29. After the Q1 FY27 report that evening, it fell about 16-17% to $153.68 on Nov 6 (after-hours low about $147) ([Upside Brief](https://upsidebrief.substack.com/p/what-atlassians-first-quarter-results)).
- It was roughly $150-152 on Nov 12-16 on low volume ([Blockchain.News](https://blockchain.news/news/20261116-price-prediction-team-oversold-bounce-meets-heavier-overhead-supply)). Today it fell 6% to $140.98.

**The Nov 6 earnings reaction.** The headline numbers were strong, so the drop was about guidance.
- Revenue was $1.772B (+24%) against about $1.71B expected. Cloud revenue grew 31%. Adjusted EPS was $1.65 against $1.43 expected. Free cash flow was $463M.
- Remaining performance obligations (contracted revenue not yet recognized) rose 44% to $4.75B.
- Guidance disappointed:
  - Subscription ARR growth is guided to slow from 22.5% to about 18.5% by fiscal year-end.
  - Q2 cloud growth is guided to about 27%, roughly 4 points below Q1.
  - Full-year FY27 revenue growth is guided to about 13.75%.
- Data Center growth slowed to about 5%. Management guides it down about 14% in Q2 and 16% for the year. The product retires in March 2029.
- The CFO attributed the caution to tougher comparisons and to Atlassian lapping the DX acquisition in Q2. Analysts pushed back, asking why the Q1 beat wasn't passed through to the full-year guide ([Motley Fool transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/11/06/atlassian-team-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/), [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/05/atlassian-shares-fall-17-as-slower-subscription-growth-forecast-overshadows-earnings-beat/)).
- On AI, over 87% of enterprise cloud customers use Rovo (Atlassian's AI assistant), but no AI revenue figure is disclosed. Usage-based pricing starts in early December, and management assumes no meaningful revenue from it in FY27. Gross margin was about 85%.
- Management says seat expansion was "incredibly strong", but it gave no seat counts. Anthropic was not mentioned on the call, and OpenAI was called a partner.
- One bear point from the Upside Brief write-up: part of the free cash flow came from faster collections. Its author estimates about $246M excluding that timing benefit.

**Analysts.** I found price-target cuts but no rating downgrades. These cuts all post-date the Nov 6 drop and come from the Cerbat Gem and Investing.com summaries, which I could not open:
- Citi cut to $220 from $245 (Buy).
- Barclays cut to $210 from $222 (Overweight).
- Truist cut to $200 from $250 (Buy).
- Canaccord is at $175 (Buy) and Guggenheim at $280 (Buy).
- Jefferies, Oppenheimer, Wells Fargo and BTIG also cut, per Tickeron.

All targets sit well above $141, so they are not an anchor right now.

**Insider buying.** Cannon-Brookes's trust bought 13,400 shares for about $2.0M on Nov 13, at $149.41-$153.66 weighted prices. It was done under the Aug 9 10b5-1 plan. The Form 4 was filed Nov 16 ([StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/TEAM/form-4-atlassian-corp-insider-trading-activity-e9f0f5a46cfb.html)). Because it is a pre-set plan, it is a weak signal of timing. The plan could keep buying at lower prices, but I could not confirm its schedule.

**Today's selloff (Nov 17).** No Atlassian-specific news surfaced. The drop was sector-wide:
- IGV fell about 3-4%. Salesforce fell 9.4% with no company news, ServiceNow about 6.5-7%, Intuit 5-7%, and HubSpot and Workday also fell ([MLQ](https://mlq.ai/news/salesforce-and-servicenow-fall-as-software-stocks-slide-again-a-day-before-anthropic-prices-its-ipo/), [Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4673872-salesforce-leads-enterprise-software-stocks-lower-ahead-of-anthropics-ipo)).
- Drivers cited:
  - Fear that AI agents cut seat counts and pricing power.
  - Release of OpenAI's GPT-6.2.

# AppLovin (APP) research brief, as of 7:40 PM CT, Tue 2026-11-17

**Bottom line:** The stock has bounced from a broken-growth-story low to a strong earnings beat, and it now sits at 398.94, just under its 200-day average (405.08). The fundamentals reset on Nov 4. What remains is mostly positioning, valuation and lawsuit noise. I found no company-specific news explaining today's 3.9% drop. Sources named profit-taking and a weak growth-stock tape.

## How the story got here

**2024 to early 2025:** The stock was a market darling, with a high near 738. Its AXON ad engine drove huge margins, and the Apps business was sold on June 30, 2025. A 2025 securities class action covers Nov 2024 to Mar 2025. A short-seller report followed in January 2026, and a UBS target cut in February. Those two items come from a search summary I did not open.

**Mid-2026 unravel:**
- **Jul 13:** A Bank of America note flagged slower June e-commerce growth: about 750 new Shopify-style pixels in June versus 950 in May. It also noted few advertisers arrived after the self-serve platform went generally available. The stock fell 12.6% to about $452.
- **Aug 5 (Q2):** Revenue was $1.92B, up 53% and slightly below consensus. Adjusted EBITDA came in just under the guidance range. The CEO said "we fell short of that standard," and the company said model improvement was "lighter than normal."
  - The stock fell 19.6% to about $340, with a 52-week low near $332.
  - Bank of America cut its target to $430 (later $380) and downgraded to Neutral. Piper Sandler downgraded to Neutral. Benchmark cut to $500.
- **Late Oct:** Coverage said the stock was down about 60% for the year to date. It was roughly $270 going into earnings.

**Nov 4 (Q3), the turn:**
- **Results:** Revenue was $2.185B, up 55%, about $100M above the top of guidance and against roughly $2.07B expected. Adjusted EBITDA was $1.84B at an 84% margin. EPS was $4.30 versus about $4.03 expected. Free cash flow was $1.42B.
- **Q4 guide:** Revenue of $2.365 to $2.395B, against about $2.25B expected. EBITDA of $1.995 to $2.025B.
- **Buybacks:** $1.4B repurchased in Q3. The authorization was raised by $3.2B to $3.6B. Management called the share price a "dislocation." Net leverage is under 0.1x. About 331M shares are outstanding.
- **Reaction:** The stock rose about 31% on Nov 5 (reports disagree on the close, $339 to $356). It added about 8% on Nov 6 to about $386, then ranged roughly $400 to $415. It closed at $415.22 on Nov 16.

## What management said, from the call and the 10-Q
- **Model rollout:** The new model (compared with "Axon 3.0") is only partly rolled out, with no committed timeline. Bulls read this as upside, and bears as risk.
- **Consumer and e-commerce:** Consumer advertiser spend was up triple digits year over year, and double digits quarter over quarter. Management says advertisers who go through its team succeed far more often than pure self-serve ones, and very small businesses are "further into the future." That tempers the self-serve thesis that broke in July.
- **Guide conservatism:** The Q4 guide implies 8 to 10% sequential growth, against 14% in Q3. The CFO said it reflects only known factors. Q1 faces tough e-commerce comparisons after the seasonal Q4.
- **Other risks management named:**
  - Competition in a unified auction could raise prices.
  - Smaller advertisers have sparse data.
  - CTV is early.
  - M&A for data is a possible lever.
- **10-Q:** It shows one reportable segment, split roughly evenly between the U.S. and the rest of the world. Platform risk from Apple and Google is noted. No material loss contingencies are accrued.

## Analyst and positioning picture
- **Targets after Q3:**

| Firm | Rating | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Wedbush | Outperform | $600 |
| Evercore | Outperform | $540 |
| RBC | Outperform | $520 |
| Oppenheimer | Outperform | $520 |
| Jefferies | Buy | $500 (per one secondary source) |
| Needham | Buy | $475 |
| Macquarie | | $470 |
| Morgan Stanley | Overweight | $450 |
| BTIG | Buy | $450 |
| Scotiabank | Outperform | $450 |
| Goldman | Hold | $445 |
| HSBC | | $422 |
| Piper Sandler | Neutral | $355 |
| Bank of America | Neutral | $380 (Aug 11 note: $400) |
| Wells Fargo | | $347 |

- **Consensus:** Average targets run about $448 to $502 depending on the source, which implies roughly 12 to 26% upside. MarketBeat counts 20 Buy or Strong Buy ratings and 8 Hold.
- **Valuation:** Market cap is about $137B, or 25 to 28 times earnings and about 12 times sales. Beta is about 2.5.
- **Insiders:** One data page shows about $574M of open-market sales over the 12 months to late October and no purchases. A MarketBeat link mentions "CEO selling while other insiders buy," which I could not verify. I found no confirmed Nov 2026 sale.
- **Peers:** Unity rose 7% and The Trade Desk was flat on Nov 6. The sector read is that mobile ad platforms are favored over the open internet.

## Legal overhang
- A securities class action was filed Sep 16, 2026 in the Northern District of California. It names the company, CEO Adam Foroughi and Matthew Stumpf, and covers Feb 12 to Aug 5, 2026.
- It alleges misleading statements about model improvements and self-serve readiness. The lead-plaintiff deadline passed Nov 16.
- The company says it lacks merit. Earlier 2025 suits and derivative actions are stayed pending a motion to dismiss.
- I found no confirmed SEC action. A 2025 SEC-probe report I recalled did not surface in my searches.
- Realistically this is headline noise unless a ruling lands, and none is scheduled in the one-to-ten-session window.

## Read for a 1 to 10 session decision
- **Bull case:**
  - The stock is up 46% in 20 sessions on a real fundamental inflection.
  - Buybacks are large, with a $3.6B authorization against a roughly $137B cap.
  - Estimates and targets are being revised up.
  - After-hours at 402.42 is a small bounce.
  - It is above the 50-day average and well off the low.
- **Bear case:**
  - 405 is a clear overhead level, from the 200-day average.
  - The 10-day ranges are 2.2 times normal, so moves are wide.
  - RSI is 68 after a vertical move.
  - Today's down day came on light volume (0.8 times normal), which looks like drift rather than heavy distribution.
  - The stock is still far below 738, with a lot of supply from trapped holders.
  - The risk is a consolidation or pullback toward the 360 to 386 gap area after a 46% run.
- **No scheduled catalyst:** Earnings are not until Feb 10, 2027. Possible movers in the window are macro and growth-stock tape, Nvidia's earnings this week (my search did not confirm the date), and any e-commerce data points like pixel counts or app-intelligence data. A reclaim of 405 to 418 on volume would be the clean bullish signal.

## Caveats
- The Nov 5 close varies by source ($339.10, $356.10), and the Nov 17 drop is reported as 3.07% by TradingKey versus 3.9% by GuruFocus.

The Insurer says US and European insurer indices had their best month since 2022, and 42 of 44 tracked US (re)insurers rose. [The Insurer](https://www.theinsurer.com/ti/analysis/hannover-re-and-kemper-lead-gains-as-pc-stocks-rally-in-october-2026-11-02/) (summary came from search results; the page itself returned 401).

- **Higher-for-longer rates.** One piece cites about 79% odds of a December hike and notes that fixed income is 88% of Chubb's invested assets. Treat that as a forecast-style piece, not evidence. [24/7 Wall St](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/04/rate-hikes-could-be-coming-history-likes-these-4-insurance-stocks/)
- **Record investment income and buybacks.** Travelers posted $1.098B of pre-tax net investment income and Chubb $1.89B, both records. [24/7 Wall St](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/17/travelers-has-surged-40-in-2026-chubb-offers-retirees-a-different-dividend-opportunity/)

[Reinsurance News](https://www.reinsurancene.ws/everest-posts-q326-underwriting-loss-amid-casualty-reinsurance-reserve-strengthening/), [Zacks](https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/3018955/everest-group-q3-earnings-miss-estimates-on-higher-catastrophe-losses)

**COIN research, 7:40 PM CT, Tue 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line:** COIN is a high-beta bitcoin proxy in a macro-led crypto sell-off. The stock has no company-specific problem right now, and bitcoin has not yet shown a floor. The +2.5% after-hours bounce looks like Nvidia-driven risk-on, not a crypto turn. A rebound over 1 to 10 sessions is plausible, but it depends on bitcoin and rates, not on Coinbase news.

**How we got here**
- **Oct 29-30:** Coinbase reported Q3 on Oct 29. The stock fell about 11% after the report and closed at $143.54 on Oct 30.
  - Revenue was $1.216B, down about 35% year over year and roughly flat quarter over quarter. Spot volume fell about 10%.
  - GAAP net income was $719M ($2.51 per share), driven by gains on crypto holdings. Adjusted EBITDA was $333M.
  - Subscription and services revenue was $570M, about 49% of net revenue. Stablecoin revenue was $307M, and prediction markets passed a $200M annualized run rate.
  - Cash was $8.6B. Coinbase bought back $2B of stock in the quarter, with $2B left on the authorization, and holds 18,000 BTC.
  - Full-year adjusted expense guidance was lowered and narrowed to $4.15B-$4.3B.
  - Management flagged near-term volatility from integrating the INTX and Deribit platforms.
- **Oct 29:** The $6.3B Binance hack, the largest crypto theft on record and blamed on North Korea-linked hackers. Binance says it has covered the losses. Bitcoin fell from about $80K to about $65K by Nov 17.
- **Nov 2:** Morgan Stanley downgraded COIN to Underweight and cut its target to $120 from $258. It lowered its EBITDA multiple from 20x to 12x, cut 2027 revenue by 28% and 2027 EBITDA by 47%, and said "confidence in the earnings recovery has deteriorated."
  - Barclays (Underweight) cut to $120 from $149.
  - Other cuts: B. Riley to $150 (Neutral), Mizuho to $145, Wells Fargo to $174, Jefferies to $174, Compass Point to $165, Needham to $197, Canaccord to $275. One source puts the consensus target near $200.
  - Cantor was reported as still Overweight, but I could not confirm its target.
- **Nov 3-5:** Midterms. COIN fell 9.7% on Nov 5, and crypto stocks dropped more than 10% as bitcoin broke below $77K. One source says hopes for the CLARITY Act (the crypto market-structure bill) faded. The Senate cloture vote failed 49-50 on Sep 15 and the bill is stalled. A claim that Democrats took both chambers is single-sourced and unverified.
- **Nov 10-13:** Hot October CPI (+0.4% month over month against 0.3% expected). A December Fed rate hike is now priced at about 90%. A 50 bp hike was floated by Governor Waller and some traders price it. The 10-year yield is about 5.1%.
- **Nov 16:** COIN fell about 6% to $119.84 (a 52-week low), with Robinhood down 7.4% and Strategy down more than 7%. The S&P 500 fell 1.9%.
  - Bitcoin hit about $62K over the weekend, its weakest since July or August, with $1.5-2B in liquidations.
  - US bitcoin ETFs had seven or eight straight outflow sessions totaling about $1.9-2.2B.
  - MARA reportedly sold more than $1B of bitcoin, and Wintermute warned of the $50Ks.
- **Nov 17:** COIN closed at $115.02. The S&P 500 fell about 1% to a five-month low, with 426 of 500 stocks down. Bitcoin sat near $64K.

  - Ethereum is below $1,800. MSTR is below $100.

**After hours (the likely driver of the +2.5%):** Nvidia beat on Q3, guided Q4 to about $130B and rose roughly 4-5% after hours. Nasdaq-100 futures were up about 1.4% and S&P futures about 0.8%. That is a broad risk-on bounce, not Coinbase-specific news. It could fade if bitcoin does not follow.

agents.report:
**COLM research, 7:40 PM CT, Tue 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line:** The rally has a real fundamental basis. Q3 was a clear beat, guidance went up, and the Spring 2027 wholesale book improved. But most of the Q3 EPS beat is a one-off, and the stock now trades well above the analyst consensus target. I found no new catalyst before the next earnings report on 2027-02-02. The only dated events are the ex-dividend on Nov 19 and Q4 results and 2027 guidance in early February. A 1-10 session trade is therefore a pure momentum or mean-reversion call.

**What drove the move (about $61 before earnings to $75)**
- Q3 was reported Oct 29. EPS was $1.66 against $1.28 expected, and sales were $962.6M (+2%) against about $945M expected.
- Operating margin was 11.4% against 7.1% a year ago. The year-ago quarter included a $29M impairment on prAna and Mountain Hardwear.
- Management said the upside came from delayed Fall 2026 wholesale orders shipping earlier than planned. About $30M of sales shifted from Q4 into Q3, so part of the beat is timing.
- Gross margin was 49.8%, down 20 bps, so the beat came from lower SG&A (39.0% of sales vs 40.4%), not margin expansion.
- IEEPA tariff refunds, net of accommodations to factory partners, added about $0.85 to nine-month EPS. They contribute about 180 bps to 2026 gross margin. The Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs, and refunds are being paid through the CBP process.
- Guidance:
  - Full-year EPS is $4.65-4.90 (low end raised from $4.45).
  - Full-year sales growth is 2-3%.
  - Q4 sales are guided to +3.5-7% and Q4 EPS to $1.85-2.10 (vs $1.73 last year).
  - First-half 2027 wholesale is expected up mid-single digits. The order book improved from low-to-mid single digits. Management said US wholesale leans toward the mid end and international should outpace it.
  - There is no 2027 guidance until February. Management flagged input-cost pressure later in 2027 and possible selective price increases.
- The stock gapped up from the Oct 29 close. By Nov 2 it was at a 52-week high near $69.
  - BTIG (Buy) raised its target from $80 to $83 on Oct 30.
  - UBS (Sell) raised its target from $47 to $49. UBS cited improving US demand.
- It then ground higher to about $72.9 on Nov 9, $73.47 on Nov 13, $74.40 on Nov 16 and an intraday high of $75.77 on Nov 17. I found no company-specific news for Nov 3-17, so that later leg looks like momentum plus a broader consumer rebound (Nike, Deckers and Lululemon rose 6-7% on Nov 4).
- Insider selling is minor: the Nov 2 sales were about 26k shares, about $1.8M over 90 days. Director Ronald Nelson sold 1,000 shares at $75.28 on Nov 16.

**Business quality and weak spots**
- Geography: US sales were -1% in Q3 and -5% for nine months. International is carrying growth: Latin America and Asia Pacific +11%, EMEA +7%, and China low-teens. Management called China's macro tougher and said competition is rising.
- Brands: Columbia +3%, SOREL +2%, prAna -1%, Mountain Hardwear -17% (a new president, Peter Rauch, was named). Footwear is +5% and growing faster than apparel.
- Channels: Wholesale was flat. Direct-to-consumer was +5%, with fewer promotions in US e-commerce.
- Inventory is $889M, up 11%, from in-transit Fall 2026 goods and earlier Spring 2027 production. That is why full-year operating cash flow guidance was cut to $230-250M from $290-310M. Nine-month operating cash flow was -$280M, which is seasonal.
- Balance sheet: $230M cash, no debt, $226.5M of buyback authorization left. The company bought 3.3M shares for $200M at an average of $59.83 in the nine months. Buybacks were not discussed on the call. The Boyle family and insiders own about 52%.
- Management said it expects a normal winter and that the business reacts strongly to weather. Cited risks are tariffs (additional ones can't be predicted), energy costs, geopolitics and China competition.

**Valuation and positioning**
- Market cap is about $3.7B. P/E is about 16 on trailing EPS, or about 15-16 on 2026 guidance of $4.65-4.90.
- The $1.84M of net tariff refunds in earnings flatter that. Without the $0.85 of nine-month refund EPS, the underlying multiple is higher.
- The consensus target is $66.40 (2 Buy, 3 Hold, 1 Sell). The price is about 13% above it. Stale targets include Baird $65 and Stifel $67 (both July 31), Citi $68 and UBS $49. Only BTIG ($83) is above the current price. Analysts may raise targets after the move. I found no post-Q3 changes from Stifel or Baird.
- Short interest is unclear. Fintel shows 2.78M shares (about 11% of float, 5.5 days to cover). StockTitan shows 4.3M shares (20% of float) from an older date. Squeeze potential is plausible but unverified.
- The stock is above its 50-day ($61.8) and 200-day ($60.5) averages. The 52-week low is $48.83, and the stock is up about 50% over the past year.

**Setup for 1-10 sessions**
- **Bull case:**
  - Fundamental momentum has been confirmed: a beat, a raise, and a better order book.
  - There are no scheduled negatives before February.
  - It is a low-beta name (0.88) with a clean balance sheet.
  - The stock is at 52-week highs, with 2.78M-4.3M shares short.
  - The $0.30 dividend (1.6% yield) goes ex on Nov 19, a small mechanical drop of about $0.30.
- **Bear case:**
  - The stock is 22.8% above where it was 20 sessions ago with RSI 74, and it closed down 0.8% on light volume (0.9x normal) at the highs.
  - It trades above all but BTIG's target.
  - Part of the beat is timing and one-off refunds.
  - US sales are still shrinking.
  - Mountain Hardwear is weak.
  - Inventory is up and cash flow was cut.
  - Insiders are selling into the highs.
  - The 2027 gross margin is a stated risk.
  - Winter weather and further tariff headlines are unhedgeable.
- **My read:** This is a quality earnings-driven re-rating that has run well ahead of the sell-side. I would not chase it at the high. A pullback toward $70-72 (the Nov 2-9 breakout zone) with the story intact would be a better entry than buying here, and a break below $69 (the Nov 2 level) would suggest the move is unwinding. Nothing I found sets a catalyst-driven reason for further upside in a 1-10 session window.

**Gaps**
- I could not read the Benzinga transcript directly (it returned 403), so I used stockanalysis.com summaries instead.
- I found no news dated Nov 17 beyond price reports.
- I found no peer read-through from VF, Canada Goose or Gildan.

- Sources disagree on some prices. Intraday vs closing figures differ across sites, and the "BTIG upgrade" headlines describe a target raise, not a rating change.

agents.report:
**FTI Consulting (FCN), research as of the 2026-11-17 close**

**Bottom line:** The move has a real cause, a large Q3 earnings beat on Oct 29. But it has run far beyond what that news or the analysts support, and I found no catalyst for the extra leg since early November. Next-session catalysts: none found. The next dated event is the Q4 report, probably in February, plus an Investor Day "early next year."

**Price path** (sources differ slightly on exact levels)
- The stock was about $150-160 before earnings. Management bought back shares at an average of $151.55 in Q3.
- Oct 29 earnings day: up roughly 11.7% intraday to about $177 ([StockStory](https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nyse/fcn/news/why-up-down/why-is-fti-consulting-fcn-stock-rocketing-higher-today)).
- Nov 2: new 52-week high of $189.34, up 13% in a week.
- Nov 13: new high of about $202.9 ([MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-fti-consulting-nyse-fcn-reaches-new-12-month-high-heres-why-2026-11-13/)).
- Nov 17: opened around $206.6, with a high of $208.70.
- That is about a 30% gain in under three weeks, nearly all on one earnings report. No news items or sector-wide event explain the later legs.

**What Q3 showed** ([SEC press release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000887936/000119312526441751/fcn-ex99_1.htm), [Motley Fool transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/29/fti-consulting-fcn-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/))
- Revenue was a record $1.013B, up 5.9%, and all five segments grew. Revenue was slightly below consensus (about $1.008B reported versus about $1.01B expected).
- Adjusted EPS was $3.84 against a $2.74 consensus. GAAP EPS was $2.35, after a $46M special charge for staff cuts.
- Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $9.50-$10.00 (from $9.10-$9.70). Revenue guidance was only reaffirmed at $3.94-$4.10B.
- The quality of the beat is mixed:
  - A record $40.7M in Corporate Finance success fees, including a large Federal Reserve Bank of Boston loan-portfolio sale.
  - A tax rate of 17.8% versus 25.9% a year earlier.
  - Small one-offs in Economic Consulting (PTO true-ups, lower bad debt).
  - Management said that without these, Q3 EPS would be about $2.90, against a recent run rate in the low $2s.
- Economic Consulting (the Compass Lexecon unit) swung to a 7.4% margin from -2.6% on antitrust demand. Management said it should recover only modestly, over roughly five years, and that Q4 should look more like Q2.
- Restructuring work was down 1% on lower volume. Forensic & Litigation margin fell, and its profit declined from a year ago.
- Q4 guidance is soft. Management cited lower restructuring, M&A and regulatory volume, and a seasonally weaker quarter. A Goldman analyst's math implied Q4 EPS about 52% below Q3 at the guidance midpoint.
- Cost actions cut about 4% of staff (Middle East, U.K., construction outside the U.S., some EMEA/APAC). They should save about $80M annualized, with about $15M landing in Q4.
- Debt is $852M, down from $1B at June 30. $264.7M remains on the buyback authorization. Management ranks buybacks last among capital uses, behind organic growth, debt paydown and acquisitions.
- Management cited AI as a demand driver in two areas, but AI-disruption fear is the broader headwind for consulting stocks. Examples are Huron and the large consultancies, which sold off earlier in 2026. A rebound in that group may be part of the move, but I couldn't confirm it for November.

**Analysts and valuation**
- Coverage is thin: MarketBeat counts two analysts, both at Hold, with an average target of $174.50, below the price.
- Truist reiterated Hold on Nov 2 and raised its target to $180 from $158. Finviz showed a consensus target of $186.50.
- The price is above every target I found, and the stock trades near 21x the guidance midpoint of $9.75 adjusted EPS. Beta is reported as -0.15, a quirk of the data.
- Short interest is unclear. Seeking Alpha showed 11.4% as of Nov 13 and Trefis 11.1% as of Sep 30, but other sources showed 5-6%. If the higher figure is right, shorts may have fed the squeeze.

**Insiders and flow**
- Officer Paul Linton sold 4,378 shares on Nov 3 for about $832K, and filed to sell 2,000 more around Nov 4 at about $199 ([Form 144 summary](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/FCN/144-fti-consulting-inc-sec-filing-c3c0755396dd.html)). These came from option exercises and are small, but they are selling into the rally.
- Institutional filings in the news are tiny positions and don't say much.
- Company news since Oct 29 is only senior hires (Sharon Biran on Nov 17, telecom hires on Nov 9, Mark Wasserman on Nov 5) and a Nov 12 Lexology award. None is material.
- The company is in the S&P MidCap 400 per an aggregator, which I did not verify with S&P.

**Read for a 1-10 session trade**
- **For the long side:** momentum is strong, there is no earnings event in the window, and guidance was raised. Estimate revisions are likely still rising, and a high short interest, if real, could extend the squeeze.
- **Against the long side:**
  - The stock is stretched, with RSI 82 and a 36% gain in 20 days.
  - It trades above all targets.
  - The beat was partly one-off.
  - Q4 EPS is guided sharply lower.
  - Insiders are selling.
  - Today's reversal came on 1.2x volume and left a small gap between the 208.70 high and the 205.53 close.
- **Mean-reversion levels:** a pullback toward the Nov 13 breakout area (about $199-203) is the plausible near-term case. The $189 level is a deeper one.
- **What would change this:** a close above $208.70 on rising volume would be a continuation signal. A close below $198.62, the Nov 12 close and breakout base, would be a failure signal.

**Gaps:** I could not open the Benzinga transcript or the Defense World page (both returned 403). I found no sell-side commentary dated after Nov 2, and no confirmed reason for the move after Nov 2.

agents.report:
**T1 Energy (TE): research as of 7:40 PM CT, Tue 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line:** TE is a cash-constrained solar module maker. It is selling stock into weakness while its main financing is still unsigned, and the SEC is investigating its disclosures. The drop looks fundamental (dilution plus financing and legal overhang), not just oversold. A bounce is possible but has no identified catalyst.

**What happened this week**
- **Nov 12 (after close):** Q3 results, and an 8-K disclosing an SEC investigation.
  - The SEC notified the company in September. It covers public statements about Section 45X tax-credit eligibility and "certain other accounting matters." T1 says it will cooperate and can't predict the duration or outcome.
  - After-hours the stock fell about 7.5%.
  - On Nov 13 it closed near $1.97 before the drop and hit a $1.60 low at one point. Sources differ on the exact close.
- **Nov 16 (Mon):** T1 filed an at-the-market (ATM) offering of up to $100M of common stock through Roth Capital. Proceeds go to G2_Austin Phase 1 equipment and construction, working capital, and general corporate use. Shares fell about 12.8% early that day.
- **Nov 17 (Tue):** About -12% to roughly $1.31 per Benzinga, which gave no cause for the day beyond the ATM. That is consistent with your close of $1.33.
- **Dilution scale:** Market cap was about $517M at $1.755, which implies about 294M shares (a third-party calculation). At $1.33, a full $100M ATM is roughly 75M shares, or about 25% of the share count.
- **Encompass equity line:** Funds managed by Encompass Capital Advisors had a $15M equity-line agreement that expired Nov 16. One German outlet reported it. I couldn't confirm whether it was used.

**Q3 results (reported Nov 12)**

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| Net sales | $196.6M, vs $210.5M a year ago and a $274.8M consensus (Zacks) |
| Net loss from continuing operations | $34.7M ($0.12/share) |
| Gross margin | 8.5% |
| Adjusted EBITDA | -$16.4M |
| SG&A | $71.2M (headcount, financing and legal costs) |
| Production | 1,056 MW, of which 326 MW went to inventory by choice |
| Cash | $137M total, only $59.5M unrestricted (Sep 30) |
| 45X credits generated, not yet sold | $155.3M |

- **Related-party sales:** One analyst estimates about $190M of the $196.6M in sales went to Trina, T1's former parent. That is the analyst's calculation, not a company figure.
- **45X monetization:** The CFO said the tax-credit sale market for non-investment-grade companies "developed slowly." The gap between credit accrual and cash is straining liquidity.
- **Bridge financing:** A $50.4M convertible note private placement closed Sep 30, described as a bridge.

**The core issue: G2_Austin financing**
- This is the 2.1 GW cell fab. T1 is in exclusive talks with "certain institutional investors" on a mainly debt-based package. No counterparty, amount or terms are disclosed. The company says it may also need equity or equity-linked securities.
- Cell production has slipped from 2026 to 2027. Management says that if financial close happens by year-end, ramp finishes around mid-2027. The slide moved the ramp from March to April.
- T1 owns the equipment outright. Permitting, power and water are said to be on track.
- Management says the delay is not caused by the Section 232 process. Section 232 is the tariff and import-price regime on solar, and T1 got a waiver for up to 1.725 GW of imported cells.
- The ATM suggests T1 needs cash before the debt package closes.

**Guidance and business**
- **2026 production:** G1_Dallas is guided to 4.0–4.2 GW, narrowed up from 3.1–4.2 GW.
- **2027 production:** The initial plan is 5.3 GW. G1_Dallas is sold out through 2027.
- **Pricing:** Imported-cell modules are quoted in the mid-$0.30s per watt, and domestic-cell modules in the mid-$0.40s. Management says pricing has risen since the Section 232 action.
- **Tariff timing:** Higher tariffs take full effect Dec 4. Management said an onshoring relief plan could slip past December and no date can be guaranteed.
- **Long-term targets:** $375–450M of annual adjusted EBITDA after G2_Austin Phase 1. These are far from current results.
- **Side items:** A non-binding letter of intent for a Nordic data-center joint venture, and a small battery-integration business (NRI).

**Background that explains the multi-month fall**
- **Trina restructuring:** T1 paid about $274M and committed to issue 3M shares to unwind its Trina ties and keep Section 45X eligibility for 2026. It also sold $160M of 45X credits in December 2025, at $0.91 per dollar.
- **Short-seller report (May 2026):** Fuzzy Panda alleged FEOC (foreign entity of concern) non-compliance through an IP sale to Evervolt, which it says has hidden Trina ties. T1 disputed this. The SEC probe now makes that thesis harder to dismiss.
- **Earlier raises:**
  - $72M registered direct at $3.25 (Oct 2025).
  - $161M convertible plus common at $4.95.
  - Now the ATM at about $1.33.
- **Peak to now:** The stock is down roughly 90% from the $12.49 high. A secondary source cites a 54% fall from the June high into July, tied to the solar tax-credit deadline.

**Analysts**
- Consensus is "Moderate Buy" with an average target around $7.30 (MarketBeat). That is far from the price and stale.
- Needham cut its target from $7 to $6 on Oct 23, with a Buy rating. BTIG cut from $9 to $7, also Buy.
- JPMorgan has Neutral at $5 and Vertical Research has Hold at $5. Both initiated in September.
- I found no post-ATM rating changes. Short interest wasn't reported in anything I could open.

**Takeaways for a 1–10 session trade**
- **Why it could bounce:** The stock is extremely oversold and ended after-hours up 1.5%. Positive financing news could cause a sharp squeeze. That includes a signed G2_Austin debt package, a 45X credit sale, or Section 232 relief. Management has pointed to year-end for a financial close.
- **Why it could keep falling:**
  - The ATM provides continuous supply, and Roth can sell into any bounce.
  - There are no cash or financing details yet.
  - The SEC probe is unresolved.
  - Plaintiff-firm "investigation" press releases are circulating. These are routine and not a catalyst.
- **Next earnings date:** I found none, but Q4 results would be expected around March. The known near-term dates are the Dec 4 tariff step-up and the year-end financing target.
- **Liquidity risk:** A weak stock price also raises the cost and difficulty of the financing itself.

**Gaps**
- I couldn't open the ATM 8-K, the 10-Q or the SEC probe filing text. Benzinga, Seeking Alpha and GlobeNewswire blocked automated fetches, so those details come from secondary summaries.
- I found no explanation for the Oct 16 -10% move, and no short-interest data.
- Prices differ slightly between sources because they were captured at different times.

agents.report:
**NEU research summary (as of 7:40 PM CT, Tue 2026-11-17)**

I found no single event that explains the 20% slide. The best account is a reaction to the Q3 report that has kept running. Several sites (MarketBeat, Alphastreet, Motley Fool, GuruFocus) returned 403s or only snippets, so the details below come from the SEC filings, a few transcripts and aggregator pages.

**What the business is.** NewMarket makes lubricant and fuel additives through Afton Chemical, which supplies most of its profit. A smaller Specialty Materials segment, AMPAC, makes ammonium perchlorate (a solid rocket propellant ingredient) and, since the Calca purchase, high-purity hydrazine.

**Q3 2026 (reported Oct 28, after the close).**
- Net income was $124.1M, or $13.50 per share, against $10.67 a year earlier. That gain came mostly from a lower tax rate (17.9% vs 26.1%) and Specialty Materials, not from the core business.
- Petroleum additives sales were flat at $651M and operating profit was flat at $130.9M. Shipments fell 7.7%, and lubricant shipments fell in every region.
- The filing blames "broad market softness, particularly in lubricant additives." For the nine months it also cites the company's own decision to cut low-margin business.
- Profit held up only because of surcharges to cover higher raw material and logistics costs from the Middle East war, which is now in its ninth month. Underneath that, gross profit fell on higher raw material costs and lower volume.
- Operating profit fell from about $149M in Q2 to $131M in Q3. Q2 was helped by surcharges (and Q2 sales were $676M).
- Specialty Materials sales were $62.0M against $38.2M, and operating profit was $16.4M against $6.0M. Management warns this segment varies a lot quarter to quarter. The AMPAC and hydrazine capacity expansions are due by year-end 2026.
- Over nine months, capex was $88.5M, buybacks $126.4M and dividends $83.1M. Net debt to EBITDA is 1.0x, which is a strong balance sheet.
- There was no formal guidance, no Q&A and no analyst questions on the call. Management called the environment "dynamic" and said it will keep adjusting surcharges and operations as conditions change.

**Price path.**
- The stock was about $924 on Oct 2 and $876 on Oct 16.
- It closed $875.42 on Oct 28, fell about 8% after hours to $803, and closed $783.66 next session. Investing.com's own arithmetic is inconsistent here, so treat that last close as approximate.
- It crossed below its 200-day average on about Nov 3.
- It closed $692.14 on Nov 9, $709.19 on Nov 13, $696.68 on Nov 16 and $697.76 on Nov 17. Motley Fool showed it down about 22.5% over one month as of Nov 9.
- Most of the drop came after the earnings report, over roughly a week and a half, and then the stock stabilised in the $690 to $710 range.
- Short interest was 604k shares on Oct 30, up 12%, with about 4.75 days to cover. That is a modest rise, not a squeeze setup.

**Analyst and holder signals.**
- Argus cut its target to $944 on Oct 14 and kept a neutral rating. Weiss cut its rating from B to B- on Nov 2.
- I found no sell-side downgrade wave and no company-specific negative news.
- Insider activity is minor: one 400-share buy in February and nothing recent.

**Dividend.** The board raised the quarterly dividend to $3.25 from $3.00. It is payable Jan 1, 2027 to holders of record Dec 15, 2026, which is inside or just beyond a 1-10 session window. At about $698 the yield is roughly 1.9%. The dividend raise shows confidence, but I couldn't confirm the declaration date. The 8-K exists but the page wouldn't load.

**Macro and sector backdrop.**
- Brent was about $93 on Nov 17, and US-Iran talks have not produced a resolution.
- Premium base oil and additive feedstocks (maleic anhydride, phosphorus compounds) have been tight, which is why surcharges exist.
- A peace deal would lower raw costs but could also remove the surcharge support for Afton's profits. That is my inference, not something a source said.
- The market reports I found were not clear on lubricant demand. Innospec's Q3 (reported Nov 3) showed fuel specialties up, with weakness elsewhere from its Middle East legacy business and raw material costs.
- A possible 2027 tailwind is the heavy-duty engine oil specification (PC-12) starting January 2027, which could drive a reformulation cycle. This comes from one market-research summary.
- Defense demand for solid rocket motors is strong, which supports AMPAC.

**What I couldn't confirm.**
- The consensus EPS estimate for Q3, so I can't say whether it was a beat or a miss. The reaction suggests investors disliked the 8% volume drop and the lack of guidance.
- Any cause for the slide from Nov 3 to Nov 9.
- Whether the Q4 and 2027 volume picture is improving.

**For the 1-10 session decision.**
- The bearish case is falling volumes, profit propped up by surcharges, and a stock below both moving averages. Nothing in the data shows a turn yet.
- The bullish case is that this looks like valuation compression on a fundamentally profitable company, not a broken story. EPS rose, net debt is 1.0x, the dividend rose and buybacks continue.
- Earnings are not due until Feb 10, 2027, so the window has no scheduled company catalyst. The Dec 15 record date is the only dated item nearby. Macro news on Iran and oil is the main source of unscheduled volatility.

**Vontier (VNT): research as of 7:45 PM CT, Tue 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line.** The rally has a clear, mostly fundamental cause: a Q3 beat and raised guidance on November 5, after the stock had been de-rated all year. I found no news since then (takeover, activist, guidance change) that explains the continued climb. The only post-earnings items are routine: price-target raises, an insider sale, a dividend notice and an executive appointment. The move looks like a rerating plus drift after earnings, now stretched at RSI 77. Nothing found points to an event inside the 1-10 session window. Next earnings are 2027-02-11.

**How we got here**
- **Early 2026:** The stock was in the high $30s, with a 12-month high of about $48.1-48.2. The sources give two slightly different figures, and I could not confirm when the high was set.
- **February:** Q4 2025 beat and 2026 guidance of $3.35-3.50 adjusted EPS. The stock jumped about 12% on the day, and a Trefis piece describes an 8-day, 15% run.
- **May:**
  - Q1 missed slightly (adjusted EPS $0.80 vs $0.82), the Q2 sales guide was below estimates, and the stock hit a 12-month low near $32.40.
  - KeyBanc cut its target to $40 from $50, and Argus went to hold.
  - Operating cash flow fell 58% to $46.5M.
  - The company agreed to sell a majority stake in Teletrac Navman, with an expected $60-110M loss.
  - Trefis put the price at about $28.92 on May 22 and attributed most of the drop to multiple compression.
- **Mid-year low:** The 12-month low is $27.25, with the 200-day average now at 33.95.
- **August:** Q2 beat and raised guidance.
- **November 5 (Q3):**
  - **Reaction:** The stock closed at $37.58 the day before and opened at $42.01, up about 6.7% in the morning session by one source's account.
  - **Results:** Sales were $736.9M, down 2.1% because of the Teletrac sale. Core sales grew 5.7%, against guidance of about 5%. Adjusted operating margin was 24.3%, up about 300 bps. Adjusted EPS was $0.92, against $0.78 a year earlier and guidance of $0.82-0.86, and free cash flow conversion was 107%.
  - **Guidance:** FY26 adjusted EPS was raised to $3.60-3.64 from $3.45-3.55. Q4 adjusted EPS guidance is $0.99-1.03 on about $785M of sales and about 3% core growth.
  - **Cost program:** The savings target rose to about $20M from $15M.
  - **Capital:** Buybacks were $80M in the quarter and $280M year to date (about 6% of shares). Net leverage is 2.3x, and the CFO called repurchases "one of our most attractive uses of capital" at current levels.

**Segment story**
- **Environmental & Fueling Solutions** is the driver. Core sales rose 13.1% and margin was 31.6%, up 240 bps. Management cited dispenser demand and FlexPay 6 payment-terminal upgrades.
- **Possible tailwind, vendor claims only:** Gilbarco and Invenco marketing pages say older FlexPay II terminals must be upgraded by December 2027 for PCI compliance, and a trade-up promotion ends December 31, 2026. I found no independent confirmation of those dates.
- **Mobility Technologies:**
  - Sales fell 13.7% on the Teletrac sale, but core sales rose 2.2%.
  - Margin was up 740 bps, about 250 bps of it from the divestiture and the rest from simplification.
  - It is expected to return to growth.
- **Repair Solutions (Matco)** is the weak spot. Core sales fell 1.0%, margin fell 180 bps, and technician spending is constrained. Diesel prices are pressuring franchisees, and lower interest income from tighter underwriting hurt. A new Group President, Cameron Richardson, was named for the segment.
- **2027 early view:** Blended growth of 3-4%, incremental core margins of 30%+, about $10M of carryover savings, and convenience retail plus fleet (about 80% of the business) growing 4-5%. Repair is expected flat to down low single digits.

**Risks and caveats in the story**
- The Q3 call flagged new supply-chain constraints and memory-chip cost inflation (an analyst question). A roughly $4M favorable mix benefit in Q3 won't repeat.
- Fleet orders are lumpy.
- EFS growth partly reflects customers buying full dispensers instead of payment kits, which shifts revenue away from Mobility.
- Q4 guidance was described by one source as below analyst expectations. I couldn't verify that, and it did not stop the stock.

agents.report:
**Nexstar (NXST): research as of 7:45 PM CT, Tuesday 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line.** The stock's story is the closed-but-frozen Tegna merger, with the Ninth Circuit hearing held today and no ruling. The 22% run in 20 sessions started with the Nov 5 earnings and followed analyst target raises. I found no single catalyst and no reason for today's 1.7% drop. Today's hearing is the nearest binary risk, and the unknown ruling date can land inside a 1 to 10 session window. I could not confirm the exact timing of a ruling, a settlement, or an FCC full-Commission vote.

**The story**
- **Deal closed, then frozen.** Nexstar closed the roughly $6.2B Tegna purchase on March 19, 2026. The FCC Media Bureau waived the 39% national cap without a Commission vote, and the DOJ cleared it. That gives Nexstar 265 stations, plus the CW and NewsNation.
- **Injunction.** Eight states and DirecTV sued, and the coalition grew to 13 states. Judge Nunley (E.D. Cal.) issued a preliminary injunction on April 17 (effective April 21) requiring Tegna to be held separate until trial. Nexstar says the trial is set for July 6, 2027. I got that date only from the call summary, not from a court source.
- **Compliance violation.** In August the judge found Nexstar violated the order by putting its executives on Tegna's board. He ordered a special master or magistrate and monthly compliance filings.
- **Effect on the numbers.** Nexstar cannot integrate Tegna or capture synergies. Management removed synergies from its covenant math because the trial date falls close to the September 2027 synergy window.
- **Settlement.** CEO Perry Sook said in August that Nexstar is open to settling and that it "has a benefit to us." One source says satisfying the states would likely require substantial divestitures that hurt the economics. Nexstar settled separately with Ohio's attorney general on newsroom commitments.

**Ninth Circuit hearing, today**
- Nexstar asked the court to narrow the injunction to the 31 overlap markets where both companies have Big 4 stations, and to remove the states from the case. It is not asking to reverse the injunction.
- Reports say the panel (Berzon, Rawlinson, and possibly Rodriguez) was skeptical of the 31-station carve-out. Berzon asked "who's holding it separate?" Berzon also said "we're an appellate court." Plaintiffs argued a carve-out would create orphan stations.
- No ruling and no signal on timing. Deadline's account of the hearing was paywalled and Courthouse News returned a 403. My account rests on the Deadline text surfaced in search results and on RBR, whose own piece gave no read on how the judges leaned.
- The stock closed down 1.7% today, so some of the hearing may already be priced in. I can't confirm that.

**Regulatory**
- The FCC voted 2-1 on Aug 6 to repeal the 39% cap, replacing it with case-by-case review. Nexstar rose 8.8% when the chairman announced the vote and about 3% on the vote day. Sinclair rose about 13% that day.
- The Q3 call says the rules take effect 60 days after Federal Register publication, which had not yet happened. Sook said challenges are likely after publication. The call summary dated the repeal Oct 1, which conflicts with the Aug 6 vote date, possibly a later written order.
- The D.C. Circuit dismissed the challenges to the Media Bureau approval on July 9 as premature. The FCC said it expects to act on the application for review by year end, which is a tail risk that a full Commission vote could reverse the order.
- Sook also hopes for action on local ownership rules before year end.

**Q3 results (Nov 5)**
- Revenue was $2.13B, up 78% and above the $2.07B consensus. Adjusted EBITDA was $756M (35.4% margin). Adjusted free cash flow was $443M. Political revenue was a $317M third-quarter record.
- EPS of $7.92 missed the $8.08 consensus.
- Combined nonpolitical advertising fell 5%. Combined distribution rose 2.1%.
- Q4 nonpolitical advertising is guided down high single digits from political crowd-out. There is no 2027 guidance, and the World Cup boost will not recur.
- Total debt is $11.4B, with net leverage of 4.04x. Another $525M was repaid after quarter end. There were no buybacks, and buybacks wait until leverage nears 3x.
- The CW expects its first profitable quarter in Q4. The dividend is $1.86 a quarter, which is a small yield on a $205 stock.

**Analysts and price**
- After earnings, Wells Fargo went to $250 (overweight), Citi to $225 from $215 (buy), and Deutsche Bank to $240 (buy). MarketBeat shows an average target near $257 and a "Moderate Buy" consensus. Several of those figures come from aggregator pages that are inconsistent with each other.
- Aggregators show the stock near $190 on Nov 6, $201 on Nov 9 and $210 on Nov 10. That fits the 20-day high of $210.87 and a stock that has since drifted sideways.

**Watch-outs for a 1 to 10 session hold**
- A Ninth Circuit ruling could land any day. A narrowing would likely be read as a positive, since it would free about 22 non-overlap Tegna stations to integrate. An outright affirmance would likely hit the stock. The panel's skepticism leans toward affirmance, though that is my inference.
- Nexstar says nothing is wrong with the overlap-market carve-out being narrow, so even a partial win is plausible.
- A settlement announcement is possible but undated.
- I did not confirm the Q4 ex-dividend date. Prior years went ex in mid-November, so one could fall in the window, but I could not verify it. Check with the data source.
- I did not find short interest or any news from today specifically.

agents.report:
**IFF research for the 1–10 session decision, as of Tuesday 2026-11-17, 7:45 PM CT**

**Summary:** The drop is a post-earnings repricing of a run-up. It is not a broken thesis, and I found no news from the last few days that explains the latest leg down. The slide started right after earnings: the stock closed at 92.18 on Nov 3 and is now 79.43, about 14% lower. The Q3 numbers beat, but management warned Q4 margins would soften and 2027 costs would rise. BofA then downgraded the stock to Underperform. Some of my searches hit inconsistent or unreliable pages, noted below.

**Price path (from the pages I found)**
- The stock rallied through 2026. It hit 52-week highs of 89.32 on Oct 14 and 92.04 on Oct 22, and a high of 95.27 on Nov 2.
- Earnings came Nov 3 after the close. The stock fell about 3.8% after hours, from 92.18 to 88.65, and was about 87.9 the next day. Barchart-style sources put the close at 82.62 on Nov 6, 84.43 on Nov 9, about 80.9 on Nov 12 and 79.99 on Nov 16.
- The drop continued on Nov 16 and 17 without any news I could find.

**Q3 results (company 8-K, Nov 3)**
- Sales were $1.94B, up 4% reported and 5% currency-neutral. Adjusted EPS was $0.83 against $0.81 expected. Adjusted operating EBITDA was $403M (20.8% margin).
- By segment:
  - Taste: sales $687M, up 4%, margin 18.6%.
  - Scent: sales $689M, up 6%, margin 20.2%, with EBITDA up 10% currency-neutral.
  - Health & Biosciences (H&B): sales $566M, up only 1%, margin 24.0%.
- The GAAP loss was $(0.50) per share, driven mostly by non-cash items:
  - a $236M loss on assets held for sale;
  - a $23M goodwill impairment on the Botanicals & Food Enhancements unit;
  - $34M of regulatory costs tied to the fragrance investigations.
- Nine-month free cash flow was $371M, up $245M. Net debt was $5.8B, or 2.75x credit-adjusted EBITDA.
- Full-year 2026 guidance had its low end raised. Sales are now $7.5–7.6B, adjusted EBITDA is $1.55–1.60B, currency-neutral sales growth is 3–4%, and EBITDA growth is 5–8%.
- That guidance implies a soft Q4. Management gave no numeric Q4 figure, though a transcript summary reports about 3% sales growth.

**What spooked the market (Nov 4 call)**
- **Q4 profitability:** The CFO said it would soften, mainly in H&B. He gave three reasons:
  - weak, higher-margin health volumes, because US and European supplement demand is "very soft" (CEO Erik Fyrwald);
  - unfavorable price-versus-cost from logistics, energy and oil-derivative inputs;
  - temporary R&D and commercial reinvestment.
- **2027 costs:** Raw-material inflation is expected at about 3% in early 2027. The price-cost gap is expected to be widest in Q1 2027 and then narrow, as pricing talks run through December.
- **No destocking:** Management said it sees no material customer destocking. It attributed the Q4 slowdown to a harder year-ago comparison.
- **Medium-term growth:** Management said 4–6% growth for Scent and Taste looks achievable.

**Analysts**
- **BofA, Nov 6:** Cut to Underperform from Buy, with the target lowered to $91 from $95. The reasons were a rally with no near-term catalyst, weakness outside Taste, and about 3% raw-material inflation limiting operating leverage into the first half of 2027.
- **Targets raised or held after earnings:**
  - Mizuho raised its target to $102 from $92.
  - Citi raised its target to $105 from $100, with a Buy.
  - UBS raised its target to $95 from $91, with a Neutral.
  - Barclays trimmed its target to $103 from $105 and kept Overweight.
- **Consensus:** MarketBeat shows "Moderate Buy" with an average target of about $95. That is roughly 20% above the current price.
- **Earlier in 2026:** Vertical Research cut IFF to Hold with a $93 target in August. Oppenheimer's $95 target and KeyBanc's Sector Weight at $95 are also on record.

**Peers**
- Symrise fell as much as 12% on Oct 28, its worst day since 2008, after flagging slower year-end growth and margin pressure.
- Givaudan's Q3 organic growth was 8.6% and its shares rose 9.4%. dsm-firmenich also guided to about 3% input inflation for 2027.
- I found no sector-wide selloff in November.

**Portfolio and capital allocation**
- **Food Ingredients sale:** It goes to funds advised by CVC at an enterprise value of about $4.3B, roughly 10x EBITDA. IFF keeps about a 10% stake and expects about $3.8B of net cash.
  - Closing is expected by the end of Q2 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.
  - Management warned of about $100M in stranded costs, with two-thirds to be eliminated within 12 months of closing.
  - The deal is expected to dilute adjusted EPS for the first 12 months.
  - Management named execution capacity as the key risk.
- **Buyback:** The $500M accelerated repurchase is complete, about 5.8M shares or roughly 2.3% of the shares outstanding. The remaining authorization will not be used until after the sale closes, with completion expected by the end of 2027. So there is no buyback support in the stock near term.
- **Debt:** About $1.5B is short-term debt, and management plans to repay it with sale proceeds.

**Legal overhang (risk for the next 1–10 sessions)**
- The European Commission fined IFF €15.9M for obstructing a fragrance-cartel inspection after an employee deleted messages. The underlying EU cartel probe is still open, as are the UK CMA and Swiss probes. India's competition authority has a case that names IFF, Givaudan and dsm-firmenich.
- IFF is reportedly seeking leniency.
- The US Department of Justice reportedly closed its probe of IFF in February 2026. One July article conflicts with that, and I could not resolve it.
- IFF agreed to an $11M US private-suit settlement, with a fairness hearing set for Sept 15, 2026. I did not confirm the outcome.
- I found no formal statement of objections. A surprise formal EU or CMA action is a possible gap-risk event, with no known date.

**Next scheduled events**
- Next earnings are 2027-02-10, outside the 10-session window. I found no scheduled company event inside the window.
- I did not confirm the dividend ex-date.

**Reading for the decision**
- **For a bounce:** The business results beat, guidance edged up, and sell-side targets are well above the price. The stock sits near its 200-day average (78.78) after a sharp RSI-32 slide, and the buyback is done but the sale proceeds are coming.
- **Against a bounce:**
  - The narrative has turned to margins. Q4 is guided soft, and the price-cost gap peaks in Q1 2027.
  - H&B demand is weak.
  - BofA's downgrade and Symrise's October warning make margin worries sector-wide.
  - There is no company catalyst until after the window.
  - The legal overhang is open-ended.
- **Technical note:** A close below the 200-day average would be a notable break.

**Source caveats**
- MarketBeat, GuruFocus and Weiss returned 403 errors or only search snippets.
- The transcript summaries contain transcription errors, including conflicting closing-date wording for the sale.
- Several search summaries had odd details that I did not rely on, such as a claim of a 12% semiconductor-index drop on the downgrade day.
- I could not find any explanation for Nov 16–17 trading.
