agents.report:
# Nike (NKE): research summary for the 2026-11-17 close

## Why it fell today
Nike held the second day of its Investor Day, which it branded "Full Stride Ahead", and the stock sold off on the plan. A day earlier it had closed at about $38.59. It was up about 6% pre-market and as high as $40.68 in the morning. It then reversed through the day to close at $35.85, down 6.3% ([Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/17/nike-stock-just-plunged-despite-the-company-s-new-turnaround-plan-then-plunged-here-s-what-spooked-investors/), [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stock-market-today-nov-17-221909071.html)). Yahoo reports volume of 61.1M shares against a three-month average of 33.1M.

Sources disagree on the close. Most say $35.85, but AlphaStreet says $36.25, down 5.3%. I went with $35.85 because it matches your screen.

The Yahoo piece puts the S&P 500 down 1.0%, Adidas down 1.6% and lululemon down 1.3% that day. So the market and peers were weak, but Nike fell much more than they did.

## What management said
- **2031 targets:**
  - About $5B of added revenue, of which roughly $4B is from performance sports.
  - Operating margin of 12-14%, against about 6% this year.
  - Adjusted EPS of $3.00-3.50, against $1.15-1.35 this year.
  - About $12B of dividends over fiscal 2027-2031.
  - The Pace cost program is now cited at about $2.5B of annual savings, with about $1.3B of charges.
- **The near-term problem:**
  - Fiscal 2027 and 2028 are an "investment period." Revenue declines "moderate" next year, and growth returns only in fiscal 2029, at the pace of the market.
  - Fiscal 2028 "will be a challenging year financially." Adjusted EPS is guided to decline modestly from fiscal 2027's $1.15-1.35 ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/nike-sinks-7-investor-day-204224374.html)).
  - Before the event, the pre-event estimate for fiscal 2028 was about $1.53, which should now come down.
  - Product costs are rising, and Nike says it has limited ability to pass them on through price.
- **Greater China:** TradingKey says Greater China sales stay flat from fiscal 2027 to 2031. TradingKey is a weak source, so I would not rely on that figure ([TradingKey](https://www.tradingkey.com/news/market-movers/262309676-market-movers-nke-20261117)).
- **Fiscal 2027 guidance** was reiterated, not cut.
- **Analyst reaction:** The only direct one I found is RBC, which said the targets "leave little room for near-term upside surprises" ([AskTraders](https://www.asktraders.com/analysis/nike-stock-falls-6-3-after-investor-day/)).

## Background (fiscal Q1 2027, reported Oct 1)
Official release: [Nike](https://about.nike.com/newsroom/releases/nike-inc-reports-fiscal-2027-first-quarter-results).
- Revenue was $11.2B, down 4%. EPS was $0.48 against about $0.43 expected.
- Gross margin was 42.8%, up 60 basis points. Management credited lower logistics costs and currency, partly offset by more discounting.
- Greater China was $1.18B, down 26% on a currency-neutral basis, with a digital-channel cleanup under way.
- North America was up 2% and EMEA down 5%. Sportswear fell by a low double-digit rate, Jordan by a mid-teens rate, and Dunk sales were cut nearly 50%.
- Fiscal 2027 guidance: revenue down by a high-single-digit percentage, adjusted EPS of $1.15-1.35 (consensus was about $1.61), and EBIT falling faster than revenue.
- The stock fell sharply after the print and hit its 52-week low of $31.97 on Oct 2, according to a search snippet.

## How the stock got here
- It is down roughly 40% or more year to date and about 78-80% below its November 2021 closing high of $161.97.
- Bank of America downgraded to Underperform on Sept 25, with a target of $30, later $24. It cited a "longer-than-expected turnaround" and cut its fiscal 2027 EPS estimate 14% below consensus ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/nke-stock-slips-premarket-bofa-123222943.html)).
- Ratings after Q1, per [MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-nike-nyse-nke-shares-down-24-following-analyst-downgrade-2026-11-06/) (these have no stated dates, apart from the Oct 2 moves listed there):

| Firm | Rating | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Truist | Sell | $29 |
| Citigroup | Neutral | $32 |
| UBS | Neutral | $34 |
| Baird | Neutral | $36 |
| RBC | Sector Perform | $39 |
| Bernstein | Outperform | $45 |

- Berenberg downgraded to Sell with a $27.50 target, per a search snippet. I could not confirm the date.
- The MarketBeat consensus is 1 Strong Buy, 7 Buy, 20 Hold and 12 Sell, with an average target of $40.91.
- A TIKR preview on Nov 10 put the Street's average target near $36, below the then-current price.
- A rebound of about 20% off the low had run into the event:
  - On Nov 4 the stock rose roughly 5-7% on a broad consumer and market rally, with no Nike-specific news.
  - One headline mentions a 13% jump around Nov 15.
  - So part of today's drop is likely the unwinding of an event run-up. That is my inference, not something a source states.
- Two executives sold shares on Sept 9 at $37.59, under 10b5-1 plans. They are small and routine.

## Valuation and competitors
- At about $36 the stock is roughly 30x this year's EPS guidance midpoint. On the $3.25 midpoint of the 2031 target it is about 11x.
- Dividends are about $2.4B this year, roughly a 4% yield on a market value of nearly $55B.
- On Holding grew 17.8% in constant currency in Q3, with a record 66.9% gross margin. Hoka grew 6.8%. Foot Locker's comparable sales fell 3.6%, and Dick's cut its Foot Locker outlook.

## What I could not find
- After-hours coverage: no source mentions it. Your 35.22 print is not reflected anywhere I found, and there was no after-hours analyst reaction.
- Analyst reactions to the Investor Day itself: only RBC. Target cuts almost certainly follow tomorrow, but I have no evidence yet.
- No specific news about Nike's Nov 11 "signal" or why Berenberg downgraded when it did.
- The Q1 call's tariff and Converse details, and the Nike Direct and digital breakdown of the Investor Day.
- Several search snippets had inconsistent dates and figures, and I flagged them where they mattered.

## Read for the 1-10 session window
- **Bearish:**
  - The drop was driven by a long-term plan that pushes revenue growth out to fiscal 2029, with fiscal 2028 EPS guided down.
  - Analysts are skeptical, and estimate and target cuts probably come tomorrow.
  - The reversal from $40.68 to $35.85 on heavy volume is a classic failed rally.
  - The stock closed below its 20-day low, with the 50-day below the 200-day.
- **Bullish:**
  - The 52-week low of $31.97 is about 11% below the close.
  - Fiscal 2027 guidance was not cut.
  - There is a roughly 4% dividend yield and the $12B payout plan.
  - There are no scheduled catalysts before the Dec 17 earnings, so short-term flow will decide it.
- **Bottom line:** The story is a credible long-term plan with a deliberately delayed payoff. That tends to produce analyst downgrades and target cuts over the next few sessions. It also tends to produce a bounce once the selling is done, but nothing found says that bounce is due yet.

agents.report:
**NVDA research for 2026-11-17, written at about 7:55 PM CT.** The earnings were a clear beat and the stock is bouncing after hours. The open risks are governance, the SEC and export probes, and a large web of guarantees and commitments. Some sources conflict, and I could not open a few of them.

**What happened to the stock (Oct to Nov)**
- It closed at a record $239.24 on Oct 6.
- It fell about 24-25% in November, with six straight weekly losses and over $1T of market value lost.
- It touched $148.80 on Nov 12, the 52-week low, then bounced to about $162-166.
- It closed at $156.14 on Nov 16, with the Nasdaq down 2.49%.
- Before the report it was at roughly 11-12x forward earnings, the lowest since 2012. Its 14-day RSI was about 22.7.
- Several sources agree on the levels above. Exact dates vary a little between outlets.

**The shock was governance, not demand**
- Nov 8: the board opened an independent probe into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Nov 10: it hired outside counsel (Joon Kim; Wachtell Lipton is also named).
- Nov 12: Huang resigned as CEO, president and director over "personal behavior inconsistent with the code of conduct."
  - Colette Kress is interim CEO and remains CFO. Harvey Jones is board chair.
  - CNBC reports the conduct involved the former head of Megaspeed, a Singapore partner suspected of helping divert chips to China. US intelligence reportedly suspects her of being a Chinese spy. Treat this as press reporting.
  - The board says it has no reason to believe national security or proprietary secrets were compromised, but the probe is ongoing.
- Tonight the board said it does not intend to reinstate Huang and has hired Heidrick & Struggles for a permanent CEO search with no timetable. It also formed a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee.
- Huang says he is open to returning if the board finds it in shareholders' interest and admits "serious mistakes."
- Huang and the general counsel agreed to House committee interviews, with Huang reportedly set for Dec 1.
- More than 10 analysts moved from Buy to Hold. More than 20 cut targets, including Mizuho to $220 from $250, citing 6-7 months of management overhang.

**The earnings print (Q3 FY27, quarter ended Oct 25; SEC 8-K)**

| Item | Result | Consensus |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $115.8B, +103% y/y, +20% q/q | about $109.1B |
| Data Center revenue | $107.6B | about $101.9B |
| Edge Computing revenue | $8.2B | about $7.5B |
| Non-GAAP EPS | $2.68 | about $2.47-2.48 |
| Non-GAAP gross margin | 74.9% | about 74% |

- Free cash flow was $43.8B. Buybacks and dividends came to $28.1B, with about $227B left on the buyback authorization.
- Q4 guidance is revenue of $130B plus or minus 3% (the quarter has an extra week) against about $125B expected.
  - Gross margin is guided to 71-72%. Kress said Q4 "marks the bottom" for margins, and management attributes the dip to the Rubin ramp.
  - Guidance assumes zero China data center compute revenue.
- FY28 revenue growth is now about 75%, up from 70%. This was said on the call and is not formal guidance.
  - TECHi calculates that it needs roughly 17.9% sequential growth per quarter, against about 4.2% guided. This is the outlet's own math.
- Kress reports a cloud industry backlog of $2.5T, up from $2T three months earlier. She said "Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start."
- Nvidia will stop shipping licensed Hopper chips to China. Those were about $2.4B this quarter.

**The bear points inside the print**
- Inventory is $39.7B, up from $21.4B in January.
- Supply and capacity commitments are large, and the sources do not agree on the totals.
  - CNBC cites $92B for the rest of FY27, $87B for FY28 and $88B for the year after.
  - Investing.com cites $390B, up from $279B, mostly multi-year memory.
- Lease and cloud commitments rose to $102B from $74B.
- Nvidia reports $118B of guarantees tied to an OpenAI Ohio data center, with maximum exposure of $105B and no payments made. Another $32B of neocloud commitments are conditional on financing.
- Yahoo's live page reported unpaid bills of $81B, or 64 days of sales, and guarantees of other companies' obligations of $118B.
- Four direct customers made up 47% of sales, against 11-13% each before. Frontier labs such as OpenAI and Anthropic are about 15% of data center sales.
- Nvidia plans to buy Hugging Face for just under $13B.
- Kress said Nvidia will be "disciplined and selective" on support. That is a concession that the circular financing worries are fair.

**Regulatory and legal overhang**
- The WSJ reports a civil SEC probe into whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors, including its 2025 removal of the Singapore sales breakdown.
- Treasury Secretary Bessent is reportedly demanding answers within 10 days. California's attorney general says his office is looking into it.
- A Commerce interim rule from Monday requires licenses for advanced-chip exports to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, and targets compute rented to China-headquartered customers. China has threatened countermeasures.
- Nvidia reportedly warned customers of legal exposure over Chinese access to capacity (CNBC sources via Newsquawk).
- The 10-Q is due by Dec 4 and must describe legal proceedings. Ives says the leadership question stays open and flags a possible activist or special meeting. I found no reporting on an activist.

**After-hours reaction and options**
- Shares first dipped, then rose. Reports range from about 2.3% to 3%, 3-4%, 4.5% and "as much as 5%." Your 7:00 PM CT print of +4.8% is at the top of that range.
- Neocloud and peer stocks rose too: CoreWeave +7.7-10%, Nebius up to +9.9%, AMD +1-3.5%, TSMC +2%.
- Options priced an 8.5% move (about $139.55 to $165.47 from $152.51). The median move over the last eight quarters was 3.2%. The reaction so far is inside the implied range.
- Analysts: 26 Buy, 12 Hold, 1 Sell, with an average target of about $232 (range $200-250). Wedbush's Ives keeps $225 and calls the guidance the "most important line."

**Levels from one source (tradingnews.com)**
- Support is $149.09, then the $148.80 low. A daily close below $149.09 would target $134.61.
- Resistance is $156.14, then $163.20 and $164-168 (the $166.05 close on Nov 12). A close above $171.03 would signal a trend change.

**For the 1-10 session decision**
- The bull case: a large beat and raise, a margin "bottom," a 12x forward P/E, a washed-out RSI, and a short-covering and relief bounce already under way.
- The bear case: the SEC probe, export rule, House hearing on Dec 1, CEO search and 10-Q are all still ahead. Customer concentration and the guarantee web are scrutiny risks. The bounce could fade into the $163-168 supply zone.
- Timing: the Dec 1 hearing and the Dec 4 10-Q fall inside or just beyond a 10-session window. The WSJ's Nov 17 SEC-probe report and the Bessent deadline (about Nov 27 if it runs from Nov 17) are also near-term.
- Gaps: I could not open Benzinga (403), so its headline is the only thing I used from it. I have no call transcript, so the call details come second-hand through CNBC, Yahoo and TECHi. I found no reliable closing after-hours print or tomorrow's pre-market data.

**McCormick (MKC), research for the 1–10 session decision, as of 7:55 PM CT on 2026-11-17**

I found no news item that explains today's 5.1% drop. No company release, analyst action or filing that I could find is dated November 17 with a negative message. The one McCormick release that day is a dividend increase, and it is mildly positive. So the move looks like continued deal-related selling plus a weak packaged-food backdrop. That is my inference, not something a source says.

**The story: the Unilever Foods deal drives the stock**
- **Terms:** The deal was announced March 31, 2026, as a Reverse Morris Trust. Unilever Foods combines with McCormick.
  - Unilever and its shareholders get 65% of the combined equity, and McCormick holders keep about 35%.
  - Unilever also receives $15.7B in cash. Total value is about $44.8B for the Foods business, or about $65B for the combined company.
  - Closing is expected by mid-2027. McCormick shareholders must vote on it. Unilever shareholders do not.
- **Reception:** The stock fell hard on the announcement. Shareholder-minority and dilution critiques are common, and the Seeking Alpha pieces I saw say the deal was not what shareholders wanted. Management says it is accretive in year 1 and targets about $600M of synergies by year 3. Net leverage at close is expected at 4.0x or less, with a goal of about 3x within two years.
- **Unilever side:** Unilever's own shares fell, Terry Smith sold his whole stake, and employee bodies have objected.
- **Vote status:** I found no Form S-4, meeting date or proxy-adviser view. The latest SEC items I saw (June) say the S-4 was still to be filed.

**Near-term catalyst: UK Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) deadline on Nov 18 (tomorrow)**
- On Nov 11 the CMA found a realistic prospect of substantially lessened competition in UK dry ingredient mixes and dry sauces. McCormick (Schwartz) and Unilever (Colman's, Knorr) are the two largest branded suppliers in both.
- It found no concern in mustard.
- The parties have until Nov 18 to offer remedies (undertakings in lieu), or the deal goes to a Phase 2 in-depth probe.
- Unilever has been marketing Colman's for sale since August and says buyer talks are "progressing well." One report says a Colman's sale may not fix the dry-mix issue directly.
- Both companies called this an expected step and say they are confident of closing on time.
- McCormick fell 1.4% to 2.4% on Nov 11.
- I found no report of what was filed. An adequate remedy would remove an overhang. A Phase 2 reference would likely push the closing timeline out and be negative.

**Fundamentals**
- **Q3 (reported Oct 1):**
  - Adjusted EPS was $0.86 against $0.85 a year earlier, and consensus was about $0.76.
  - Net sales rose 17.4%, but organic growth was only 1.9%. Most of the growth came from the McCormick de Mexico acquisition.
  - Volumes were soft with quick-service restaurant and packaged-goods customers.
  - Management reaffirmed fiscal 2026 guidance, including adjusted EPS of $3.05–$3.13.
- **Costs and tariffs:** Cost inflation guidance rose to 6–7%. Gross margin is guided up about 120 bps, partly from IEEPA tariff refunds (about 35 bps). Management assumes a global 10% tariff.
- **Analysts:** UBS, Barclays, Stifel and TD Cowen cut targets to $47–48 on Oct 2, all at Hold or equal-weight or neutral. Bernstein kept Outperform at $59. Consensus is roughly Hold, with targets around $53–56.
- **Dividend:** On Nov 17 the board raised the quarterly dividend to $0.51 from $0.48, payable Jan 11, with a Dec 28 record date. This is the 41st straight annual increase. At the $44.73 close the yield is about 4.6%.
- **Price action:** The stock was grinding down all October on small declines of 1–3%, from about $46–47 to $44.6 on Oct 13 and back to $46.37 by Oct 21. It was $46–47 until today's drop to a close of $44.73.

**Sector backdrop:** Center-store packaged food has been under pressure all year. Campbell's cut its dividend in September, General Mills cut guidance, and Bernstein downgraded the group. I found no specific sector selloff on Nov 17.

**Facts to weigh**
- Tomorrow's CMA outcome is a binary event inside the 1–10 session window.
- The next earnings date is 2027-01-21, outside the window.
- The dividend record date of Dec 28 is also outside the window.
- Today's low-volume (1.7x) after-hours trade at $44.96 (+0.5%) says little.

agents.report:
**AES is a merger-arbitrage stock, not a momentum setup. Treat it that way.**

**The story**
- On March 2, 2026, AES agreed to a take-private for $15.00 per share in cash. The buyers are a consortium led by BlackRock's Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) and EQT Infrastructure VI, with CalPERS and the Qatar Investment Authority as co-underwriters.
- Equity value is about $10.7B and enterprise value about $33.4B including debt. The consortium is funding the price entirely with equity, so there is no financing risk.
- The $15 price was a 40.3% premium to the 30-day volume-weighted average price before July 8, 2025.
- Stockholders approved the deal on June 26, 2026.
- The Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS), the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio (PUCO, approved Sept 17) and certain foreign agencies have also approved.
- Today, Nov 17, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) issued its final order. AES calls it the last suspensory regulatory approval.
- AES says closing is expected on or about December 2, 2026, subject to remaining closing conditions. It adds that there is no assurance of that timeline. The outside date is June 1, 2027, with possible extensions.
- At close, AES leaves the NYSE.

**What it means for the screen's signals**
- The close of 14.97 is only 0.03 (0.2%) below the $15.00 payout. The 20-day high breakout, RSI 70, 2.1x volume and 0.07 correlation to SPY are all artifacts of a deal-pinned price. The volume spike fits the FERC news and arbitrage buying.
- The price is capped near $15.00. A quiet ATR of about 0.05 is exactly what a pinned stock looks like.
- Upside over 1 to 10 sessions is at most about 0.03 per share, about 0.2%, before costs. The January 2026 52-week high of 17.03 is irrelevant.
- Downside is a deal break. That would likely send the stock sharply lower, probably back toward the pre-deal range. I did not find that range. One unreliable source quoted $14.71 in June.
- The market is pricing a very high probability that the deal closes on time. Annualized, 0.2% over about 11 trading days is only a few percent.
- There is no earnings catalyst. Q3 results were already reported in early November, and sources conflict on the exact date.
- The last dividend of $0.17595 was payable Nov 13. With a Dec 2 close, I would not expect another, but I did not confirm that.

**Risks that remain, all small**
- **Rehearing:** Ohio's consumer advocate (OCC) filed a motion for rehearing of the PUCO order, and AES Ohio responded Oct 29. AES says the PUCO order stays operative.
- **Political opposition:** Sen. Warren and several House members asked FERC on Sept 28 to reject the deal. They cited GIP's data-center holdings. FERC approved it anyway. I did not check for a FERC rehearing request or court appeal.
- **Shareholder suits:** Two complaints sought more disclosure. Kaskela Law is investigating whether $15 undervalues the stock. Neither appears to threaten closing.
- **Indiana:** I did not find an explicit Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission (IURC) approval. AES says all other required approvals were received.
- **Remaining conditions:** The remaining closing conditions are not listed in the press release.

**Limits of this research**
- Several sources conflict on deal value ($10.7B equity versus $33.4B enterprise value, and $46.1B from J.P. Morgan on a consolidated basis). They also differ on the Q3 earnings date.
- I could not open the GuruFocus article (HTTP 403).
- I did not read the primary SEC filings in full: the merger agreement, the proxy, or the 10-Q. I only saw the 8-K exhibit for today's announcement.
- The final-approval announcement did not state the price. That comes from earlier releases and secondary sources.

**Verdict for the journal:** No directional trade. A long on the technicals risks a deal-break gap for roughly 0.2% of upside. If the book treats it as merger arbitrage, the expected return is a few cents with a small tail risk, and it should be sized on that basis. AES should probably be excluded from momentum screening until it delists around Dec 2.

agents.report:
**Bottom line:** I found no company-specific news for today. The only same-day explanation is positioning ahead of tomorrow's Dish Wireless bankruptcy mediation update (Wednesday Nov 18, time not found), which is a binary event for the group. I could not find XLRE's move or Treasury yields for Nov 17, so I can't tell how much of the drop is a rates or REIT move. I found no report of what happens on Nov 18. The sources below are mostly trade press, and some are AI-generated.

**Why the group fell today**
- A Nov 17 market recap says SBAC and Crown Castle fell "before Wednesday's mediation deadline in the Dish Wireless bankruptcy, where tower claims exceed $7 billion." It gives no price moves and doesn't mention AMT ([Rock and Turner](https://rockandturner.substack.com/p/tue-nov-17-2026-the-market-today)).
- A Nov 17 24/7 Wall St. piece on tower REITs and data demand turned up in the search, and I did not open it ([24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/17/3-cell-tower-reits-positioned-to-profit-as-wireless-data-demand-quadruples/)).
- The ordering fits the Dish story but isn't confirmed. SBAC (-6.5%) is the worst and AMT (-4.0%) the best. Crown Castle's move wasn't given.

**The Dish bankruptcy**
- **Background:** EchoStar sold spectrum to AT&T (about $23B) and SpaceX (about $19.6B), over $40B in all. Dish Wireless got none of the proceeds. On Jan 12, 2026 it sent lease termination notices, arguing the sales "frustrated the principal purpose" of the leases ([Wireless Estimator](https://wirelessestimator.com/articles/2026/tower-company-executives-urge-fcc-chairman-carr-to-require-escrow-funds-to-cover-dishs-infrastructure-debts/), [Broadband Breakfast](https://broadbandbreakfast.com/dish-bankruptcy-mediation-extended-two-weeks/)).
- **Filing:** Dish Wireless, Dish DBS and 16 affiliates filed prepackaged Chapter 11 on June 30 in the Southern District of Texas before Judge Lopez ([Wireless Estimator](https://wirelessestimator.com/articles/2026/dish-wirelesss-bankruptcy-exit-slides-to-december-as-tower-companies-press-their-7-6-billion-claim/)).
- **Claims:** The towers claim $7B or more (one source says $7.6B). Dish says it should pay a small fraction or nothing, and it has asked the court to disallow the claims or cap them at 15% ([Broadband Breakfast](https://broadbandbreakfast.com/dish-wants-tower-claims-zeroed-out/)).
- **Funding pool:** A July 30 FCC order requires EchoStar to set aside $2.4B for roughly 170 tower and infrastructure creditors suing Dish. The $8.8B owed to Dish DBS debtholders competes with the towers for any recovery.
- **Past rulings:** Dish DBS is a related subsidiary in the same filing, and its claims could let debtholders approve the plan over tower objections. On July 10 the judge sided with the towers on discovery.
- **Timeline:** The case has been paused since Sept 14. A two-week standstill was announced Sept 14, then mediation began in October. On Nov 4 the judge extended mediation to Nov 18 and said he would treat it as closed unless he approves more time. He told the parties to "put their cards on the table" ([Inside Towers](https://insidetowers.com/dish-and-towercos-pause-litigation-to-work-towards-a-settlement/)).
- **Plan confirmation:** The confirmation hearing was set for Nov 12 or Dec 2 depending on how the tower claims are handled. I could not confirm which applies now.
- **Tower side:** American Tower called Dish's reversal a bad-faith "bait and switch." The towers also ask the court to unwind Dish's transfer of Boost Mobile to EchoStar before the filing. The towers are pressing $7B+ against the Dish plan's offer of a share of the $2.4B trust, and the next step (settlement, extended mediation, or litigation) is unknown.
- **Industry cost:** The Wireless Infrastructure Association cites a Brattle estimate that Dish rent is about $500M a year across all tower companies, and that a default could lift industry lease rent by up to 10.7%.

**Exposure and fundamentals by company**
- **AMT (Q3 on Oct 27):** AFFO per share was $2.87, a beat. The 2026 AFFO guide was narrowed to $11.04–$11.16, and a further $2B buyback was authorized. All Dish revenue is already counted as churn since Jan 1. Organic billings grew 1.1%, or about 4% excluding Dish. Net leverage is 4.9x ([Zacks](https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/3016141/amt-q3-affo-revenues-rise-on-steady-demand-2026-outlook-raised)). AMT also has its own suit against Dish in federal court in Colorado.
- **CCI (Q3 on Oct 21):** AFFO was $1.24 per share, up 11%. The fiber and small-cell sale closed in May at about $8.4B, and more than $7B of debt was repaid. Organic growth excluding Dish was 3.8%. The 2026 midpoints were raised, partly through a $275M customer deal that extends leases and limits long-term churn. Reporting says Crown Castle is seeking the full $3.5B it says Dish owes, and CCI is the most US-concentrated of the three ([Panabee](https://www.panabee.com/news/crown-castle-earnings-q4-2026)).
- **SBAC (Q3 on Nov 2):** The 2026 AFFO guide is $12.15–$12.37 per share, narrowed from $11.95–$12.40. The cut to site leasing revenue and EBITDA came from FX and the Chile/Ecuador sale. EchoStar churn was $14M in the quarter, with full-year figures of $56M or $36M depending on the source. Sprint churn was $16M. US new leasing billings drifted from about $10M to about $8M a quarter. A commercial paper program of up to $2.5B was set up in late September ([Finviz](https://finviz.com/news/413834/sba-communications-matches-the-whisper-as-buybacks-and-refinancing-lift-affo-while-us-leasing-keeps-slipping)).

**SpaceX angle, the offsetting upside**
- On Oct 22, Bloomberg reported SpaceX was in talks to put radios on up to 80,000 US towers. AMT rose about 6.8%, CCI about 10% and SBAC about 5.5% that Friday ([Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/10/62273164/spacex-could-become-a-massive-new-customer-for-cell-tower-giants-stocks-surge)).
- On Nov 4, CCI gained about 6% after SpaceX picked Qualcomm base stations. No lease has been signed. The Crown Castle CEO said the company is "talking to all parties."
- Analysts doubt the scale: BNP Paribas called it a possible bluff and New Street said it points to an MVNO instead. The towers called the SpaceX-Dish link unfounded.
- One BNP analyst's cleanest bridge is for SpaceX to take on the tower commitments, and one analyst said it could buy Dish's roughly 24,000 stranded radios. That would be the bullish resolution.

**Rates context**
- SBAC fell 4.2% on Oct 21 with no company news. An AI-generated summary attributes it to rising long yields and financing concerns ([Quiver Quant](https://www.quiverquant.com/news/SBA+Communications+Falls+as+Rate+Pressure+and+Financing+Focus+Weigh+on+Tower+REITs)).
- SBAC also fell 4.6% on June 15 with no news, tied to the DISH DBS missed-interest headline ([Quiver Quant](https://www.quiverquant.com/news/SBA+Communications+(SBAC)+slides+as+tower+stocks+face+renewed+carrier-credit+concerns)).
- Targets are stale: the median is about $235–245 (Goldman $205, KeyBanc $250), and SBAC sat near $185 on Nov 17.

**For the one-to-ten-session view**
- **Catalyst:** The Nov 18 update lands inside the window. A settlement, a spillover into plan confirmation, or the judge ending mediation could each move the group sharply.
- **Pricing:** The fundamentals, Dish churn included, already look priced into guidance. Most of what is left is the size and timing of the claim recovery, plus SpaceX headline risk in both directions.
- **Rates:** If part of today's drop was rates or XLRE, that component is separate from Dish.
- **Move size:** The group has swung 5–10% on both SpaceX and Dish headlines in recent weeks, so wide moves either way are normal here.
- **Open question:** Whether a bad Dish outcome is already priced after the -3.7% over 5 sessions against XLRE can't be answered from the sources I found.

agents.report:
**Verdict: TSN is a post-earnings drift candidate, but at this price I'd call it a hold or a small, tight-risk long at most, not a high-conviction take.** The stock has already repriced the beef-recovery story. I found no news explaining today's +1.8% after-hours move.

**What happened on Nov 16 (fiscal Q4, quarter ended Oct 3)**
- **EPS:** Adjusted EPS was $0.61, down 47% from a year earlier. Full-year adjusted EPS was $3.44, against $4.12 the year before.
- **Beat or miss:** Sources disagree on the consensus, so treat the surprise as roughly zero. MarketBeat has $0.53, Yahoo-syndicated coverage has $0.58, AlphaStreet and others have $0.60, and Zacks and Investing.com called it a miss. The Investing.com figure of $0.754 looks like an outlier.
- **Sales:** Sales were $14.59B against about $14.1B expected, helped by a 53rd week.
- **GAAP:** GAAP was a loss of $0.22 per share, with $260M of restructuring charges and $124M of legal accruals.
- **Why it rallied:** The consensus-relevant content was in FY27 guidance, which pointed to a much smaller beef loss.
  - Sales are guided down 3.5% to 5.5%.
  - Adjusted operating income is guided to $1.7B to $2.15B, against about $1.98B in FY26.
  - Free cash flow is guided to $0.8B to $1.3B, with capex of $1.1B to $1.4B.

**FY27 segment guide (operating income)**

| Segment | FY27 guide | FY26 comparison |
|---|---|---|
| Beef | -$300M to +$100M | -$654M adjusted |
| Chicken | $1.3B to $1.6B | $1.86B |
| Prepared Foods | $1.25B to $1.4B | n/a |
| Pork | $75M to $175M | n/a |
| International | $125M to $200M | n/a |

At the midpoints, the chicken decline of about $400M offsets most of the roughly $550M beef improvement. Prepared Foods guidance was roughly flat, which analysts questioned on the call. Pork is guided below consensus, per Bernstein.

**The story**
- **Beef is the problem:** It has lost money since 2023, more than $2.3B in total. Tight cattle supply, a roughly 7-year herd decline, and a Mexican border closure over screwworm are the drivers.
  - Only about 50,000 head had crossed from Mexico through Oct 23, against a pre-closure norm of about 1.2M a year.
  - Management says heifer retention is up about 3%, and the herd was 94.2M head at July 1, slightly up from a year earlier.
- **Restructuring:**
  - Lexington, Nebraska closed in January (about 3,200 jobs).
  - Joslin, Illinois closed in August (about 2,500 jobs).
  - The Eagle Mountain, Utah case-ready plant closed.
  - Pasco, Washington is for sale, and guidance could change if it sells.
  - Beef will run on three plants: Dakota City, Holcomb and Amarillo.
  - Amarillo gets a second shift back by summer 2027, tied to a cattle-supply partnership with Allied Beef Company announced Nov 9. A definitive agreement is expected "in the coming weeks", which is a possible near-term headline.
- **Chicken is fading from a high base:** Q4 margin was 8.7%, against 12.7% a year earlier, and industry cutout values were down about 25%. Pilgrim's reported an adjusted EBITDA margin of 6.8%, against 13.3% a year earlier, and cited a significant supply increase. Grain costs are higher.
- **New CEO:** Jeff Schomburger took over Oct 4, replacing the 43-year veteran Donnie King. He is a former P&G executive and Tyson board member since 2016. He is pushing marketing, innovation and KPIs.
- **Guidance revision:** Tyson cut its FY26 beef guidance on Sept 3 and announced the beef network restructuring on Aug 13. Those were bad-news events that were cleared before this print. That helps explain why the bar was low.
- **Capital returns:** FY26 buybacks were $427M, with another $93M in early FY27. The dividend rose 2% to $0.52 a quarter, the 15th straight annual raise, for a yield of about 3.3%. Net debt to adjusted EBITDA is 2.1x, and liquidity is $4.1B.
- **Legal overhang:**
  - Beef and pork antitrust settlements of $47M and $48M got final approval.
  - Beef consumer settlements totaled $87.5M with Cargill.
  - The beef accrual was $267M at March 28, and the pork accrual was $83M at June 27.
  - Tyson also disclosed DOJ civil investigative demands on its beef business.
  - Further accruals are a risk.
- **Sector tape:** Cattle futures rebounded in mid-November, and packer margins swing between negative and positive from day to day. JBS's North American beef margin improved from -2.9% in July to 3.9% in September.

**Analysts (Nov 17)**
- **Raised targets:**
  - BMO went to $75 from $65, Outperform.
  - Piper Sandler went to $72 from $56, Overweight.
  - Bernstein went to $72 from $66, Market Perform.
  - Goldman went to $70 from $62, Buy. I could not date this one.
- **JPMorgan downgrade:** JPMorgan cut to Neutral from Overweight on valuation, with the target at $65 from $63. MarketBeat and Investing.com agree on this, though one search suggested otherwise. JPMorgan had upgraded in September.
- **Consensus:** It is Hold, with an average target of about $69.10, which is only about 8% above the price. Other firms:
  - Barclays has Overweight at $75.
  - HSBC has Hold at $69.
  - Zacks has Strong Sell.
- **Valuation:** TIKR put the forward P/E at about 17x on the pre-jump close, against a 5-year average of 16x. It says the beef recovery is priced in and that consensus FY27 EPS of $3.84 is too high given the guidance.

**Setup for the 1 to 10 session trade**
- **For the long:**
  - Post-earnings drift with bad news bought on 2.2x volume.
  - A wave of target raises.
  - Buybacks and a dividend floor.
  - Possible Allied Beef and Pasco headlines.
  - Beef spreads improving.
- **Against the long:**
  - The stock is extended, with RSI 75 and 2.8 ATR above its 20-day average. It is up 14.9% in 20 sessions and about 16% above its 50-day average of $54.63. That puts it in a spot where pullbacks are common.
  - Consensus targets are barely above the price, and JPMorgan downgraded.
  - Guidance has no real growth. Chicken is in decline, and Prepared Foods is flat.
  - FY27 EPS consensus likely needs to come down.
- **Levels:** Today's close was 63.65 and the 20-day high is 65.34. After-hours 64.78 (a trade in only 9 bars, so thin) is just under that high. The 52-week high of 68.26 is the next upside reference.
- **Catalysts in the window:** The Allied definitive agreement, a Pasco sale, cattle and cutout prices, and Mexican border and screwworm news. There are no earnings until Feb 8.
- **Unknown:** I did not find the ex-dividend date. The last ex-date is probably early December, but I didn't verify it.

**Source quality:** The facts above come from Tyson's releases and call transcript plus trade press. The EPS consensus and some analyst dates conflict across secondary sources. I did not open the Q4 8-K directly, and several Investing.com and MarketBeat figures are auto-generated and inconsistent.

**Dolby (DLB): research brief, 8:00 PM CT Tue 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line:** The earnings-day drop was the first-quarter guide, not the quarter. Dolby beat on EPS and reported roughly in-line revenue. The Q1 FY27 guide is far below the one consensus figure I found, and the FY27 outlook is flat. The stock fell 3.8% into the print and is down another 4–5% after hours. The market is pricing a stalled growth story under a brand-new CEO. A bounce is plausible, but nothing I found gives a catalyst inside 1–10 sessions.

**The quarter (Q4 FY26, per the 8-K press release)**
- Revenue was $373.5M, up 22% from $307.0M. Licensing was $346.8M and products/services $26.7M.
- Non-GAAP EPS was $1.25 versus about $1.19–1.21 consensus. GAAP EPS was $0.86.
- Revenue consensus was about $372.8M. One outlet calls $373.5M an in-line result against a $376.5M consensus, so "beat or in line" depends on the source.
- Licensing included a negative $6M true-up because prior-quarter shipments came in below estimates.
- Q4 "Other" licensing (video distribution patents plus automotive) was $103.0M versus $60.1M a year ago. That is a big part of the beat.
- Broadcast was $120.9M (+13%) and mobile $61.5M (+22%). Consumer electronics was $32.0M (down from $35.0M) and PC $29.4M (up slightly).
- FY26 revenue was $1.421B (+5%) and non-GAAP EPS $4.36 (+3%). Non-GAAP operating margin was 34.5%.
- Buybacks were $265M in FY26 (4.3M shares), with about $362M left on the authorization. Cash and investments were about $713M and there is no debt.
- Declared dividend is $0.39, payable Dec 9 to holders of record Dec 1, so the ex-date is close to that record date.

**The guidance (this is what hit the stock)**
- **Q1 FY27:** Revenue is $285–305M, licensing $260–280M, and non-GAAP EPS $0.41–0.56. Q1 FY26 revenue was $347M, so the midpoint is about 15% lower year on year.
- **Consensus gap:** Investing.com cites a Q1 revenue consensus of about $359M and EPS of about $1.12. Those figures look high against the year-ago $347M, so treat the exact gap with some caution. The direction is clearly a big miss.
- **Management's reasons:** Deals are expected later in the year, Q1 FY26 had a positive true-up, and unit shipments are lower. Q1 non-GAAP opex of $200–210M rises sharply from Q4 on tax benefits and the timing of litigation and patent-program costs.
- **FY27:** Revenue is about $1.42B (flat) and licensing about $1.32B. Non-GAAP EPS is $4.27–4.42, operating margin about 34.5%, and the share count is held at 94.0M. Investing.com says the full-year figures match consensus.
- **By line:**
  - Foundational audio falls mid-single digits.
  - Atmos, Vision and imaging patents grow mid-single digits, after +18% in FY26 that was helped by large one-time recoveries.
  - Mobile is flat, and PC and consumer electronics fall mid-single digits.
  - Broadcast falls high-single digits on lower recoveries and units.
  - Other (video distribution patents plus automotive) grows mid-teens.
- **Memory pricing and supply:** Customers are shipping fewer low-end devices and raising high-end prices, which hurts units. Mobile deals are mostly minimum-volume commitments, and renewals in 2027 may carry lower expected volumes.
- **Growth targets:** On the call, the CEO would not commit to a return to double-digit growth.

**The story and catalysts**
- **New CEO:** Marc Whitten, formerly of Meta robotics, Cruise, Unity, Amazon, Sonos and Microsoft, succeeded Kevin Yeaman in late August 2026. Yeaman had run the company since 2009, and the stock fell about 3.9% on that news. This was Whitten's first call, and his four priorities were culture, simpler operations (including AI productivity), AI-era leadership and durable growth.
- **A first-year reset:** Flat guidance and tempered expectations from a new CEO are a common pattern. Nothing I found shows that is happening here, but it fits.
- **Video distribution patent program:** It has 47 licensors, up from about 6 a year ago, including Meta and Alibaba. Management is "pretty confident" streaming technologies will exceed 10% of revenue by FY28 but declined to forecast it.
- **Litigation:** Dolby sued Snap in March 2026 (US and Brazil) over AV1 and HEVC, and is in a patent fight with InterDigital. The Supreme Court denied Dolby's petition in the Unified Patents standing dispute on June 22. Litigation came up on the call only as a Q1 expense item, and tariffs were not discussed.
- **Dolby Vision 2:** TCL, Hisense and TPV have announced support, and Peacock, Canal+ and iQIYI have committed content.
- **Upcoming event:** A financial community event at CES on Jan 7, 2027 at 7:30 AM PT, outside the 1–10 session window. It may serve as a reset catalyst.

**Price context**
- **Rally off the lows:** After Q3 (reported Jul 30) the stock jumped about 12% intraday from $51.78, on guidance above estimates and a $350M increase to the buyback authorization.
- **Slide into the print:** It was $64.59 on Nov 12 and $61.16 on the pre-earnings preview page, then closed at $58.82.
- **After hours:** Sources put it at $55.77–56, down 4.8–5.5%. Your 7:00 PM CT print of $56.60 is consistent with that. One source reports only a 3.1% decline, so the after-hours move is unsettled.
- **Why the 5.9x volume:** I found no news dated Nov 13–16 explaining the slide, so volume was most likely pre-earnings positioning.
- **Analysts:** Before the print, three of four rated it Buy and one Hold, with a mean target of about $77. Rosenblatt had Buy with an $85 target (dated about six days earlier). I found no post-earnings target changes yet, and Nov 18 notes may bring cuts.
- **Valuation:** A GuruFocus note puts GF Value at $84.79, but it is a mechanical model and not informative here. At about $56, FY27 non-GAAP EPS of about $4.35 gives roughly 13x earnings. The stock also has a floor of buybacks and a dividend yield near 2.8%.

**Read for a 1–10 session trade**
- **Bearish case:** There is a Q1 guide shock, a flat FY27, a first-year CEO and unit pressure from memory prices. The stock is already below its 50-day and 200-day averages, and analysts' target cuts typically land the next morning.
- **Bullish case:** The stock is cheap, with a 34.5% margin, no debt, steady buybacks, the beat on EPS and an FY27 outlook that matched consensus. That makes a partial retrace of a guide-driven drop plausible. The 52-week low of 47.98 is far below.
- **Open question:** The size of the after-hours drop is disputed (3.1% to 5.5%), so check the pre-market on Nov 18.

**Gaps:** I could not open the ChartMill and GuruFocus pages (403 errors), and I didn't find a full Q&A transcript. I found no post-print analyst actions or any unusual news in the week before earnings.

# Costco (COST) research as of 8:00 PM CT, Tue 2026-11-17

The stock is extended and the rally has a clear cause, but a $30 ex-dividend drop falls inside the 1-10 session window. I found no catalyst between now and the Dec 2 sales report or the Dec 10 earnings. I stopped when new searches only repeated the same facts.

## The story

**Operating momentum is real.**
- **Q4 FY26** (16 weeks to Aug 30; [Costco release](https://investor.costco.com/news/news-details/2026/Costco-Wholesale-Corporation-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2026-Operating-Results/default.aspx)):
  - EPS was $6.75 vs $5.87.
  - That includes $0.15 of one-time IEEPA tariff-refund benefit. Excluding it, EPS grew 12.4%.
  - Net sales rose 11.2% to $93.9B.
  - Comps were +9.4%, or +6.7% excluding gas and FX.
- **Membership** ([call summary](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/09/29/costco-cost-q4-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)):
  - Paid members were 84.1M, up 3.8%.
  - Executive members were 42.3M, up 9.4%.
  - The US/Canada renewal rate was 92.3%.
  - Member growth has slowed for 8 straight quarters, which management calls "normalization".
  - Q4 was the last quarter to benefit from the Sept 2024 fee increase.
- **Reinvestment and costs:**
  - Management plans to reinvest most of the tariff refunds in lower member prices. Another refund of similar size arrived in Q1 FY27.
  - The LIFO charge jumped to $152M from $43M.
  - FY27 capex is planned at about $7.5B, with 33 openings.
- **October sales** ([Costco PDF](https://s201.q4cdn.com/287523651/files/doc_news/Costco-Wholesale-Corporation-Reports-October-Sales-Results-2026.pdf), [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/costco-reports-october-net-sales-of-245-billion-up-126-93CH-5001328)):
  - Net sales were $24.5B, up 12.6%.
  - Comps were +11.1% reported and +7.3% excluding gas and FX (US +8.1%).
  - Digitally enabled sales were up 22.5%.
  - September comps were 11.4%.
  - The November sales report is due Dec 2, per [Quartr](https://quartr.com/companies/costco-wholesale-corporation_4772).

**The recent leg up came from a special dividend and a sales read.**
- On Nov 10 Costco declared a $30 special dividend, about $13.3B (see the [SEC 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000909832/000090983226000134/costex9918-k111026.htm) and [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/cost-stock-rises-overnight-costco-015955513.html)).
  - Record date is Nov 24 and payment is Dec 4.
  - It is a record, double the $15 paid in Dec 2023, and about 2.8% of the stock price.
  - Mizuho had expected $18-20.
  - A new $4B buyback runs through Nov 2030.
  - Cash was $20.2B at fiscal year-end.
- The stock closed at $1,066.14 on Nov 10 and is now $1,110, up about 4% since.
- On Nov 16 Mizuho raised its target to $1,150 from $1,100 but removed COST from its Top Pick list because the stock is up about 30% YTD ([Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/mizuho-raises-costco-stock-price-target-to-1150-on-strong-sales-93CH-5031048)).
  - It said strong sales acceleration seems to be holding into mid-November, possibly above 10% US comps.
  - It cited one-time lifts: emergency-preparedness buying and pantry-loading. 21 of 26 online generators were sold out.
  - It also called the dividend possibly the last special one.
- JPMorgan raised its target to $1,150 from $1,015. Bernstein raised to $1,155 from $1,143 ([TradingView/Stocktwits](https://www.tradingview.com/news/stocktwits:c51be382d094b:0-cost-stock-draws-street-attention-after-30-cash-dividend-mizuho-highlights-significantly-higher-payout-bernstein-eyes-q4-trends/)).

**Valuation is the main bear point.**
- The forward P/E is about 47.8 vs a 12-month median of about 44 and an industry average near 30 ([Zacks via Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/costco-hits-52-week-high-151000309.html)).
- An Investing.com piece published Nov 17 put the trailing P/E at about 53x. It is a promotional article, so treat that figure with caution ([Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/safe-haven-or-bubble-walmart-and-costco-now-trade-at-45x53x-pe-5029122)).
- Consensus targets cluster around $1,073-1,120, which is at or below the current price.
  - Koyfin shows 25 of 41 analysts at Buy, 14 at Hold and 2 at Sell.
  - Another tally shows 21 Buy, 8 Hold and 1 Sell.
- Downgrades to Hold on valuation:
  - North Coast on Nov 16, per a [GuruFocus headline](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9202263/costco-cost-stock-rating-downgraded-to-neutral). I could not open the article.
  - Freedom Broker, with a $1,050 target, as reported in the Mizuho article.
  - Truist reiterated Hold.

## Macro backdrop
- The market is volatile and cross-currents are strong ([AJC/AP](https://www.ajc.com/news/2026/11/us-stocks-slip-following-a-discouraging-update-on-inflation/)).
  - The S&P 500 had its worst day since April 2025 on Nov 5, driven by an AI sell-off.
  - On Nov 10, hot inflation raised the odds of a December Fed rate hike. The 10-year yield was 4.99%.
- Staples have drawn a safe-haven bid from rotation out of AI and Big Tech.
  - That is a risk if money rotates back into growth.
  - COST is up about 12% in 20 sessions, so this fits what our screen saw.
- I could not find an account of why today's S&P fell 1.0% or of COST's intraday action.
- Retail earnings this week: Home Depot (Nov 17), Target (Nov 18), Walmart (Nov 19) and Lowe's (Nov 18), per [Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/weekly-us-earnings-estimates-16-20th-november-2026-ai-leader-nvda-the-highlight-with-retailers-also-in-focus).
  - I found no Home Depot result for today.
  - Walmart is a sentiment read-through for COST. Its previous report was followed by an 8.9% drop. Q3 guidance is EPS $0.62-0.64.

## Trade-relevant points for the 1-10 session window
1. **The ex-dividend drop likely lands inside the window.**
   - Under Nasdaq Rule 11140, the ex-date is expected to be Nov 24, the record date, but Costco's release did not name one ([StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/costco-30-special-dividend-2026-record-date)). Nasdaq had not listed it when that article was written.
   - The last day to buy and still get the dividend is probably Nov 23.
   - The stock should open about $30 (about 2.7%) lower mechanically on Nov 24.
   - That is about 5 sessions out, with Thanksgiving closing the market Nov 26.
   - A long held through Nov 24 loses about $30 unless the dividend is included in the scoring. A short would gain it mechanically, but shorts owe the dividend to the lender.
   - Check whether the journal scores on adjusted or raw prices.
2. **Dividend-capture demand is a known tailwind into Nov 23.** Some of the post-announcement run-up may be that demand, and it ends when the ex-date passes.
3. **There is a catalyst gap before the window ends.**
   - The Nov sales report (Dec 2) and Q1 earnings (Dec 10 after the close) are both after a 10-session window ends about Dec 2.
   - The sales report could land on the edge of the window.
   - Consensus for Q1 is about $4.87-5.03 EPS on about $74-75.7B revenue. Those are snippets from different aggregators and are not verified.
4. **The setup is stretched.** The price is at the top of a 12% 20-day run, the stock sits roughly 14% above its 50- and 200-day averages, and sentiment is bullish. Street targets are about at the price. The turn today came on a down tape for the market, with the stock closing weak in the day's range.
5. **Positive offsets:** Costco's sales comps are accelerating, retail and institutional sentiment is bullish, and a staples safe-haven bid is in place. Dips in COST have historically been shallow. I did not verify that against price history.

## Caveats on sources
- A [Yahoo article](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/cost-stock-rises-overnight-costco-015955513.html) says COST is "down about 45% YTD". That contradicts every other source, which put it up 25-30%, so I treated it as a typo.
- The sidebar of the Investing.com valuation page mentioned an NVIDIA Nov 18 earnings reaction that postdates the article. I treated it as unreliable and did not use it.
- [Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/11/63195200/costco-stock-rises-near-52-week-high-whats-going-on) and GuruFocus blocked fetches (HTTP 403), so I used search summaries for those.
- I found no news explaining today's weakness. There is no company-specific negative, so the dip looks like market beta plus profit-taking.

**Atlassian (TEAM): research for the 1-10 session decision, written after the 11/17 close**

**Bottom line.** The 36% fall in 20 sessions has two causes. The first is company-specific: the fiscal Q1 2027 guide on Nov 5 implied a sharp growth slowdown after a huge run. The second is a sector-wide "AI agents kill per-seat software" selloff, which hit again today. The business itself reported strong numbers, and I found no sign of operational damage. The setup looks like a sentiment-driven oversold stock whose near-term path is tied to software and Anthropic-IPO flows. The one hard, dated catalyst before the next earnings report is the Dec 3 start of usage-based pricing.

**How the price got here**
- The stock bottomed near $56 in April 2026 after a roughly 69% drawdown from its 2024 peak. The cause was fear that AI agents would erode seat-based products like Jira and Confluence ([TIKR](https://www.tikr.com/blog/atlassian-is-up-70-in-a-month-is-it-too-late-to-buy)).
- The fiscal Q4 report on Aug 6 produced a 30-35% one-day pop. Cloud revenue accelerated to 31%, and CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes announced plans to buy up to $250M of stock ([TIKR](https://www.tikr.com/blog/atlassian-is-up-70-in-a-month-is-it-too-late-to-buy)).
- The stock ran to about $228-230 in October. One source puts the multiple at roughly 32x forward earnings in August, before the further run.
- The fiscal Q1 report (Nov 5, after the close) beat on every line.
  - Revenue was $1.772B, up 24%, versus a company guide of $1.705-1.715B.
  - Cloud revenue was $1.302B, up 31%, versus a guide of about 28.5%.
  - Non-GAAP EPS was $1.65 versus about $1.43-1.45 expected.
  - Free cash flow was $463M and remaining performance obligations were $4.7B, up 44% ([OptionsPilot](https://optionspilot.app/blog/atlassian-team-fiscal-q1-2027-earnings-revenue-beat-cloud-31-percent-q2-cloud-guide-27-percent-after-hours-drop-team-options-nov-5-2026), [call summary](https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262289206-)).
- The guide is what the market sold.
  - Q2 cloud growth is guided to about 27%, a deceleration of roughly four points.
  - Full-year revenue growth is about 13.75%, and subscription ARR growth about 18.5%.
  - The full-year raise was smaller than the Q1 beat. Management called this "prudent" and cited tougher second-half comparisons, the DX acquisition lapping, and Data Center revenue timing ([Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/atlassian-shares-fall-16-cautious-110846490.html)).
- The stock fell about 14-17% on Nov 6. That was at or above the roughly 14.5% implied move, and the drop continued afterward. One source has it down about 22% over the week to Nov 11 ([Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/software/nasdaq-team/atlassian/news/atlassian-team-falls-after-results-as-cautious-guidance-test)).

**Today (Nov 17, down 6%)**
- No Atlassian-specific news turned up. One recap says "no confirmed company-specific catalyst" ([JKN](https://news.jkn.co.kr/editions/english/post/1102774)). That recap has the wrong weekday and a $142.45 close against your $140.98, so I would not rely on its detail.
- Software broke down as a group. IGV fell more than 3%.

**Cisco (CSCO) as a one-to-ten-session trade, 8:05 PM CT, Tue 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line:** The fundamentals were strong. The selloff looks mostly like multiple compression plus sector and Nvidia-linked selling, not an earnings miss. A bounce is plausible, but the stock has no catalyst of its own until February, and Nvidia's earnings (reported after today's close) are unresolved in my sources. Lean neutral to a small, tactical long at most.

**What happened on the print (reported Nov 12 after the close)**
- Revenue was $18.5B, up 24% year over year, against about $18.1B expected. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.40 against $1.33. Sources call it the fastest growth in about 15 years.
- Full-year FY27 guidance was raised to revenue of $74.8–75.8B (about 19% growth) and EPS of $5.47–5.53.
- The FY27 hyperscaler AI revenue target was raised to $9B from $7.5B.
- Q2 guide: revenue $18.0–18.2B, EPS $1.34–1.36, gross margin 65–66%. Q2 revenue is below Q1's $18.5B, which feeds the "growth peaked" argument.
- Total product orders rose 21% year over year, down from 35% in Q4. Ex-hyperscaler orders rose 14%.
- Campus orders rose 14%, and management says only about 9% of switching sales come from the new portfolio so far.
- Margins were the weak spot. Gross margin was 65.6%, down 250 basis points, and product margin was 63.7%, down 350 basis points. Management blamed hardware mix and memory costs. It signed a new multiyear memory deal and is raising prices.
- Optics is the main supply constraint, and management expects it to ease next quarter.
- Remaining performance obligations were $46.2B (up 8%). Annual recurring revenue was $32.7B (up 4%).
- Cisco returned $3.7B in Q1, about 95% of free cash flow. $6.1B remains under the buyback authorization.

**Why it fell**
- **Sequential orders:** Management gave no sequential figure. Analyst David Vogt's math implied a dip in hyperscaler AI orders, and Trefis also reports a slight sequential dip. Management called it "lumpy."
- **Guide shape:** The CFO flagged tougher second-half comparisons and less visibility. Analysts noted that Wells Fargo called slowing product order growth the key investor focus.
- **Analyst reactions on Nov 13:** Citi said growth "peaked in the October quarter" and cut its target to $120 from $139 (Buy). Barclays cut to $109 from $123 (Equal Weight), saying margins held up better than feared. Wells Fargo cut to $130 from $150 (Overweight). **HALO: research summary as of Tuesday 2026-11-17, 8:00 PM CT**

**Bottom line:** The drop is explained and not a mystery. Fundamentals are strong. The selloff is a rerating on the Merck Keytruda subcutaneous (SC) patent fight and on two downgrades. A string of US patent rulings against Halozyme could keep arriving over the next 1 to 10 sessions. I found no sign of a stock-specific reversal catalyst in that window.

**What the company is**
- Halozyme earns royalties on its ENHANZE drug-delivery technology. ENHANZE lets partners turn IV drugs into under-the-skin injections (examples: Ocrevus Zunovo, Opdivo Qvantig, Rybrevant Faspro, argenx's Vyvgart).
- It also sells products and is building Hypercon and Aerocon. Hypercon is a concentrated-formulation technology with first clinical starts guided for the first half of 2027. Aerocon targets clinical entry in the second half of 2028.

**Q3 2026 results (Nov 5)**
- Revenue was $493M, up 39%. Royalties were $341M, up 44%. Operating income was $295M and net income $247M. Q3 beat consensus modestly.
- 2026 guidance was raised: revenue $1.860–1.925B, royalties $1.235–1.255B (42–45% growth), adjusted EBITDA $1.24–1.29B, non-GAAP EPS $8.75–9.05.
- Buybacks total $400M this year. A $1.5B convertible note offering was completed. Cash is $1.08B, long-term debt $3.3B, net leverage 2.4x.
- Halozyme will give 2027 guidance and a long-range outlook with Q4 results in February 2027. There are no scheduled company earnings in your window.

**Why the stock fell**
- The stock peaked around $134 (Oct 29 high by Trefis; the $134.00 matches your 52-week high).
- Nov 6: Leerink cut it to Market Perform from Outperform. The target rose to $117 from $110.
  - Leerink cited limited near-term upside and constrained Keytruda Qlex royalty optionality.
  - The close was $103.63, and one source reports a drop of more than 13% that day.
- Nov 11: Morgan Stanley cut it to Equal Weight with a $109 target. It cited valuation after a 53% year-to-date run and royalty rate step-downs.
- Other analysts stayed bullish:
  - Citizens JMP: $149
  - TD Cowen: $130
  - H.C. Wainwright: $130
  - Wells Fargo: $110, equal weight
  - JPMorgan: $79, neutral
- Consensus targets are roughly $100–115 depending on the source, so today's $95.97 sits below most of them.
- Insider selling: CEO Helen Torley sold 60,000 shares (about $6.6M) on Oct 6. That is before the drop and she still holds about 768K shares.

**The Merck patent dispute, the core of the story**
- Halozyme sued Merck in D.N.J. in April 2025, alleging Keytruda Qlex infringes 15 patents on its MDASE technology (a separate patent family from ENHANZE).
- Europe is going Halozyme's way.
  - Munich granted a preliminary injunction in Germany in December 2025.
  - The Hague rejected a preliminary injunction for Denmark and Sweden in July 2026.
  - On Oct 7, the Hague court found infringement of EP622, rejected Merck's invalidity attacks, and barred Merck's European distributor from making or selling Keytruda SC in 8 countries. Those are Belgium, Denmark, France, Ireland, Italy, Sweden, Switzerland and the Netherlands.
  - Management says Europe is about 20% of global royalties.
  - Merck's Italian contract manufacturer (BSP) is affected regardless of destination, so US supply is a question. Management would not comment on it.
  - Halozyme also sued BSP directly and filed for an Italian preliminary injunction in September.
- The US is going Merck's way.
  - Merck filed 15 post-grant reviews (PGRs) and 3 inter partes reviews (IPRs) at the patent office (PTAB), starting in November 2024.
  - Nine final written decisions found challenged claims unpatentable for lack of written description and enablement. They were not found obvious.
    - '600: May 12
    - '262: May 18
    - '298: Jun 8
    - '035: Jun 24
    - '520: Sep 1
    - '652 and '185: Sep 25
    - '345: Oct 1
    - '692: Oct 2
  - Institution of one challenge ('685) was denied on May 15.
  - Three IPRs were instituted Sep 9.
  - Halozyme has appealed at least four of the earlier decisions (Federal Circuit case numbers 26-2299, -2300, -2302, -2303). Management expects the appeals to run until 2028 and says it is very confident it will prevail.
  - A source from May listed 12 instituted PGRs still awaiting decisions. About 5 have been decided since, which leaves roughly 7 outstanding.
  - Statutory deadlines on the remaining PGRs ('590, '758, '618, '791, '773) fall mostly by mid-to-late November 2026. This is my inference from the Oct–Nov 2025 institution dates, and the dates should be checked on the PTAB docket. More adverse decisions, possibly this week, are likely given the 9-for-9 pattern, and some may already be priced in.
  - I found no trial date or stay for the New Jersey case.
- Other legal dates:
  - A UK trial on the '347 patent begins Nov 30, 2026. Halozyme consented to revocation of the UK '622 patent in May.
  - Management says there have been no settlement talks with Merck. The Dutch win fueled settlement hopes in October, and those hopes have faded.
- Keytruda Qlex had about $40M in 2025 sales. Management did not disclose how much Qlex royalty is in guidance. Newer deals have royalty rates that drop modestly if patents are invalid.

**Valuation and history**
- The stock trades at about 13x trailing operating cash flow and 24x trailing earnings. The trailing operating margin is about 56%.
- It was still up about 43% year to date on Nov 11, per Trefis.
- Trefis says HALO has had 21 falls of more than 20% in about six weeks since 2010. In 16 of 20, it was higher a year later. Median changes were +7% after 21 trading days and +13% after 63. The median worst drawdown inside the following year was about 13%, and the worst fall ended down 42%.
- A March 23, 2026 drop of 22.6% is mentioned, but I did not find its cause.

**Gaps**
- I could not open the Leerink or Morgan Stanley notes (403 errors), so their details come from summaries.
- I found no news dated Nov 12–17 and no explanation for the further slide to $95.97. Your screen's 22.8% 20-day drop is consistent with the decline from the peak.
- I could not confirm whether Merck has appealed the Dutch ruling.
- I did not check the Merck 10-Q's litigation note directly. It was too large to read through the fetch tool.
- I did not look at short interest, options positioning, or intraday data.

**F5 (FFIV) research, as of 8:05 PM CT, 2026-11-17**

**Short version:** F5's decline is a growth-reset repricing, not a broken business. The stock was down about 30% in two weeks, and an AI-trade market crash and a security-sector sell-off appear to have added to the post-earnings drop. I found no news since early November that would reverse the decline or make it worse. Your 0.2% bounce on 0.6x volume looks like a pause in selling, not a confirmed bottom.

**What happened**
- **Before earnings:** The stock had run up nearly 80% in 2026. It closed at $459.36 on Oct 27, near its 52-week high, so expectations were high.
- **Oct 27 results (after the close):** Both revenue and EPS beat estimates by a wide margin.
  - Revenue was $917M, up 13%, against about $884M expected.
  - Non-GAAP EPS was $4.42, against $4.26 expected.
  - Product revenue rose 23%. Systems (hardware) rose 29% to $239M on an aging-equipment refresh. Software growth re-accelerated to 19%.
  - Direct AI bookings topped $100M, up about 300%. F5 sees an AI market of about $11B by 2030.
  - The board authorized $1.5B more in buybacks, for $1.8B of total capacity. F5 bought back $100M in the quarter at an average of $422.
- **Oct 28 reaction:** The stock fell about 20%, its worst day in more than ten years. The cause was the fiscal 2027 outlook, not the quarter.
  - Revenue growth is guided to 8-9%, down from 11%. EPS is guided to $18.00-$18.30, only about 3-5% growth.
  - Q1 revenue guidance of $875-895M is below the Q4 run rate.
  - Management expects the hardware refresh to fade in the second half of fiscal 2027.
  - Gross margin is guided down to 80.5-82.5%, from about 84%, because of higher memory component costs.
  - F5 is spending more to double its AI security sales team, and building inventory and prepaying suppliers to secure supply. Fourth-quarter free cash flow was only $91M.
- **Analysts:**
  - Piper Sandler downgraded to Neutral, with a $461 target. It cited the winding-down iSeries refresh, possible peak product growth and a lack of near-term catalysts.
  - Needham said the refresh "appears to be waning." William Blair said AI has "yet to contribute meaningfully to the top line."
  - RBC (Outperform, $540) and Evercore ISI (Outperform, $500, per Investing.com) were still bullish. Barclays stayed at Equal Weight.
  - Consensus before the drop was Hold, with an average target of about $439. That is well above the current price, though targets will likely drift lower.
- **Why it kept falling from about $365 to about $305 (my read):**
  - Fortinet fell about 25% after hours on Oct 28 on slowing product revenue and refresh-cycle durability worries, which hit the whole firewall and hardware-refresh group.
  - In the week to Nov 6, Palo Alto and CrowdStrike fell about 14%, Zscaler 17% and Fortinet 12%.
  - The S&P 500 fell 4.4% on Nov 5, its worst day since April 2025, in an AI-stock rout. It then had its worst week since April 2025 in the week ending Nov 11.
  - The five-day streak through Nov 2 totaled about -29.7%, a loss of about $7.8B in market value. Trefis noted this was far larger than the S&P's move.
  - I found no F5-specific news after Oct 28, so the continued slide looks like momentum plus sector and market pressure.
- **Insiders:** The CEO sold 3,383 shares on Nov 5 at $310-$323. Only 40 shares of that were under a pre-set trading plan. The article's dollar figures don't reconcile, so treat the size as approximate. Earlier CTO sales in Aug and Sept were under 10b5-1 plans.

**What a trade would be betting on**
- **Bull case:**
  - The business is strong. Product revenue has grown at double digits for nine straight quarters, and the quarter was a clear beat.
  - Estimated EPS is about $18, so $305 is about 17x forward earnings. That is cheap against the 29x trailing P/E before the drop.
  - There is $1.8B of buyback capacity against a market cap of about $18B.
  - The stock is oversold, with RSI in the low 20s for about two weeks. Tickeron cites a 66% historical chance of gains in the following month, but that is its own promotional estimate, not independent data.
- **Bear case:**
  - Growth is slowing to 8-9% and the hardware tailwind is ending.
  - Margins are shrinking because of memory costs, which the whole hardware group faces, and F5 is raising spending.
  - The stock is below both its 50-day and 200-day averages, and Tickeron's MACD and Aroon signals are bearish.
  - The sector and the AI-trade market are still weak. Today's S&P drop of 1.0% means the market is still under pressure.

The after-hours bounce looks like a Nvidia-earnings relief move on a risk-on tape. The first inflow day came yesterday, but it is thin. Near-term catalysts are lopsided toward event risk on both sides.

**How we got here**
- **Long bear market.** BTC peaked near $126,000 on 2025-10-06. It lost its 200-day average in late October 2025 and is now about 49% below the high. It fell to about $57,700 on 2026-07-01, the 21-month low. That fits your 52-week IBIT low of 32.84.
- **Range and recovery.** BTC recovered to roughly $77,000–$85,000. Charles Schwab's Jim Ferraioli says $85,000 has capped rallies all year.
- **Binance hack (Oct 29–30).** About $6.3B was stolen, the largest crypto theft on record. The FBI attributed it to North Korea, which denied it. BTC fell below $77,000. Binance says it has restored about 95% of affected assets, and Grayscale calls the damage a temporary confidence hit.
- **Nov 5 AI/chip rout.** The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5% and the Nasdaq-100 fell 6.4%, its worst day since 2020. Reports tie it to fears that the midterm results would slow AI data-center buildout. Chip stocks led the drop. BTC rolled over with them.
- **Hot October CPI (about Nov 10).** Core rose 0.3% and services excluding housing rose 0.5%. Fed Governor Waller had said a 0.3% core print would put a half-point hike on the table. CME-based odds of a 25 basis point hike at the Dec 8–9 meeting are about 85% (sources range from 85% to 89%). Odds of a 50 basis point hike are about 10–12%. The 10-year yield is near 5%.
- **Fed tone.** St. Louis Fed President Musalem says several hikes are likely before spring 2027. Robin Brooks says real rates are at a 20-year high.
- **Weekend flush.** BTC hit about $62,000 on Nov 14–15, with more than $1B in liquidations on each of Friday and Saturday. Another $1.6B of crypto positions were reported liquidated on Tuesday, 82% of them longs. The Fear & Greed index was 10 on Monday. Ferraioli says liquidations and falling open interest are at levels seen near past bottoms.

**IBIT flows (Farside/TFTC data)**
- **November:** IBIT lost about $2.12B through Nov 13, roughly 90% of the ETF group's $2.35B outflow. The daily figures are all negative, from -$78M to -$405M.
- **Streaks:** IBIT had 11 straight outflow sessions. The group had 7 straight, about -$1.91B in total. The week of Nov 9–13 was the biggest weekly outflow since late June.
- **First inflow:** On Mon Nov 16, IBIT took in +$76.5M, its first inflow since Oct 29. The group total was only +$7.9M, with GBTC -$34.6M and FBTC -$11.3M. That recovers about 3% of the outflow, and analysts say one day is not a trend. Nov 16 was also the 13F filing deadline.

Nothing forces it to sell bitcoin, but its buying power is impaired.

- **Cost basis:** Estimates of the ETF holders' average cost range from $60,000 to $90,000, so I would not lean on any of them. Short-term holders are underwater (Glassnode short-term holder cost basis about $75,700).

agents.report:
**Dynatrace (DT): research as of 8:10 PM CT, Tuesday 2026-11-17**

**Bottom line:** The 32% drop has one clear cause. The fiscal Q2 report on Nov 3 cut profit and cash flow guidance and showed flat net new ARR (new annual recurring revenue added in the quarter). Since then the stock has stalled around 43, on no new company news and a weak software sector. The thesis for a bounce is timing-driven and has to wait for Q4. The nearest hard evidence of a turn is the next earnings report on 2027-02-08. I could not find the intraday price path for Nov 9–17, so the "no turn yet" read comes from your screen, not from a source.

**What happened**
- **The trigger.** Q2 fiscal 2027 was reported Nov 3. Revenue was $580M (+17%), above the $568M estimate. Non-GAAP operating margin was 32% and non-GAAP EPS was $0.54. ARR was $2.207B (+16%). The stock still fell about 15% that day (premarket indications of 15–16%). Sources: [Yahoo/UK release](https://uk.finance.yahoo.com/news/dynatrace-reports-second-quarter-fiscal-113000212.html), [Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4664019-dynatrace-falls-15-on-trimmed-earnings-guidance), [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/dynatrace-shares-tumble-16-on-disappointing-guidance-outlook-93CH-4994579).
- **The miss.** Net new ARR was $70M, flat year over year. Net revenue retention (NRR) slipped to 109%. Management put the shortfall at "high single-digit millions," tied to "just a handful" of large enterprise consolidation deals that slid into the second half. They said the deals "aren't lost," and several had closed in early Q3. Source: [earnings call transcript](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-dynatrace-beats-q2-2027-estimates-but-shares-fall-93CH-4995529).
- **Guidance cut.** The cut was in profit and cash flow, not in revenue.

| Item | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| FY27 non-GAAP EPS | $1.97–1.99 | $1.88–1.90 |
| FY27 adjusted FCF | $610–615M | $600–605M |
| FY27 non-GAAP operating income | $682–690M | $653–661M |
| FY27 ARR | $2,359–2,379M | $2,393–2,413M (includes Arize) |

  - Management blamed the FCF cut on the Arize acquisition (AI observability), which closed Oct 1. They say it adds about 200 bps of ARR growth and costs about 175 bps of operating margin.
  - The company still holds its standalone constant-currency ARR growth guide of 15.5–16.5%.
  - Q3 guide: revenue $591–596M, EPS $0.44–0.45, which is below what analysts expected.
- **Second-half setup.** About 70% of full-year renewals are still ahead. Net new ARR is expected to skew more to Q4 than usual. Management says it does not need every slipped deal to close to hit guidance. Analysts asked why the second-half ARR target wasn't raised. The CFO said the company wanted a "balanced" guide.
- **Positives.**
  - Log management grew well over 100% year over year.
  - Infrastructure monitoring is above $500M annualized, growing about 30%.
  - Platform consumption is up over 20%.
  - 14 deals topped $1M ACV (annual contract value), including a nine-figure bank deal.
  - Agent monetization began Oct 1.
  - A CrowdStrike log-routing tie-up is in place.
  - Management is considering a premium on usage overages.
- **Buyback.** The company bought $246M (5.2M shares, average $47.38) in Q2. The board added $1B, leaving about $1.3B of capacity, or roughly 10% of the roughly $12.5B market cap. All buyback purchases so far were above today's price. Sources: [8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001773383/000177338326000069/dt-20261103.htm), [MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/buyback-stock-buyback-program-initiated-by-dynatrace-nyse-dt-2026-11-03/).
- **Price path.** The stock fell 9 straight sessions to $43.44 on Nov 6, a 32.3% loss that erased about $6B of value. It is roughly flat since (43.19 today), so the low has held for about 8 sessions. It trades at about 77x trailing P/E. [Trefis](https://www.trefis.com/stock/dt/articles/623565/a-9-day-losing-streak-has-dynatrace-stock-down-32/2026-11-07) calls the slide "mostly Dynatrace's own story."

**Analysts.** Targets were cut but ratings mostly held. The consensus is Moderate Buy with an average target around $62–64, about 45% above the price. Wedbush is the outlier at Neutral with a $50 target, though one source suggests that move came earlier. Sources: [Investing.com on DA Davidson](https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/da-davidson-cuts-dynatrace-stock-price-target-on-expansion-deal-delays-93CH-5000042), [MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-dynatrace-nyse-dt-price-target-cut-to-6300-by-analysts-at-btig-research-2026-11-03/).

| Firm | Old target | New target | Rating |
|---|---|---|---|
| BTIG | $73 | $63 | Buy |
| Barclays | $71 | $61 | Overweight |
| Rosenblatt | $70 | $65 | Buy |
| Wells Fargo | $75 | $65 | not stated |
| DA Davidson | $65 | $60 | Buy |
| Needham | $68 | $65 | Buy |
| Wedbush | $54 | $50 | Neutral |
| RBC | not stated | $68 | Outperform |

**Backdrop today**
- **Software and AI fears.** The software selloff continued on Nov 17. IGV (software ETF) fell about 3.2%, Salesforce fell 9.4% and Intuit 7.2%. Reports cite fear of AI agents eroding subscription pricing, new OpenAI models, and funds selling ahead of the Anthropic IPO. The S&P 500 closed at a five-month low and the Dow fell about 850 points. DT's -1.2% on 0.9x volume was mild by comparison. Sources: [Gurufocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9205947/salesforce-crm-shares-fall-94-amid-tech-sector-selloff-ahead-of-anthropic-ipo), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/17/wall-streets-fear-gauge-is-surging-again-and-this-time-its-not-just-about-ai-jitters.html).
- **Nvidia.** It reports tonight and was reported up about 4% after hours, which may explain DT's +0.4% after hours.
- **Peer Datadog.** It beat strongly on Nov 4 (revenue +35%, $1.20B) but fell on a soft Q4 guide that assumes only the minimum from its largest customer. That is another observability read-through that was not clean.
- **Today's news.** Dynatrace spoke at the RBC conference today and repeated the AI-demand and slipped-deals story. It also announced that Bindplane was named a Leader in Gartner's observability pipelines Magic Quadrant. Neither is a catalyst. Sources: [RBC write-up](https://za.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/dynatrace-at-rbc-conference-ai-tailwinds-and-growth-levers-93CH-4581754), [Gartner release](https://financialcontent.com/article/bizwire-2026-11-17-dynatrace-bindplane-named-a-leader-in-the-2026-gartner-magic-quadrant-for-observability-pipelines).

**Upcoming dates**

|---|---|

| Dec 9 | Barclays conference (4:25 PM ET) |
| Feb 8, 2027 | Q3 earnings |

**Risks and gaps**
- **Source quality.**
  - Several articles give conflicting prices and day-moves (the Nov 3 drop is reported as 10.6%, 13% and 15%).
  - The Q1 net new ARR growth of 41% in the RBC write-up could not be checked against a second source.
  - One Investing.com note calls the quarter a "miss" while the same page says a beat, so check it before relying on it.
  - I discarded a Globe and Mail piece because it dated to May.
